content.content:
# Compilation Prompt — Consolidated Transcripts → One Chronological Teaching Document

This is the prompt that produced a genuinely excellent result the first time (a 5-part
"Faith" sermon series compiled into one polished, chronologically-correct, voice-preserving
markdown document). Use it verbatim with placeholders filled in, against an LLM chat that
takes file attachments — or hand this whole file plus the transcripts to an agent with
Write access and ask it to follow §"Structural Rulebook" directly.

## What to attach

1. All N consolidated part-transcripts from `consolidate-transcripts.sh`
   (e.g. `Faith 1.txt` … `Faith 5.txt`).
2. Any broader-context recordings that cover the same material inside a wider session —
   e.g. full meeting/Google-Meet transcripts, if you have them. These aren't required, but
   they're what let the compiling model recover the *true* chronological order and connective
   context the numbered parts alone don't carry.

## The prompt (fill in the brackets)

```
Attached are transcripts of a series on [TOPIC] done by [TEACHER/SPEAKER NAME]
([N range, e.g. 1-5]).

After that, the attached are actual transcripts ([SOURCE, e.g. Google Meet]) from
which the [TOPIC] series was taught (broader in context as they cover entire
sessions as compared to the [N] parts that only cover the teaching).

From the above, generate (compile them into) one teaching on [TOPIC] by [TEACHER
NAME]. .md format. In the file, there should be a chronological flow of the
[TOPIC] series ([N range] doesn't really reflect the manner in which they were
taught — you might find that part 1 was taught after part 4). I think the [N
range] parts nail the teaching well, whereas the other transcripts sort of give
some context. If [TEACHER NAME] made any prayers/declarations/punchlines/
statements be sure to include them in the file, still in a chronological manner.
Also all scripture [or: quotes/citations from your authoritative source] to be
referenced in [NKJV, or your default translation/edition] unless of course
otherwise stated. Verify every citation against a real source rather than
relying on memory — including the chapter/verse number itself, not just the
wording. If [TEACHER NAME]'s spoken reference doesn't match what they're
quoting, don't just silently fix it: keep what they actually said as their own
words, and give the correct citation right alongside it. Format well —
headings, titles, bold, italic, etc.

This is a professional [TOPIC] document. Do not leave out a thing — that
includes not leaving out what was actually said, even a wrong reference number,
in favor of a silently "corrected" version. Let it be such that it is as if
[TEACHER NAME] is speaking directly to whoever reads it.
```

The load-bearing phrases, and why each one matters (don't drop these when adapting):
- **"doesn't really reflect the manner in which they were taught"** — this is the single
  instruction that forces real chronological reasoning from internal evidence, instead of
  the model lazily trusting the file numbering. Without it, you get parts 1-5 in that literal
  order, which is very likely *wrong*.
- **"the other transcripts sort of give some context"** — explicitly ranks the two source
  types (numbered teaching parts = primary structure/weight; broader recordings = context
  filler), so the model doesn't over-weight the noisier, less-curated source.
- **"be sure to include them ... still in a chronological manner"** — prayers/declarations/
  punchlines are exactly what a lazy summarizer drops first. Naming the category explicitly
  is what keeps them in.
- **"unless of course otherwise stated"** — the one correctly-scoped escape hatch: don't
  force the standard translation over a quote the speaker explicitly attributed elsewhere.
- **"Verify every citation against a real source rather than relying on memory"** — added
  after a real failure: a compiling model recalled "Romans 12:4" confidently and was wrong
  (the content quoted was Romans 2:4). Fluent, confident recall of a Bible reference is not
  verification. See "The Scripture Citation Rule" below for the exact pattern once you've
  verified — this phrase only covers *checking*, not *rendering*.
- **"don't just silently fix it ... keep what they actually said ... give the correct citation
  right alongside it"** — completeness applies to the speaker's own words too, including their
  mistakes. A silently "corrected" citation deletes real information: what the speaker
  actually said, uncertainty and all. See the worked example below.
- **"Do not leave out a thing"** — sets completeness, not summarization, as the goal. This is
  a compile, not a digest. This now explicitly includes wrong-but-spoken citations, not just
  prayers/declarations/punchlines.
- **"as if [name] is speaking directly to whoever reads it"** — the instruction that produces
  first/second-person voice preservation instead of third-person academic paraphrase.

---

## Structural Rulebook (reverse-engineered from the reference output)

If you're generating this directly (an agent with Write access, not a separate chat), follow
this structure — it's what the prompt above reliably produces, made explicit:

1. **Title block**: H1 title that names the *theme*, not "Compiled Transcript" (e.g. "The
   Life of Faith"). H2 "A Teaching Series by [Name]". H3 venue/series line. Bold date range.
   Horizontal rule.
2. **Epigraph**: the 1-2 scripture/quotes most central to the whole series, blockquoted,
   italic verse text, em-dash citation, translation noted — set before any narrative content.
3. **"A Note Before We Begin"**: an introductory framing section in the speaker's own first-
   person voice, drawn from their *actual opening remarks in the chronologically-earliest
   session* — not a generic AI-written preamble. If the earliest session has no natural cold
   open, use its first substantive paragraph.
4. **One "# PART [ordinal]: [session's own descriptive title]" section per distinct session**,
   in true chronological order, each carrying:
   - H3 date of that session (only if the source states or clearly implies one — don't invent
     dates)
   - H2 thematic subheadings for each major movement of thought
   - H3 subheadings tied to specific source-passages taught, each immediately followed by
     the passage **quoted from the real, verified reference text** (not the speaker's
     paraphrase, and not an unverified citation number — see "The Scripture Citation Rule"
     below) in a blockquote with citation
   - Body prose that preserves the speaker's actual phrasing, rhetorical repetition, and
     idiom — paraphrase as little as humanly possible; this is a transcript compile, not a
     summary
   - **Bold** for the speaker's key doctrinal/declarative one-liners
   - Blockquotes (same `>` syntax as scripture) for standout verbatim quotes, illustrative
     asides, and personal anecdotes — visually distinct from body prose
   - A dedicated callout subsection for any ritual/ceremonial moment (e.g. "## Communion
     Declaration — [date]"), with the prayer/declaration text preserved close to verbatim
5. **Closing section**: the final prayer/declaration from the chronologically-last session,
   verbatim, blockquoted.
6. **Summary table**: `| Session/Date | Theme | Key Scripture |`, one row per PART, in
   chronological order.
7. **"Core Declarations" list**: 8-10 numbered, pithy one-line doctrinal takeaways distilled
   from across the whole series — these are for skimming/reference, not new content.
8. **Closing pull-quote**: the single most memorable line from the whole series, blockquoted
   with attribution.
9. **Footer**: italic attribution block — compiled-from note, organization, date range,
   speaker name.

### Voice rules
- First person ("I") when the speaker refers to themself; second person ("you") when they
  address the audience directly. The reader should feel spoken to, not informed about.
- Keep the speaker's own structuring language ("Now let me ask you something," "I want you
  to see something here") — it's part of what makes the compile feel authentic rather than
  ghostwritten.

---

## The Scripture Citation Rule

Two failure modes, both wrong in opposite directions:

1. **Transcribing the speaker's spoken paraphrase as if it were the literal verse text.**
   (The original problem this rulebook already covered.)
2. **Silently "correcting" a misspoken chapter/verse number** — swapping in the right
   reference without showing that the speaker said something different. This looks tidier,
   but it deletes real information: what the speaker actually said, mistake and all. A
   reader (or the speaker themself, checking the document later) has no way to tell a
   verified correction from an invented one if corrections are invisible.

The fix for both is the same three-part pattern, and it requires the citation to have
actually been checked against a real source first (Method §5 in `skill.md` — not memory,
however confident):

1. Keep the speaker's own words — their paraphrase, and their spoken reference if they gave
   one, right or wrong — in the prose, attributed as what they said.
2. Immediately follow with the verified citation, in a normal scripture blockquote, supplying
   the real verse text.
3. Never present step 2 as if it were part of what the speaker said. It's the compiler
   supplying the real text, and the phrasing should make that clear (see example).

**Worked example** (a real case, from the "Emotional Intelligence" series, verified against
biblegateway.com/NKJV after the compiling model's first pass got the reference wrong from
memory):

> Pastor Charles introduced this as "the book of Romans, chapter 12 and verse 4" — the verse
> whose content he's actually quoting is Romans 2:4:
>
> > *"Or do you despise the riches of His goodness, forbearance, and longsuffering, not
> > knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance?"*
> > — Romans 2:4 (NKJV)

Notice what this does *not* do: it doesn't pretend he said "2:4," and it doesn't present the
verified text as something he recited verbatim. It shows both — what was actually said, and
what's actually true — without erasing either one.

# Life Is Happening For You

## A Teaching by Ken Muritu

### ByPass Cell Church — a breakout session of Royal Priesthood (RP)

---

> *"Sow for yourselves righteousness; Reap in mercy; Break up your fallow ground, For it is time to seek the Lord, Till He comes and rains righteousness on you."*
> — Hosea 10:12 (NKJV)

> *"For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities nor powers, nor things present nor things to come, nor height nor depth, nor any other created thing, shall be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord."*
> — Romans 8:38-39 (NKJV)

---

## A Note Before We Begin

I want to be honest with you about where this teaching starts, because it's been a minute since I've shared the word in a setup like this — a cell, not a platform.

It's been a minute, like it's been long, before I share the word with such a setup. I normally speak, and in the speaking maybe I might throw some verses, and you get to the effect of the verses. But really, to stand — I remember the last time Benson told me, "Ken, you will be ministering to the cell." I remember when Benson was starting to lead us in prayer, and I saw the way he opened with the verses. He started with Isaiah 45:19 — *"I have not spoken in secret, in a dark place of the earth."* I thought, this is a man of God. And today the Spirit is really ministering to us.

I've been reminded of high school, when I was the follow-up coordinator — the class rep, sort of — for my class. I used to love that space. For some reason I don't know why, it used to grip me — you get to hear the word of God, and you get to see the hearts of the people who are listening to you. They are expectant. They are waiting for that time. Living with them, you know most of them are people of vurugu, people of fighting — you talk to them and to others, but when that time comes, you see a girl sitting there listening, and you can see the word you're sharing is doing something on their hearts.

So I've been reminded of that. And that's the heart I'm bringing into this room tonight.

---

# PART ONE: Life Is Happening For You, Not To You

## The Fallow Ground

Yesterday we were having a session with our father, and he told us to read the book of Romans. I was reading through Romans chapter 8, and I could see the love of God — the intention of God to man, the intention of God to His sons.

There is this thing I'm trying to structure in my thoughts, because so many things are coming to my head. But there comes a time — maybe because of where I've been brought up, maybe because of the systems we've gone through, maybe academics, maybe even the patterns — where we get to a place where we're not doubting the love of God, but at the same time we're not believing it completely.

You have faith, you're a believer, you come to church, you join watches, you join fasting. You give — you give with your time, you even give with money. You're doing the things that, if we're looking at it, you're supposed to be receiving for. But then you wonder why, at certain times, when you really want something to work, it's not working out.

**There comes a time when the systems of the earth, the systems of men, the patterns of our lives, contribute to the way we approach God — the way we believe in Him.** And sometimes you'll even question: "Is God really working? Does God really love me?" You're trying to look at a certain situation, a certain circumstance, and you cannot see God in it. You're trying to piece it together, and it's not making sense at all.

I heard someone say recently — and it is for that reason you hear so many people say they've left church, or no longer believe in God, because it doesn't make sense to believe. Most people — and I'm saying men, because we have friends over a conversation — will really want to show that believing in God is pointless. They question: if God exists, if God is a good God, a loving God, a just God — then why do we have wars? Why do people kill each other? Why do we have divorce? Why do we have the many evils of the earth?

But I have come to realize that the way the systems of the earth work, the way we have been brought up — it was not in God's design. **God designed the earth, but He gave men to dominate it, and the men who are dominating the earth have influenced so many things that are happening in it.** Looking back at how I came to meet RP, and the way I've grown in that space — the man of God, most of the time, if you listen to his heart, he'll show you: yes, the systems of the earth are not working. But that does not mean that is God's design in your life. So He is calling you to a space of understanding — that you cannot blame God for the designs of the systems of the earth.

I love it when Benson began to talk about the Spirit. I want us to read from **Hosea 10:12**:

> *"Sow for yourselves righteousness; Reap in mercy; Break up your fallow ground, For it is time to seek the Lord, Till He comes and rains righteousness on you."*
> — Hosea 10:12 (NKJV)

Many of the things we encounter as men, in our walk with God, we might come to a point where you think God is not with you. Sometimes you can see life as happening *to* you — things are happening to you. You approach situations from a point of them happening to you. **But in the desire of God, things are not happening to you — things are happening for you. God is dealing with you.**

There is a fallow ground. It says, "Break up your fallow ground." There is a fallow ground to be broken, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit is very essential for the breaking of that fallow ground — because it takes a man with the Spirit of God, a man the Spirit works with, to understand: things are not happening to me, they are happening for me.

> When you sit down quietly and look back at the things you thought would kill you — the things you survived, the things that gave you so much pressure you couldn't sleep, the moments where you thought, "It is the end, there is no way" — when you look back, you can actually trace the doings of the Lord in that thing.

The fellowship of the Holy Spirit requires that you are conscious of the Spirit at every time. It requires you to respond to situations in accordance with the Spirit.

## Understanding the Spirit Requires Understanding the Love of God

For the fallow ground to be broken, it requires you to have the Spirit and fellowship with the Spirit. But there is something else. As I was reading Romans — **to actually understand the Spirit of God, you need to understand the love of God.** You need to see God as a Father who is loving, who is interested in your life, who is concerned.

Many times the devil — personally I've been there — even when you know God loves you, you're not conscious of it. You haven't forgotten it, but you're not conscious of it, and you can see it in the way you're thinking, the way you're reacting to things. There comes a time when you just meditate on how God has been loving, on His love.

**And in such situations, when you cannot see how God is loving in your life, you will try to earn that love.** Again, we go back to the way you've been brought up — you think you always have to earn love, always have to earn something. So you try to do certain actions to justify the love of God in your life. Some of us — you're in God, people know you're a believer, but the reason you're serving is because you think by serving, God will reward you, or love you more.

**But before God calls you for people — before He calls you to a place — He first calls you to Himself.** That is God. Again, that place of fellowship. If you look at the sessions we've been having with the man of God — the word, coming here to cell group, Benson encouraging us to read the word of God, to live by that word, to respond to situations with the word, to delight in the word — it is calling you back to a relationship with God, a fellowship with God, a communion with God, before He calls you for a generation, for your business, your family. God has called you to be the Joseph of your household. But He first calls you to Himself, to commune with Him.

No wonder — when you are fighting with that, when you have not understood that, God will walk you through a journey until you reach a place where you say, for yourself, "I need God for myself. I need God for me." God will deal with you well.

## The Blacksmith and the Potter

Benson was reading, in **2 Corinthians 3:18** — you know, when we talk of fire: before the night of pruning, there was a session we had about fire. Fire will squeeze you, but the work of fire is to refine. Think of the people who work gold — blacksmiths. When I place a piece of metal in fire because I want to refine it, **the piece of metal has no say in the process.** It cannot even offer suggestions — "God, I want you to know, I want half of me to stay out of the fire and half to go in." No. It is the work of the one who holds the metal to determine whether that metal is refined or not.

The same for a potter. The clay has no say in what the potter is doing. The potter is the one deciding, "I want this clay to be like this." And **the desire of God is for you to be like Him — to walk like Him.**

> *"But we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, just as by the Spirit of the Lord."*
> — 2 Corinthians 3:18 (NKJV)

That is what our Father has been pointing us to. Sometimes, revelation comes and you look back at the prayers you were making — you realize you were praying for something already within your reach. Something that was already your inheritance. I was reaching for something I called it — "is it Philippians?" — that says, *"You are the portion of my inheritance and my cup..."* Someone in the room caught it faster than I did: **Psalm 16:5.**

> *"O Lord, You are the portion of my inheritance and my cup; You maintain my lot. The lines have fallen to me in pleasant places; Yes, I have a good inheritance."*
> — Psalm 16:5-6 (NKJV)

The way we've been brought up — maybe the way our parents raised us — shapes the way we approach life, even the way we ask God for things. You're asking for something, and God is saying, "Do you know I want you to reign in that thing you're asking for? That thing you're begging for — if only you could behold and see — it is already within your reach." There is a battle in the journey where you haven't fully risen to see yourself at that stage, where you operate from.

## Ambassadors of Christ, Seated in Heavenly Places

I remember a conversation with my father where I asked him — I can't remember exactly what — but he told me, maybe it's obvious, but **why is RP called Priesthood Embassy? Because we are ambassadors of Christ.** Ambassadors are foreigners to the place they live. There's a word that says we are *in* the world, but not *of* it. So there is a place we operate from. No wonder you cannot see life the way people out here see it. No wonder you cannot reason with people who blame the economy, who blame the government — not that it isn't true — but there is a place you operate from, a place you perceive life from, different from the people of this earth.

We are seated in heaven. We are seated high above, princes, powers.

> *"But God, who is rich in mercy, because of His great love with which He loved us, even when we were dead in trespasses, made us alive together with Christ (by grace you have been saved), and raised us up together, and made us sit together in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus."*
> — Ephesians 2:4-6 (NKJV)

There is a place we are seated as sons, and from that place we are supposed to operate, from that place we are supposed to see life. Even in your seeking — you might think seeking is like God is somewhere, you go seek, then you return and leave God back there. But even in your seeking, it shifts your mentality around seeking itself, because **God is within you. He resides in you.** So even in your seeking, you're seeking from a place of fellowship, from a place of communion.

## It Is Not in the Doing — It Is in the Becoming

> *"Praise the Lord! Oh, give thanks to the Lord, for He is good! For His mercy endures forever."*
> — Psalm 106:1 (NKJV)

This debate — "Is God really good? Is God really a just God?" — should not even be a debate, because if we realize how good God is. His mercy — I remember someone teaching once that His mercies are new every morning; they endure forever. In the morning, before you even do anything wrong, before you do the bad things of the day, mercy is already there. And when guilt has taken hold of you, He's looking at you in your guilt saying, "My mercy endures forever."

**There is no single thing you can do — even your service — that earns God's goodness to you.** Your measure of righteousness as a person is not by actions. God is not so interested in you doing things. You might be going through the motions — going to Kisumu, and it's just an activity, or it's a real posture of the heart. It depends on your heart posture.

**It is not the doing. It is not you coming to the cell group session, it is not you attending a prayer watch. It is not in the doing — it is in the becoming.** The person you become.

Pastor Benson was reading from 2 Corinthians. I love the analogy of the blacksmith and the potter, and this scripture: **it is God who decides when you're ready.** You might feel, "I'm ready, You can use me — bring that mountain, bring those people who will speak to it." But then something happens. Times that humble you. You say, "I go back to God in mercy. I thought I was good. God, I need You."

> *"But we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, just as by the Spirit of the Lord."*
> — 2 Corinthians 3:18 (NKJV)

The desire of God is that when He looks at you, He can see Himself — not something casual. When we go into ministry, you can minister, you can worship, you can give the word. When we go into business, can you see God in that thing? The desire of God is across all spheres of your life. If God Himself cannot fail at a thing, you cannot fail in business. **Whatever does not limit God cannot limit you.**

> *"But God's will is great in strength, and I have come that you may have life and have it in abundance."*

That's how I remembered it in the room — the actual text reads:

> *"The thief does not come except to steal, and to kill, and to destroy. I have come that they may have life, and that they may have it more abundantly."*
> — John 10:10 (NKJV)

There is an expression of the life of God He wants you to have — not just life, but life in abundance, the fullness of His life. In whatever space you're in — your company, your business — can you see the fullness of God in that thing? There is an expression of life that God is after, and that is the expression of His glory in that thing you're doing.

## The Word Is Alive and Must Grow

From all of that, the desire of God is for your eyes to be opened, that you may see His love in all things. When you're reading the word of God — I love the Faith series we've had with our Father — I've felt it, the word is a sword, slashing me left, right, center. Because there is a reality you're being invited to walk into — a reality of transformation.

Once we had these goals — crazy goals — "I'm going to read the whole chapter today." Ask me about Ezekiel, I can tell you what it says. Ask me where Elijah climbed, what Elisha did — every account, "It is very good." But beyond you knowing that information, beyond having that knowledge base — **is there a transformation? Is there something that word has done in your life?**

Because scripture says:

> *"I have been crucified with Christ; it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me; and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself for me."*
> — Galatians 2:20 (NKJV)

Breaking the fallow ground requires this realization: it is no longer you who is living. I had this thinking growing up that I always had to be in control of things, that I needed to know what is happening, what is happening next. And I had a problem, and that problem toppled down to my faith — because faith is the evidence of things. When I cannot see a thing, I have an issue, because I want to know.

**The breaking of the fallow ground requires an understanding that we have been crucified with Christ — that life is not happening to you, it is happening for you.**

For you to be crucified with Christ, to die to yourself, to come to a point of understanding — Benson used to say, "this life is not my own." And I'm inviting each of you to that understanding. This life is not your own. The man of God — a very interesting man of God — at times he comes to us very tired, and he tells us. If it were up to how he felt, he'd rather receive than come and teach. But this man has come to an understanding: it is not in him to decide. **If the Spirit broods, if the Spirit speaks, you have no will but to obey.**

The word of God is alive, and it must grow.

> *"And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld His glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth."*
> — John 1:14 (NKJV)

Now the Word is flesh. Now we behold His glory, because it has become flesh. We mentioned it is not in the doing, it is in the becoming. When you're being invited into a space of the word, it is not for you to know, not for you to be informed — it is for you to be called into a person. It is for you to become the person of God, the very image of God.

Sometimes in life, the word does not make sense at all. I have a friend — most of my friends are not very spiritual — but I love them anyway. There's one who questions everything, very learned, very smart, very brilliant. He'll tell me, "Ken, let's think logically. Doesn't the Bible say this and this and this?" I don't disagree with him — but I say, put ourselves in this actual situation, in context, and this doesn't apply. There are situations in life where I think it's because God is not responsible for the systems of the earth. There's a systems theory — if you're an engineer, you know: if you design a system to work a certain way, or a code, and you set that program to run a certain way, the moment you input something and it outputs something, you can't argue with it, because that is exactly how it's set up to work. And times will come when you're trying to speak the word into something, and you cannot see it manifest according to the word — the word doesn't fit and doesn't come.

But the good thing is: **because the word is alive, every situation you introduce it to — it doesn't matter if that situation is dead, doesn't matter if it doesn't respond to the word — by default, it grows.** When you introduce a seed to all the conditions necessary for germination, it has no choice — it has no option — it must germinate, it must grow. **Therefore, every situation that receives the word of God comes alive, because the word is unchangeable.**

## Nothing Can Separate You From His Love

Maybe to read Romans chapter 8 again — an emphasis on the love of God, and how important that is. It says — where did I start — let me find it:

> *"For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities nor powers, nor things present nor things to come, nor any other created thing, shall be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord."*

I said "Romans 38:38 to 39" while I was searching for the page, and then "4:38" trying to find my place — what I was actually reading, once I found it, was:

> *"For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities nor powers, nor things present nor things to come, nor height nor depth, nor any other created thing, shall be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord."*
> — Romans 8:38-39 (NKJV)

Whoever was writing this was trying to look at things — trying to name everything he could think of — and then just said, "nor any other created thing," to cover the rest. **When you are born again, you are in Christ. And the love of God resides in Christ.** So by the fact that you are in Christ, by the fact that you are a believer, born again — you cannot be separated from the love of God. Because God's love is amazing. He is a good God. This whole conversation stems from the love of God — it requires you to see His love, to understand that you can speak to things, that you can walk in the word, that you can actually do it.

So, behold His love.

## Walking By Faith, Not By Sight

I know the word of God is a seed. The moment you plant a seed, it must grow. So you must talk by faith. Now that you understand nothing can separate you from the love of God — sometimes you ask, "Am I really with God? Can I really be used as an instrument, as a vessel?" I think this is the battle so many young Christians face. We can all attest to that. You feel like there's a place you need to reach before you're ready to be used.

And it is all, maybe, because of condemnation. You can be condemned because of things you've done, because you're looking at yourself. I, by the way — across most of my time in RP, I was a joker. A serious joker. There was a time a sister was choosing an intercessor and I told her, "You want to speak something to my life before you call me?" — I wasn't serious. I was looking at myself, and I couldn't see the ability God was seeing in me, but it was in me. Same as when we tell someone, "Emmy, you lead us in the presence of the Lord with your voice," and you say, "With my voice?" — you can't see what God sees in you.

**When you cannot see that thing God is seeing in you, you're reminded you ought to walk by faith and not by sight.** The things you're seeing are things perceived in the flesh. But when you live a life of faith, walking will push you beyond your comfort zone. No wonder there's that battle with God — because it's comfortable to live in the flesh, and it's very challenging to live in the Spirit. It takes real walking in the Spirit to look at someone failing, at a house about to be foreclosed on, and speak life into it without being shaken.

**So you must walk in faith.** When you come to cell church, we will pray for you, we will celebrate you, we will give you a chance to minister. But even as you do those things — it is your responsibility, as Emmy, as me, Ken — even though I'm doing that thing, how have I aligned my mind to become that thing? Has it become substance in my life? Have I become that thing God desires me to be?

**Because there will come a time when a demand will be placed on you.** Not just by us — by your family, in your company. There will come a time you won't be able to text Benson, and maybe he won't pick up, and you'll have to stand in that moment on your own. And that is why God does not want to be praying for you every time you text Him — He has set structures. You should be praying. We can get lost in the *action* of prayer — the sacrifice of nine to ten, five to six — and forget that the reason you've been placed in that space is for you to become that thing, to tap into that reality.

A demand will be placed on you in your family. You will have children. For men, you are the priest of your house. For the ladies — you are royal priest too, the wife of a priest. **So there will come a time. Are you prepared for it?**

We will pray for you. The man of God will place you in a department and tell you to serve. But in your serving, will you take time to become that thing? This goes beyond church — it even goes to the opportunity you've been given in the company you work in. It's your responsibility to use that opportunity to become. Some of us will say, "It was a miracle, I wasn't qualified, but I got the role." Don't forget — you've been placed. The fact that it's a miracle means it's an opportunity for you to become that thing. RP is one of the spaces I've seen young people do things that leave me shocked — both in service and in the world. It's the same everywhere: you were born in a poor background, but there will come a time you *are* the background you overcome. **It is your responsibility, beyond the actions, to become that thing. Beyond just doing stuff — take your time, invest in the word of God, become that thing.**

---

I don't want to go too far tonight. There's another part I'll record as audio, just to set your expectations — we'll walk down through the character of God. Because it's also important to understand His character. Society has shaped God in a very different way from who He actually is. Our upbringing, our trauma, our pain, our guilt, our condemnation — the systems of the earth portray God in a manner that isn't really Him. **Because God is a Father. He is a good Father.**

It is my desire, and I believe it is the desire of God, that all of us — me, you — understand that God is good, that life is not happening to us, it is happening for us, and that we tap into that reality and operate from that place.

## Closing Prayer

*Ken led the room into prayer — the declarative portions in English are preserved here verbatim; the passages between them were spoken in tongues.*

> Thank You, Lord, because You are loving. It is Your desire and it is Your will to see us prosper. It is Your desire and it is Your will for us to manifest the power that is within us.
>
> There are times, Lord, we have doubted Your love. There are times we have doubted that this journey — are we really walking with You? But flood our eyes with light, that we may behold Your love. That we may behold Your love.
>
> That we will not beg for what is rightfully ours. We will not pray and ask for things that are within our reach.
>
> Even as we interact with Your word, we are interacting with Your word to become that word. We declare that Your word is being made flesh in our lives. It is being made flesh in our situations, in our families, Lord.
>
> Because You say in Your word that You are the portion, Lord — You are the portion of our inheritance. We have a good inheritance. Our lines have fallen to pleasant places.
>
> Father, thank You because You will cause us to see. You will cause us to see Your goodness in our lives. You will cause us to see that life is not happening to us, it is happening for us.
>
> You are good. You are kind. You are faithful. We praise Your name.
>
> Heavenly Father, we thank You because of Your love. Thank You because You are a good God. Thank You because You are a kind God. Thank You because You are a good Father. Thank You because You are the Shepherd of Your pasture. Thank You because You are loving, Lord. Thank You because there is an agenda You have for us, Lord — beyond the things we are doing, beyond our service, beyond our actions, beyond our lives. There is an agenda, and Your agenda is great. Your agenda is big.
>
> Father, flood our eyes with light, that we may see, and that we may operate from where You have called us, Lord. You've called us to be ambassadors with Christ. We operate from that place, oh God. We choose to perceive life differently, in accordance with Your word. We choose to walk in accordance with that word, Lord. We choose to respond to situations with Your word.
>
> Father, we declare that Your word is being made flesh in our lives, Lord — in the areas of our workplaces, oh God, in our belief, in our mentality, in our mind. Every stronghold, Lord, that has kept us in the same place, that has kept us in circles — every stronghold is being brought to the authority of Your word, to the authority of You, oh God. Every stronghold is being broken in the name of Jesus, Lord.
>
> We behold Your love. We behold Your goodness. We behold Your faithfulness, Lord. In Jesus' mighty name. Amen. We pray and we believe. Amen.

---

## Summary

| Session | Theme | Key Scripture |
|---|---|---|
| ByPass Cell Church (Royal Priesthood breakout) | Life is happening *for* you, not *to* you — moving from doing to becoming | Romans 8:38-39 |

## Core Declarations

1. Life is not happening to you — it is happening for you.
2. God calls you to Himself before He calls you to a people.
3. Your measure of righteousness is not by actions — it is not in the doing, it is in the becoming.
4. Nothing — no power, nothing present or to come — can separate you from the love of God.
5. The word of God is alive; wherever it is introduced, it grows, whether or not the situation responds to it.
6. You are seated in heavenly places in Christ — an ambassador operating from a different place than the systems of the earth.
7. God's mercy is new every morning and endures forever; He is not waiting for you to earn it.
8. Walking in the Spirit will always feel more costly than walking in the flesh, but it is the only place you cannot be shaken.
9. You will not beg for what is already your inheritance — see it, and rise to reign in it.
10. Beyond the doing — the serving, the ministry, the position — is the question: have you become the thing God has called you to be?

---

> *"It is not in the doing. It is in the becoming."*
> — Ken Muritu

> *"Sow for yourselves righteousness; Reap in mercy; Break up your fallow ground, For it is time to seek the Lord, Till He comes and rains righteousness on you."*
> — Hosea 10:12 (NKJV)

> *"For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities nor powers, nor things present nor things to come, nor height nor depth, nor any other created thing, shall be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord."*
> — Romans 8:38-39 (NKJV)

---

## A Note Before We Begin

I want to be honest with you about where this teaching starts, because it's been a minute since I've shared the word in a setup like this — a cell, not a platform.

It's been a minute, like it's been long, before I share the word with such a setup. I normally speak, and in the speaking maybe I might throw some verses, and you get to the effect of the verses. But really, to stand — I remember the last time Benson told me, "Ken, you will be ministering to the cell." I remember when Benson was starting to lead us in prayer, and I saw the way he opened with the verses. He started with Isaiah 45:19 — *"I have not spoken in secret, in a dark place of the earth."* I thought, this is a man of God. And today the Spirit is really ministering to us.

I've been reminded of high school, when I was the follow-up coordinator — the class rep, sort of — for my class. I used to love that space. For some reason I don't know why, it used to grip me — you get to hear the word of God, and you get to see the hearts of the people who are listening to you. They are expectant. They are waiting for that time. Living with them, you know most of them are people of vurugu, people of fighting — you talk to them and to others, but when that time comes, you see a girl sitting there listening, and you can see the word you're sharing is doing something on their hearts.

So I've been reminded of that. And that's the heart I'm bringing into this room tonight.

---

# PART ONE: Life Is Happening For You, Not To You

## The Fallow Ground

Yesterday we were having a session with our father, and he told us to read the book of Romans. I was reading through Romans chapter 8, and I could see the love of God — the intention of God to man, the intention of God to His sons.

There is this thing I'm trying to structure in my thoughts, because so many things are coming to my head. But there comes a time — maybe because of where I've been brought up, maybe because of the systems we've gone through, maybe academics, maybe even the patterns — where we get to a place where we're not doubting the love of God, but at the same time we're not believing it completely.

You have faith, you're a believer, you come to church, you join watches, you join fasting. You give — you give with your time, you even give with money. You're doing the things that, if we're looking at it, you're supposed to be receiving for. But then you wonder why, at certain times, when you really want something to work, it's not working out.

**There comes a time when the systems of the earth, the systems of men, the patterns of our lives, contribute to the way we approach God — the way we believe in Him.** And sometimes you'll even question: "Is God really working? Does God really love me?" You're trying to look at a certain situation, a certain circumstance, and you cannot see God in it. You're trying to piece it together, and it's not making sense at all.

I heard someone say recently — and it is for that reason you hear so many people say they've left church, or no longer believe in God, because it doesn't make sense to believe. Most people — and I'm saying men, because we have friends over a conversation — will really want to show that believing in God is pointless. They question: if God exists, if God is a good God, a loving God, a just God — then why do we have wars? Why do people kill each other? Why do we have divorce? Why do we have the many evils of the earth?

But I have come to realize that the way the systems of the earth work, the way we have been brought up — it was not in God's design. **God designed the earth, but He gave men to dominate it, and the men who are dominating the earth have influenced so many things that are happening in it.** Looking back at how I came to meet RP, and the way I've grown in that space — the man of God, most of the time, if you listen to his heart, he'll show you: yes, the systems of the earth are not working. But that does not mean that is God's design in your life. So He is calling you to a space of understanding — that you cannot blame God for the designs of the systems of the earth.

I love it when Benson began to talk about the Spirit. I want us to read from **Hosea 10:12**:

> *"Sow for yourselves righteousness; Reap in mercy; Break up your fallow ground, For it is time to seek the Lord, Till He comes and rains righteousness on you."*
> — Hosea 10:12 (NKJV)

Many of the things we encounter as men, in our walk with God, we might come to a point where you think God is not with you. Sometimes you can see life as happening *to* you — things are happening to you. You approach situations from a point of them happening to you. **But in the desire of God, things are not happening to you — things are happening for you. God is dealing with you.**

There is a fallow ground. It says, "Break up your fallow ground." There is a fallow ground to be broken, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit is very essential for the breaking of that fallow ground — because it takes a man with the Spirit of God, a man the Spirit works with, to understand: things are not happening to me, they are happening for me.

> When you sit down quietly and look back at the things you thought would kill you — the things you survived, the things that gave you so much pressure you couldn't sleep, the moments where you thought, "It is the end, there is no way" — when you look back, you can actually trace the doings of the Lord in that thing.

The fellowship of the Holy Spirit requires that you are conscious of the Spirit at every time. It requires you to respond to situations in accordance with the Spirit.

## Understanding the Spirit Requires Understanding the Love of God

For the fallow ground to be broken, it requires you to have the Spirit and fellowship with the Spirit. But there is something else. As I was reading Romans — **to actually understand the Spirit of God, you need to understand the love of God.** You need to see God as a Father who is loving, who is interested in your life, who is concerned.

Many times the devil — personally I've been there — even when you know God loves you, you're not conscious of it. You haven't forgotten it, but you're not conscious of it, and you can see it in the way you're thinking, the way you're reacting to things. There comes a time when you just meditate on how God has been loving, on His love.

**And in such situations, when you cannot see how God is loving in your life, you will try to earn that love.** Again, we go back to the way you've been brought up — you think you always have to earn love, always have to earn something. So you try to do certain actions to justify the love of God in your life. Some of us — you're in God, people know you're a believer, but the reason you're serving is because you think by serving, God will reward you, or love you more.

**But before God calls you for people — before He calls you to a place — He first calls you to Himself.** That is God. Again, that place of fellowship. If you look at the sessions we've been having with the man of God — the word, coming here to cell group, Benson encouraging us to read the word of God, to live by that word, to respond to situations with the word, to delight in the word — it is calling you back to a relationship with God, a fellowship with God, a communion with God, before He calls you for a generation, for your business, your family. God has called you to be the Joseph of your household. But He first calls you to Himself, to commune with Him.

No wonder — when you are fighting with that, when you have not understood that, God will walk you through a journey until you reach a place where you say, for yourself, "I need God for myself. I need God for me." God will deal with you well.

## The Blacksmith and the Potter

Benson was reading, in **2 Corinthians 3:18** — you know, when we talk of fire: before the night of pruning, there was a session we had about fire. Fire will squeeze you, but the work of fire is to refine. Think of the people who work gold — blacksmiths. When I place a piece of metal in fire because I want to refine it, **the piece of metal has no say in the process.** It cannot even offer suggestions — "God, I want you to know, I want half of me to stay out of the fire and half to go in." No. It is the work of the one who holds the metal to determine whether that metal is refined or not.

The same for a potter. The clay has no say in what the potter is doing. The potter is the one deciding, "I want this clay to be like this." And **the desire of God is for you to be like Him — to walk like Him.**

> *"But we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, just as by the Spirit of the Lord."*
> — 2 Corinthians 3:18 (NKJV)

That is what our Father has been pointing us to. Sometimes, revelation comes and you look back at the prayers you were making — you realize you were praying for something already within your reach. Something that was already your inheritance. I was reaching for something I called it — "is it Philippians?" — that says, *"You are the portion of my inheritance and my cup..."* Someone in the room caught it faster than I did: **Psalm 16:5.**

> *"O Lord, You are the portion of my inheritance and my cup; You maintain my lot. The lines have fallen to me in pleasant places; Yes, I have a good inheritance."*
> — Psalm 16:5-6 (NKJV)

The way we've been brought up — maybe the way our parents raised us — shapes the way we approach life, even the way we ask God for things. You're asking for something, and God is saying, "Do you know I want you to reign in that thing you're asking for? That thing you're begging for — if only you could behold and see — it is already within your reach." There is a battle in the journey where you haven't fully risen to see yourself at that stage, where you operate from.

## Ambassadors of Christ, Seated in Heavenly Places

I remember a conversation with my father where I asked him — I can't remember exactly what — but he told me, maybe it's obvious, but **why is RP called Priesthood Embassy? Because we are ambassadors of Christ.** Ambassadors are foreigners to the place they live. There's a word that says we are *in* the world, but not *of* it. So there is a place we operate from. No wonder you cannot see life the way people out here see it. No wonder you cannot reason with people who blame the economy, who blame the government — not that it isn't true — but there is a place you operate from, a place you perceive life from, different from the people of this earth.

We are seated in heaven. We are seated high above, princes, powers.

> *"But God, who is rich in mercy, because of His great love with which He loved us, even when we were dead in trespasses, made us alive together with Christ (by grace you have been saved), and raised us up together, and made us sit together in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus."*
> — Ephesians 2:4-6 (NKJV)

There is a place we are seated as sons, and from that place we are supposed to operate, from that place we are supposed to see life. Even in your seeking — you might think seeking is like God is somewhere, you go seek, then you return and leave God back there. But even in your seeking, it shifts your mentality around seeking itself, because **God is within you. He resides in you.** So even in your seeking, you're seeking from a place of fellowship, from a place of communion.

## It Is Not in the Doing — It Is in the Becoming

> *"Praise the Lord! Oh, give thanks to the Lord, for He is good! For His mercy endures forever."*
> — Psalm 106:1 (NKJV)

This debate — "Is God really good? Is God really a just God?" — should not even be a debate, because if we realize how good God is. His mercy — I remember someone teaching once that His mercies are new every morning; they endure forever. In the morning, before you even do anything wrong, before you do the bad things of the day, mercy is already there. And when guilt has taken hold of you, He's looking at you in your guilt saying, "My mercy endures forever."

**There is no single thing you can do — even your service — that earns God's goodness to you.** Your measure of righteousness as a person is not by actions. God is not so interested in you doing things. You might be going through the motions — going to Kisumu, and it's just an activity, or it's a real posture of the heart. It depends on your heart posture.

**It is not the doing. It is not you coming to the cell group session, it is not you attending a prayer watch. It is not in the doing — it is in the becoming.** The person you become.

Pastor Benson was reading from 2 Corinthians. I love the analogy of the blacksmith and the potter, and this scripture: **it is God who decides when you're ready.** You might feel, "I'm ready, You can use me — bring that mountain, bring those people who will speak to it." But then something happens. Times that humble you. You say, "I go back to God in mercy. I thought I was good. God, I need You."

> *"But we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, just as by the Spirit of the Lord."*
> — 2 Corinthians 3:18 (NKJV)

The desire of God is that when He looks at you, He can see Himself — not something casual. When we go into ministry, you can minister, you can worship, you can give the word. When we go into business, can you see God in that thing? The desire of God is across all spheres of your life. If God Himself cannot fail at a thing, you cannot fail in business. **Whatever does not limit God cannot limit you.**

> *"But God's will is great in strength, and I have come that you may have life and have it in abundance."*

That's how I remembered it in the room — the actual text reads:

> *"The thief does not come except to steal, and to kill, and to destroy. I have come that they may have life, and that they may have it more abundantly."*
> — John 10:10 (NKJV)

There is an expression of the life of God He wants you to have — not just life, but life in abundance, the fullness of His life. In whatever space you're in — your company, your business — can you see the fullness of God in that thing? There is an expression of life that God is after, and that is the expression of His glory in that thing you're doing.

## The Word Is Alive and Must Grow

From all of that, the desire of God is for your eyes to be opened, that you may see His love in all things. When you're reading the word of God — I love the Faith series we've had with our Father — I've felt it, the word is a sword, slashing me left, right, center. Because there is a reality you're being invited to walk into — a reality of transformation.

Once we had these goals — crazy goals — "I'm going to read the whole chapter today." Ask me about Ezekiel, I can tell you what it says. Ask me where Elijah climbed, what Elisha did — every account, "It is very good." But beyond you knowing that information, beyond having that knowledge base — **is there a transformation? Is there something that word has done in your life?**

Because scripture says:

> *"I have been crucified with Christ; it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me; and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself for me."*
> — Galatians 2:20 (NKJV)

Breaking the fallow ground requires this realization: it is no longer you who is living. I had this thinking growing up that I always had to be in control of things, that I needed to know what is happening, what is happening next. And I had a problem, and that problem toppled down to my faith — because faith is the evidence of things. When I cannot see a thing, I have an issue, because I want to know.

**The breaking of the fallow ground requires an understanding that we have been crucified with Christ — that life is not happening to you, it is happening for you.**

For you to be crucified with Christ, to die to yourself, to come to a point of understanding — Benson used to say, "this life is not my own." And I'm inviting each of you to that understanding. This life is not your own. The man of God — a very interesting man of God — at times he comes to us very tired, and he tells us. If it were up to how he felt, he'd rather receive than come and teach. But this man has come to an understanding: it is not in him to decide. **If the Spirit broods, if the Spirit speaks, you have no will but to obey.**

The word of God is alive, and it must grow.

> *"And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld His glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth."*
> — John 1:14 (NKJV)

Now the Word is flesh. Now we behold His glory, because it has become flesh. We mentioned it is not in the doing, it is in the becoming. When you're being invited into a space of the word, it is not for you to know, not for you to be informed — it is for you to be called into a person. It is for you to become the person of God, the very image of God.

Sometimes in life, the word does not make sense at all. I have a friend — most of my friends are not very spiritual — but I love them anyway. There's one who questions everything, very learned, very smart, very brilliant. He'll tell me, "Ken, let's think logically. Doesn't the Bible say this and this and this?" I don't disagree with him — but I say, put ourselves in this actual situation, in context, and this doesn't apply. There are situations in life where I think it's because God is not responsible for the systems of the earth. There's a systems theory — if you're an engineer, you know: if you design a system to work a certain way, or a code, and you set that program to run a certain way, the moment you input something and it outputs something, you can't argue with it, because that is exactly how it's set up to work. And times will come when you're trying to speak the word into something, and you cannot see it manifest according to the word — the word doesn't fit and doesn't come.

But the good thing is: **because the word is alive, every situation you introduce it to — it doesn't matter if that situation is dead, doesn't matter if it doesn't respond to the word — by default, it grows.** When you introduce a seed to all the conditions necessary for germination, it has no choice — it has no option — it must germinate, it must grow. **Therefore, every situation that receives the word of God comes alive, because the word is unchangeable.**

## Nothing Can Separate You From His Love

Maybe to read Romans chapter 8 again — an emphasis on the love of God, and how important that is. It says — where did I start — let me find it:

> *"For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities nor powers, nor things present nor things to come, nor any other created thing, shall be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord."*

I said "Romans 38:38 to 39" while I was searching for the page, and then "4:38" trying to find my place — what I was actually reading, once I found it, was:

> *"For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities nor powers, nor things present nor things to come, nor height nor depth, nor any other created thing, shall be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord."*
> — Romans 8:38-39 (NKJV)

Whoever was writing this was trying to look at things — trying to name everything he could think of — and then just said, "nor any other created thing," to cover the rest. **When you are born again, you are in Christ. And the love of God resides in Christ.** So by the fact that you are in Christ, by the fact that you are a believer, born again — you cannot be separated from the love of God. Because God's love is amazing. He is a good God. This whole conversation stems from the love of God — it requires you to see His love, to understand that you can speak to things, that you can walk in the word, that you can actually do it.

So, behold His love.

## Walking By Faith, Not By Sight

I know the word of God is a seed. The moment you plant a seed, it must grow. So you must talk by faith. Now that you understand nothing can separate you from the love of God — sometimes you ask, "Am I really with God? Can I really be used as an instrument, as a vessel?" I think this is the battle so many young Christians face. We can all attest to that. You feel like there's a place you need to reach before you're ready to be used.

And it is all, maybe, because of condemnation. You can be condemned because of things you've done, because you're looking at yourself. I, by the way — across most of my time in RP, I was a joker. A serious joker. There was a time a sister was choosing an intercessor and I told her, "You want to speak something to my life before you call me?" — I wasn't serious. I was looking at myself, and I couldn't see the ability God was seeing in me, but it was in me. Same as when we tell someone, "Emmy, you lead us in the presence of the Lord with your voice," and you say, "With my voice?" — you can't see what God sees in you.

**When you cannot see that thing God is seeing in you, you're reminded you ought to walk by faith and not by sight.** The things you're seeing are things perceived in the flesh. But when you live a life of faith, walking will push you beyond your comfort zone. No wonder there's that battle with God — because it's comfortable to live in the flesh, and it's very challenging to live in the Spirit. It takes real walking in the Spirit to look at someone failing, at a house about to be foreclosed on, and speak life into it without being shaken.

**So you must walk in faith.** When you come to cell church, we will pray for you, we will celebrate you, we will give you a chance to minister. But even as you do those things — it is your responsibility, as Emmy, as me, Ken — even though I'm doing that thing, how have I aligned my mind to become that thing? Has it become substance in my life? Have I become that thing God desires me to be?

**Because there will come a time when a demand will be placed on you.** Not just by us — by your family, in your company. There will come a time you won't be able to text Benson, and maybe he won't pick up, and you'll have to stand in that moment on your own. And that is why God does not want to be praying for you every time you text Him — He has set structures. You should be praying. We can get lost in the *action* of prayer — the sacrifice of nine to ten, five to six — and forget that the reason you've been placed in that space is for you to become that thing, to tap into that reality.

A demand will be placed on you in your family. You will have children. For men, you are the priest of your house. For the ladies — you are royal priest too, the wife of a priest. **So there will come a time. Are you prepared for it?**

We will pray for you. The man of God will place you in a department and tell you to serve. But in your serving, will you take time to become that thing? This goes beyond church — it even goes to the opportunity you've been given in the company you work in. It's your responsibility to use that opportunity to become. Some of us will say, "It was a miracle, I wasn't qualified, but I got the role." Don't forget — you've been placed. The fact that it's a miracle means it's an opportunity for you to become that thing. RP is one of the spaces I've seen young people do things that leave me shocked — both in service and in the world. It's the same everywhere: you were born in a poor background, but there will come a time you *are* the background you overcome. **It is your responsibility, beyond the actions, to become that thing. Beyond just doing stuff — take your time, invest in the word of God, become that thing.**

---

I don't want to go too far tonight. There's another part I'll record as audio, just to set your expectations — we'll walk down through the character of God. Because it's also important to understand His character. Society has shaped God in a very different way from who He actually is. Our upbringing, our trauma, our pain, our guilt, our condemnation — the systems of the earth portray God in a manner that isn't really Him. **Because God is a Father. He is a good Father.**

It is my desire, and I believe it is the desire of God, that all of us — me, you — understand that God is good, that life is not happening to us, it is happening for us, and that we tap into that reality and operate from that place.

## Closing Prayer

*Ken led the room into prayer — the declarative portions in English are preserved here verbatim; the passages between them were spoken in tongues.*

> Thank You, Lord, because You are loving. It is Your desire and it is Your will to see us prosper. It is Your desire and it is Your will for us to manifest the power that is within us.
>
> There are times, Lord, we have doubted Your love. There are times we have doubted that this journey — are we really walking with You? But flood our eyes with light, that we may behold Your love. That we may behold Your love.
>
> That we will not beg for what is rightfully ours. We will not pray and ask for things that are within our reach.
>
> Even as we interact with Your word, we are interacting with Your word to become that word. We declare that Your word is being made flesh in our lives. It is being made flesh in our situations, in our families, Lord.
>
> Because You say in Your word that You are the portion, Lord — You are the portion of our inheritance. We have a good inheritance. Our lines have fallen to pleasant places.
>
> Father, thank You because You will cause us to see. You will cause us to see Your goodness in our lives. You will cause us to see that life is not happening to us, it is happening for us.
>
> You are good. You are kind. You are faithful. We praise Your name.
>
> Heavenly Father, we thank You because of Your love. Thank You because You are a good God. Thank You because You are a kind God. Thank You because You are a good Father. Thank You because You are the Shepherd of Your pasture. Thank You because You are loving, Lord. Thank You because there is an agenda You have for us, Lord — beyond the things we are doing, beyond our service, beyond our actions, beyond our lives. There is an agenda, and Your agenda is great. Your agenda is big.
>
> Father, flood our eyes with light, that we may see, and that we may operate from where You have called us, Lord. You've called us to be ambassadors with Christ. We operate from that place, oh God. We choose to perceive life differently, in accordance with Your word. We choose to walk in accordance with that word, Lord. We choose to respond to situations with Your word.
>
> Father, we declare that Your word is being made flesh in our lives, Lord — in the areas of our workplaces, oh God, in our belief, in our mentality, in our mind. Every stronghold, Lord, that has kept us in the same place, that has kept us in circles — every stronghold is being brought to the authority of Your word, to the authority of You, oh God. Every stronghold is being broken in the name of Jesus, Lord.
>
> We behold Your love. We behold Your goodness. We behold Your faithfulness, Lord. In Jesus' mighty name. Amen. We pray and we believe. Amen.

---

## Summary

| Session | Theme | Key Scripture |
|---|---|---|
| ByPass Cell Church (Royal Priesthood breakout) | Life is happening *for* you, not *to* you — moving from doing to becoming | Romans 8:38-39 |

## Core Declarations

1. Life is not happening to you — it is happening for you.
2. God calls you to Himself before He calls you to a people.
3. Your measure of righteousness is not by actions — it is not in the doing, it is in the becoming.
4. Nothing — no power, nothing present or to come — can separate you from the love of God.
5. The word of God is alive; wherever it is introduced, it grows, whether or not the situation responds to it.
6. You are seated in heavenly places in Christ — an ambassador operating from a different place than the systems of the earth.
7. God's mercy is new every morning and endures forever; He is not waiting for you to earn it.
8. Walking in the Spirit will always feel more costly than walking in the flesh, but it is the only place you cannot be shaken.
9. You will not beg for what is already your inheritance — see it, and rise to reign in it.
10. Beyond the doing — the serving, the ministry, the position — is the question: have you become the thing God has called you to be?

---

> *"It is not in the doing. It is in the becoming."*
> — Ken Muritu

---

## Done — same drill, followed through completely

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Standalone NeuTTS synthesis helper.

Called by tts_tool.py via subprocess to keep the TTS model (~500MB)
in a separate process that exits after synthesis — no lingering memory.

Usage:
    python -m tools.neutts_synth --text "Hello" --out output.wav \
        --ref-audio samples/jo.wav --ref-text samples/jo.txt

Requires: python -m pip install -U neutts[all]
System:   apt install espeak-ng  (or brew install espeak-ng)
"""

import argparse
import struct
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def _write_wav(path: str, samples, sample_rate: int = 24000) -> None:
    """Write a WAV file from float32 samples (no soundfile dependency)."""
    import numpy as np

    if not isinstance(samples, np.ndarray):
        samples = np.array(samples, dtype=np.float32)
    samples = samples.flatten()

    # Clamp and convert to int16
    samples = np.clip(samples, -1.0, 1.0)
    pcm = (samples * 32767).astype(np.int16)

    num_channels = 1
    bits_per_sample = 16
    byte_rate = sample_rate * num_channels * (bits_per_sample // 8)
    block_align = num_channels * (bits_per_sample // 8)
    data_size = len(pcm) * (bits_per_sample // 8)

    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(b"RIFF")
        f.write(struct.pack("<I", 36 + data_size))
        f.write(b"WAVE")
        f.write(b"fmt ")
        f.write(struct.pack("<IHHIIHH", 16, 1, num_channels, sample_rate,
                            byte_rate, block_align, bits_per_sample))
        f.write(b"data")
        f.write(struct.pack("<I", data_size))
        f.write(pcm.tobytes())


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="NeuTTS synthesis helper")
    parser.add_argument("--text", required=True, help="Text to synthesize")
    parser.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="Output WAV path")
    parser.add_argument("--ref-audio", required=True, help="Reference voice audio path")
    parser.add_argument("--ref-text", required=True, help="Reference voice transcript path")
    parser.add_argument("--model", default="neuphonic/neutts-air-q4-gguf",
                        help="HuggingFace backbone model repo")
    parser.add_argument("--device", default="cpu", help="Device (cpu/cuda/mps)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    # llama_cpp (backbone) offloads to GPU only for the literal string "gpu";
    # torch (codec) only accepts "cuda". A single --device value can't satisfy
    # both — "cuda" silently no-ops on the backbone, leaving it on CPU.
    backbone_device = "gpu" if args.device == "cuda" else args.device
    codec_device = args.device

    # Validate inputs
    ref_audio = Path(args.ref_audio).expanduser()
    ref_text_path = Path(args.ref_text).expanduser()
    if not ref_audio.exists():
        print(f"Error: reference audio not found: {ref_audio}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    if not ref_text_path.exists():
        print(f"Error: reference text not found: {ref_text_path}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    ref_text = ref_text_path.

Honest answer: I don't have a built-in voice-cloning tool of my own. But there's a real, free, local capability already wired into your Hermes setup — just not installed yet. Here's exactly what I found, not a guess:

**What's actually there:**
- `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/tools/neutts_synth.py` — a working wrapper around **NeuTTS Air** (by Neuphonic), a genuine zero-shot voice-cloning TTS model. It runs **locally, on CPU, free, no API key** — good fit for this machine (no GPU needed).
- It's referenced in Hermes's broader `tts_tool.py` as one of several providers — the only *local* one that does actual voice cloning (KittenTTS/Piper are local but fixed-voice; MiniMax/ElevenLabs also clone voices but are paid cloud APIs needing a key).

- There's already a reference sample sitting there (`neutts_samples/jo.wav` + exact-matching `jo.txt`) — someone tested this before, so the pattern is proven on this machine.

**How it actually works:** you give it a short (~13-15 sec) clean reference clip of a voice + the *exact* transcript of what's said in it. From then on, any text you type gets synthesized in that cloned voice — precisely what you're asking for.

**One honest caveat:** the ByPass recording is a ~24kbps room recording with audience interjections layered in — clone quality depends heavily on how clean the reference clip is, so I'd need to pick a short, isolated, clear segment of just you speaking (I already have the full verbatim transcript, so I can match text to audio exactly).

def text_to_speech_tool(
    text: str,
    output_path: Optional[str] = None,
    speed: Optional[float] = None,
    instructions: Optional[str] = None,
    provider: Optional[str] = None,
) -> str:
    """Convert text to speech audio with long-form chunking.

    Long text is normalized, split into provider-safe chunks, synthesized
    sequentially, and packed against destination platform upload limits.
    Each provider request is encoded to its final format before files are
    packed. Multi-chunk voice output is re-encoded when combined; failed
    combines preserve separate valid files, and no over-limit final artifact
    is returned.

    On messaging platforms, the returned MEDIA:<path> tag is intercepted
    by the send pipeline and delivered as a native voice message.
    In CLI mode, the file is saved to ~/voice-memos/.

    Args:
        text: The text to convert to speech. Provider-specific per-request
            character caps apply automatically (OpenAI 4096, xAI 15000,
            MiniMax 10000, ElevenLabs 5k-40k depending on model); longer
            input is split into ordered chunks without silent truncation.
        output_path: Optional custom save path.
        speed: Optional playback speed multiplier (0.25-4.0).
        instructions: Optional voice-design guidance (tone, emotion, pacing).
        provider: Optional TTS provider override.

    Returns:
        str: JSON result with success, file_path, file_paths, and MEDIA tag.
    """
    if not text or not text.strip():
        return tool_error("Text is required", success=False)

    # Normalize text via the shared cleaner: markdown, emoji, think blocks,
    # verifier footer, units, newline flattening.
    try:
        from tools.tts_text_normalize import prepare_spoken_text
        text = prepare_spoken_text(text, max_chars=None)

Good progress — it's now downloading the actual packages (torch, transformers, etc.) rather than just resolving. Confirming: `resemble_perth` just landed, which is genuinely relevant to your commercialization question.

## Answering your pipeline/commercialization question directly

**Yes, this is fully possible with free, open-source, local tools** — that's exactly what we're building. To be concrete about what "the pipeline" actually is:

- `~/bin/speak-as-ken.sh "your text"` → outputs an audio file in your cloned voice. Works with typed text, pasted/piped text (`echo "..." | speak-as-ken.sh -`), or a whole file (`speak-as-ken.sh - < script.txt`).
- It's a thin wrapper around Hermes's own `text_to_speech_tool()` — not something I hacked together standalone. That function already handles long-text chunking (sentence-aware, ~2000 chars per NeuTTS call), normalization, and stitching chunks back into one audio file. So pasting a full paragraph or a whole script works out of the box, not just short lines.
- Zero marginal cost per generation — it's local CPU inference, no API key, no per-character billing.

**On commercializing it — the license actually works in your favor, verified just now (not assumed):** NeuTTS Air is **Apache 2.0** — genuinely permits commercial use. Two details worth knowing if you take this toward a product:
1. Every clip NeuTTS generates is automatically watermarked (the "Perth" watermarker, imperceptible to the ear but detectable) — that's a responsible-use feature already built in, not something you'd need to add.
2. The model card is explicit that voice cloning requires the cloned person's consent — fine for your own voice; if "use it for other people" later means *other users* cloning *their own* voice (an ElevenLabs/kikivoice-style product), that's the same model everyone else in this space uses. If it ever means cloning *someone else's* voice without their say-so, that's the one line I'd flag as worth stopping to think about, not a technical limitation but a real consent one.

Once the install finishes (still downloading — torch/transformers are the big ones), I'll run the wrapper end-to-end with a real test sentence and send you the audio so you can actually judge the clone quality yourself.

        # Critical flag choice: `--extra all`, NOT `--all-extras`. The

        # deps that fail offline). See pyproject.toml's [all] for the

        # progress UI instead of staring at a frozen prompt.
        if UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT="$SCRIPT_DIR/venv" $UV_CMD sync --extra all --locked; then

content.text:
## Fully reverted, and verified — not just assumed

- Killed the running synthesis test and model download before it wrote anything of size (HF cache confirmed at 8KB, effectively empty).
- Uninstalled everything via `uv sync --extra all --locked` — Hermes's own hash-verified lockfile — rather than manual `pip uninstall`, which matters: it also caught and fixed **6 shared transitive packages our install had silently bumped** (`protobuf`, `pygments`, `pytz`, `rpds-py`, `tqdm`, `typing-extensions`, `watchfiles`, `wcwidth`, `yarl`) back to Hermes's exact pinned versions. A plain `pip uninstall` of just the packages we added would have missed that drift entirely.
- **Verified, not assumed, that Hermes is fine**: restarted `hermes-gateway.service` live — it came back up cleanly on a fresh PID with normal startup output, no errors.
- Removed: `espeak-ng`, the voice sample + config block in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`, the `speak-as-ken.sh` wrapper, and the diagnostic/extraction files in Downloads.
- **Kept**: the compiled teaching `.md` and the raw ByPass transcript `.txt` — those are from the earlier transcription task, unrelated to voice cloning, so I left them alone.

**Disk: 83% → 60%** (3.1G free), pip itself is gone from the venv (matches the original state exactly), venv is back to 241M.

One thing worth remembering for when we pick this back up: Hermes actually has its own curated `voice` extra in `pyproject.toml` (part of `setup-hermes.sh`'s `_ALL_EXTRAS`), which likely includes NeuTTS at properly tested, hash-verified pinned versions — that's almost certainly the right path next time, instead of raw `pip install neutts[all]` pulling fresh-latest versions straight from PyPI (which is exactly what caused the CUDA-wheel pull, the `antlr4` build failure, and the `torchao`/`torchtune` version conflict this round).

So this isn't a camera problem at all — it's a **rendering** problem. guvcview's default preview widget uses SDL2, and SDL's window-embedding trick for the live preview is known to render blank under native Wayland (this session's `XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`, confirmed).
