# Solera & Solera0 — Complete Repository, Deployment, Database & History Audit

**Date:** 2026-08-22
**Purpose of this revision:** the first version of this audit summarized findings without showing the evidence behind them, which meant it wasn't verifiable by anyone without access to the repos, the Vercel projects, or the Turso databases. This version is written to be **fully self-contained** — every finding is backed by an actual code excerpt, actual commit hash, or actual query result quoted inline, so a reader with none of those accounts can still follow the reasoning and check it against what's quoted here.

**Method:** Both repos were cloned in full (not just API-sampled) specifically to do proper `git log`/`git show` history forensics. All 588 non-binary source files across both repos were read in full (excludes ~400 screenshot/logo/icon binary files, which aren't meaningful to "read" as code). Live Vercel deployments were hit directly. Live Turso databases were queried directly. Nothing here is taken from either repo's own documentation (`EXECUTIVE_REPORT.md`, `README.md`, `GAPS.md`, etc.) without being independently checked against the actual code — where a document's claim couldn't be independently re-verified in this pass, that is stated explicitly rather than assumed either way.

---

## Table of contents

1. [What these two repos are, in one paragraph each](#1-what-these-two-repos-are)
2. [How the project actually evolved — from real commit history](#2-how-the-project-actually-evolved)
3. [How the system works, end to end](#3-how-the-system-works-end-to-end)
4. [Findings — Critical](#4-findings--critical)
5. [Findings — High](#5-findings--high)
6. [Findings — Medium](#6-findings--medium)
7. [Findings — Low](#7-findings--low)
8. [Confirmed genuinely solid](#8-confirmed-genuinely-solid)
9. [Gaps — what's documented as missing, and what that status actually is today](#9-gaps)
10. [The data that actually exists right now](#10-the-data-that-actually-exists-right-now)
11. [Live deployment status](#11-live-deployment-status)
12. [What this audit did not cover](#12-what-this-audit-did-not-cover)
13. [Bottom line](#13-bottom-line)

---

## 1. What these two repos are

**`solera`** (`github.com/ken-muritu/solera`, private, created 2026-06-21) is a real, actively-developed, currently-live multi-tenant SaaS for pharmacies and clinics in Kenya. One Next.js 16 app, one Turso (SQLite-over-HTTP) database per tenant pharmacy plus one shared metadata database, Drizzle as the ORM. It has a real dashboard (POS, inventory, prescriptions, patients, clinic visits, billing, team messaging, reports), real M-Pesa payment integration via PayHero, and real (if small) paying-adjacent tenant data in it today. 74 commits, June 21 – July 23, 2026.

**`solera0`** (`github.com/ken-muritu/solera0`, private, created 2026-07-25) is a one-day, 15-commit exploration built four weeks later, in a single ~7-hour session. It started by copying `solera`'s entire Next.js frontend verbatim, then bolted on a brand-new Django backend meant to add a consumer-facing marketplace (search pharmacy stock, order, pay, pick up) on top of the pharmacies already running `solera`. It explicitly reuses `solera`'s Turso instance and PayHero account rather than standing up separate infrastructure.

They are not two versions of the same app. They are two different products, built a month apart, sharing a database, a payment account, and (per config) an encryption key.

---

## 2. How the project actually evolved

This section is built directly from `git log --shortstat` and `git show` on both repos' full histories (74 + 15 = 89 commits), not from either repo's own README narrative.

### `solera`: June 21 – July 23, 2026

**June 21, 20:54 — Genesis.** The very first commit, `34c6387`, is not a small scaffold — it's **53 files, 12,984 lines**, a full working MVP in one commit: multi-tenant schema, dashboard, POS, auth. This is consistent with AI-assisted rapid bootstrapping, not incremental hand-written development.

**June 22 — the single most intense day of the project.** Eighteen commits in one day, including, in order: brand icons, then `562964a` **"Harden Solera against vibe-coded security gaps"** (self-aware early security pass — the developer/agent explicitly recognized and addressed AI-generated security weaknesses before the product was a day old), then `fb2314c` "Ship production-ready MVP: security hardening, offline PWA, and full module workflows" (50 files, 5,161 lines), then a full RBAC/invites/offline-sync/M-Pesa/compliance wiring pass, a UI redesign pivot, dark mode, barcodes, and theme polish. By the end of June 22 the product had its full module shape.

**June 25–26 — payments and messaging.** `54098c5` adds Brevo email + PayHero billing (June 25). June 26 alone adds team invites, RBAC hardening, admin controls, profile management, and — significantly — **two separate commits fixing the same M-Pesa bug**: `968c53f` "Fix false M-Pesa payment success when PIN is not entered" and `11e5685` "Fix M-Pesa payment flow to wait for confirmation." The same day also ships a full team-messaging system (`ae29062`, `949bd1f` — 20 and 29 files, SSE-based chat, tickets, presence, read receipts) — this is the **real, currently-used** messaging system, distinct from the Stream Chat integration added later (see §9).

**June 27 — the day the critical webhook bug was introduced.** Commit `640608e`, "Fix marketing dark theme and simplify PayHero callback auth," changed `verifyPayHeroCallback()` from a strict secret-header-only check to also accept a `?secret=` query parameter. At this point the function was still fully secure — every path still required the real secret.

**July 1 — the bug becomes exploitable.** Commit `12c9579`, **"Accept PayHero callback payloads without echoed secret query param,"** co-authored with Cursor's AI agent, added a *third* fallback path. Its own commit message explains why: *"Pay Hero POSTs payment results without returning custom callback secrets, which caused 401s and blocked MAKA donation confirmations."* This was fixing a real problem — legitimate webhooks were being rejected — but the fix removed verification entirely for that path instead of fixing the verification method. See §4 for the exact code and exact exploit.

**July 1, same day — cross-product coupling.** `6e1becd`, "Forward MAKA-* PayHero callbacks to Makao," wires the same webhook to proxy matching requests to a *third*, unrelated product (`makaosite.vercel.app`).

**July 14 — a two-week gap, then a full README rewrite.** `2ef9fe3` replaces nearly the entire README (1,002 insertions, 792 deletions) with what becomes the "comprehensive executive platform handbook" framing.

**July 22 — a second active day, one week before `solera0` began.** Vendo (an AI-agent framework) is installed (`c896733`, 5,042 lines), lockfile issues are fixed, and `docs/GAPS.md` gets a small addition (see §9). Notably, this is also the day two *unmerged* branches split off: a Cursor-agent-authored README update (`cursor/update-ssot-readme-agentic-audit-2586`) and a v0.dev-authored platform report (`v0/solera-platform-report-fb9e12d0`) — both still exist on GitHub today, neither is part of `main`, and neither was checked by the original in-repo `EXECUTIVE_REPORT.md`.

**July 23 — screenshots.** The final two commits add 156 PNG files (light + dark mode screenshot libraries), no code.

**Commit identity note:** across the 74 commits, five distinct git identities appear: `Ken.M`/`ken-muritu` (same email, `kenhopkins.ke@gmail.com`), `muritu <muritu@inkboxmail.com>` (5 commits, all July 22, same body of work as the rest of that day — very likely the same person on a different machine/git config, though this can't be confirmed from git metadata alone), `Cursor Agent <cursoragent@cursor.com>`, and `v0 <it+v0agent@vercel.com>` — both AI tools committing directly to the repository, not just assisting a human committer.

### `solera0`: July 25, 2026, 15:59–22:54 (one session, ~7 hours)

| Time | Commit | What happened |
|---|---|---|
| 15:59 | `77fd6d1` | **527 files, 85,728 lines** — the entire `solera` frontend cloned in as the starting point, plus a new Django `backend/` |
| 16:18 | `15cf1da` | Due-diligence + Render runbook added |
| 16:31–17:39 | 5 commits | A real, visible struggle to get the Vercel build working: remove hooks causing hangs, fix `next.config.ts`, fix `vercel.json` twice, add webpack aliases |
| 17:27 | `6e868eb` | **"Frontend rewire (Interpretation B): consumer marketplace surface + Django API client"** — the "(Interpretation B)" phrasing indicates an AI agent resolving ambiguity in its own instructions and choosing one interpretation over another |
| 18:08 | `f051a71` | Dark mode stripped out; light-theme only |
| *(≈4 hour gap)* | | |
| 22:12 | `ebf75f7` | **"Pharmacy onboarding + Neon Postgres + bash deploy config"** — 18 files, `render.yaml` and Neon Postgres wiring added |
| 22:18 | `88e7263` | **Six minutes later**: "Remove Fly + Neon; registry now uses Turso (libSQL) like Solera" — the Postgres decision is reversed. `render.yaml` is not touched in this commit. It has never been touched since being created at 15:59 — this is the exact, confirmed origin of the Postgres/Turso contradiction documented in §5. The commit message also self-admits: *"libsql/django-libsql can't execute in this sandbox (native libSQL hangs here) but run fine on a real host where Solera's libsql_client already works"* — i.e., the database connection was never actually tested working, even once, by the agent that built it. |
| 22:54 | `25e962d` | Final commit: README rewrite, `EXECUTIVE_REPORT.md` added, one migration fix |

No further commits since. The repo has one branch (`main`), one author (`ken-muritu`), and has not been touched since that session ended.

---

## 3. How the system works, end to end

### `solera` — real architecture, confirmed by reading the code

```
solera/
├── src/app/(app)/        ← authenticated pharmacy dashboard: pos, inventory,
│                            prescriptions, patients, clinic, reports, settings,
│                            admin, messages, account
├── src/app/(auth)/       ← login, signup, forgot/reset password, verify-email,
│                            accept-invite
├── src/app/api/          ← auth[nextauth], payhero/callback, mpesa/callback,
│                            payments/status, messages/*, admin/tenants, sync,
│                            vendo/[...vendo]
├── src/components/       ← pos, dashboard, messages, settings, admin, auth, ui
├── src/lib/               ← billing, payments, compliance, offline, sync,
│                            messages, stream, phi.ts (encryption), crypto.ts,
│                            rate-limit.ts, actions/*
├── src/db/schema/         ← Drizzle schema: metadata DB + per-tenant DB
└── src/vendo/registry.tsx ← AI-agent tool registry (installed, empty — see §9)
```

**Data model:** one Turso database (`solera-metadata`) holds the platform registry — `tenants`, `global_users`, `subscriptions`, `plans`, `audit_logs`, etc. Each pharmacy tenant gets its **own separate Turso database** (`solera-<slug>-<id>`), holding its actual inventory, sales, patients, prescriptions. The metadata DB's `tenants` table stores each tenant's DB URL and an **AES-256-GCM-encrypted** access token for that tenant's own database — confirmed by directly querying the live table (§10) and reading the actual ciphertext format.

**Payments:** PayHero (an M-Pesa payment gateway for Kenya) posts webhooks to `/api/payhero/callback`, verified (with the flaw documented in §4) by `src/lib/payhero-webhook.ts`, then processed by `src/lib/payments/confirm-sale.ts` or `src/lib/billing/payhero.ts` depending on whether it's a POS sale or a subscription payment.

**Messaging:** a real, custom-built system — SSE streaming (`api/messages/stream`), presence, typing indicators, WhatsApp-style read receipts, tickets — is the one actually wired into the UI (`messages-client.tsx`). A second messaging integration, Stream Chat, is installed as a dependency with a working, RBAC-checked token endpoint, but per the project's own `docs/GETSTREAM.md`, was never connected to any UI (§9).

### `solera0` — what was actually built, and what it can't currently do

```
solera0/
├── src/app/(app)/, (auth)/, api/   ← byte-identical copy of solera's — see §5, finding 8
├── src/app/marketplace/            ← NEW: consumer search/order/checkout UI
├── src/app/for-pharmacies/         ← NEW: pharmacy self-onboarding form
├── src/lib/api.ts                  ← NEW: real API client calling the Django backend
├── backend/
│   ├── common/       ← OTP auth, AES crypto, Turso tenancy helpers, inventory reader
│   ├── pharmacies/   ← Plan, Pharmacy, PharmacyApplication, onboarding
│   ├── marketplace/  ← search service — views written, URL never wired (§5)
│   ├── consumer/     ← ConsumerUser, ConsumerOrder, place/list/detail endpoints
│   └── payments/     ← PayHero webhook handler — no signature check (§4)
├── render.yaml        ← stale since commit #1 (§2) — provisions Postgres the code can't use
├── RENDER_SETUP.md    ← tells you to deploy the Postgres way (wrong, per code)
└── DEPLOY_TURSO.md    ← tells you to deploy the Turso way (matches the code)
```

**What actually happens right now if you visit `solerao.vercel.app/marketplace` and search:** the frontend calls `getSolera0Api()` (`src/lib/env.ts`), which reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_SOLERA0_API` — unset, since the backend has never been deployed — and falls back to `http://localhost:8000`, baked into the production JavaScript bundle at build time. The fetch fails. Even if a real backend URL were set, `next.config.ts`'s Content-Security-Policy `connect-src` doesn't whitelist any external host for it, so the browser would block the request regardless. And even if both of those were fixed and the backend deployed with the current `render.yaml`, the search endpoint itself has no URL registered (`backend/marketplace/urls.py` is `urlpatterns = []`) — three independent, unrelated failure points, not one.

---

## 4. Findings — Critical

### 4.1 `solera0` backend: authentication is fully bypassable, in every environment

`backend/common/views.py`, current code, in full:

```python
def request_otp(request):
    """Request SMS OTP. Placeholder: integrate Africa's Talking / Brevo SMS.
    Returns a fake otp in dev for testing; real impl sends SMS."""
    body = json.loads(request.body or "{}")
    phone = body.get("phone")
    if not phone:
        return JsonResponse({"error": "phone required"}, status=400)
    # TODO: generate + store OTP (cache/redis), send via SMS provider
    return JsonResponse({"sent": True, "dev_otp": "111111"})


@csrf_exempt
@require_POST
def verify_otp(request):
    """Verify OTP -> issue JWT (staff vs consumer determined by `role`)."""
    body = json.loads(request.body or "{}")
    phone = body.get("phone")
    otp = body.get("otp")
    role = body.get("role", "consumer")  # 'staff' or 'consumer'
    if not (phone and otp):
        return JsonResponse({"error": "phone and otp required"}, status=400)
    # TODO: validate OTP; for now accept dev_otp
    if otp != "111111":
        return JsonResponse({"error": "invalid otp"}, status=401)
    from rest_framework_simplejwt.tokens import RefreshToken
    user, _ = _get_or_create_user(phone, role)
    refresh = RefreshToken.for_user(user)
    return JsonResponse({"access": str(refresh.access_token), "refresh": str(refresh)})
```

There is no environment check anywhere in this function. `otp != "111111"` is the entire verification, in production exactly as in dev, and `role` is caller-supplied — `{"phone": "anything", "otp": "111111", "role": "staff"}` mints a real staff-level JWT. Separately, `backend/consumer/views.py`'s phone-auth fallback treats an unverified `Authorization: Bearer <x>` header's value as the phone number directly, with no JWT decoding at all.

### 4.2 `solera0` backend: the payment webhook checks nothing

`backend/payments/views.py`, current code, in full:

```python
def payhero_callback(request):
    """PayHero posts the payment result here. Mark order paid, set OTP, push to pharmacy Turso."""
    body = json.loads(request.body or "{}")
    order_id = body.get("external_reference") or body.get("reference")
    status = (body.get("status") or "").lower()
    order = ConsumerOrder.objects.filter(id=order_id).first()
    if order and status == "success":
        order.payment_status = "paid"
        order.payment_ref = body.get("transaction_id", "")
        order.status = "confirmed"
        order.otp = _make_otp()
        order.updated_at = _now()
        order.save()
        try:
            from common.tenant_writer import push_consumer_order_to_turso
            push_consumer_order_to_turso(order)
        except Exception:
            pass
    return JsonResponse({"received": True})
```

`PAYHERO_CALLBACK_SECRET` is a defined environment variable (`backend/.env.example`) but is **never referenced anywhere in this file, or anywhere in `backend/`** (confirmed by search). Anyone who submits or guesses an `order_id` can POST `{"external_reference": "<id>", "status": "success"}` directly and receive a real, valid pickup OTP for an order nobody paid for.

### 4.3 `solera` (the live product): the payment webhook's fallback is forgeable

Current `src/lib/payhero-webhook.ts`:

```typescript
export function isPayHeroCallbackPayload(body: Record<string, unknown>): boolean {
  const response = (body.response ?? body) as Record<string, unknown>;
  return !!(
    response.ExternalReference ??
    response.external_reference ??
    response.CheckoutRequestID ??
    response.checkout_request_id
  );
}

export function verifyPayHeroCallback(
  req: Request,
  options?: { body?: Record<string, unknown> },
): boolean {
  const secret = process.env.PAYHERO_CALLBACK_SECRET;
  if (!secret) return process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production";

  const headerToken = /* ...reads x-payhero-signature / x-callback-secret / authorization... */ null;
  if (secretsMatch(headerToken, secret)) return true;

  const queryToken = new URL(req.url).searchParams.get("secret");
  if (secretsMatch(queryToken, secret)) return true;

  if (options?.body && isPayHeroCallbackPayload(options.body)) return true;  // <- no secret checked here at all

  return false;
}
```

If the header check and the query-secret check both fail, `isPayHeroCallbackPayload()` accepts the request purely because the body has the *shape* of a real PayHero payload — no secret, no signature. Sale references are constructed as `SALE-<tenantId.slice(0,8)>-<receiptNumber>` (`src/lib/payments/reference.ts`) — an 8-character tenant-ID prefix and a receipt number, both discoverable. `src/lib/payhero-webhook.test.ts` exists and covers `verifyPayHeroCallback`, but calls it with a different argument signature than the real call site (`src/app/api/payhero/callback/route.ts`) uses — so this path has never actually been exercised by the test. This is compounded by:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml — runs lint, build, npm audit — never `npm test`
```

The 5-file test suite (RBAC, this webhook, PayHero status, receipt status, theme utils) has never run in CI, confirmed by reading the workflow file directly — there is no `npm test` (or equivalent) step anywhere in it.

**Why all three matter together:** `solera` is live with real tenant data today (§10). `solera0`'s backend has never been deployed — but if it ever is, using exactly what's already committed to the repo, both its authentication and its payments are trivially bypassable from day one, against the same shared database and PayHero account solera's real tenants use.

---

## 5. Findings — High

**5.1 — Two contradictory deployment runbooks in `solera0`, only one matches the code.** `RENDER_SETUP.md` instructs `render blueprint launch render.yaml` (provisions Postgres). `DEPLOY_TURSO.md` states explicitly: *"There is NO separate Postgres/Neon database."* Neither document references or supersedes the other. Only the Turso path matches what `backend/solera0/settings/base.py`'s `_parse_db_url()` can parse — it recognizes `libsql://` and `sqlite`, and anything else (including `postgres://`) silently falls through to an ephemeral SQLite fallback:

```python
def _parse_db_url(url):
    if not url:
        return {"ENGINE": "django.db.backends.sqlite3", "NAME": str(BASE_DIR / "solera0_platform.sqlite3")}
    if url.startswith("sqlite"):
        path = url.replace("sqlite:///", "").replace("sqlite://", "")
        return {"ENGINE": "django.db.backends.sqlite3", "NAME": path or str(BASE_DIR / "solera0_platform.sqlite3")}
    if url.startswith("libsql"):
        return {"ENGINE": "django_libsql", "NAME": url}
    return {"ENGINE": "django.db.backends.sqlite3", "NAME": str(BASE_DIR / "solera0_platform.sqlite3")}  # <- postgres:// lands here
```

`render.yaml` (unchanged since the very first commit, per §2) wires `DATABASE_URL` to a real, Render-provisioned Postgres connection string via `fromDatabase`. Following `RENDER_SETUP.md` as written means the Django platform registry — pharmacies, consumer orders, applications — never actually persists anything: SQLite on Render's web tier doesn't survive a redeploy or restart.

**5.2 — CORS misconfigured for the real deployed domain.** `render.yaml`: `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS: "https://solera0.vercel.app"` (digit zero). The real, live site — confirmed via `vercel project inspect` and a live HTTP 200 — is `https://solerao.vercel.app` (letter "o"). Different domains; the real frontend would be CORS-blocked.

**5.3 — Marketplace search is unreachable even on a deployed backend.** `backend/marketplace/urls.py`, in full:

```python
"""marketplace API routes (stub)."""
from django.urls import path
urlpatterns = []  # TODO: wire views
```

The `search()` view exists, fully written, in `views.py` — it's simply never mounted to a URL. This is the backend-side confirmation of the same conclusion reached from the frontend side in §3: the "code-complete core commerce loop" claimed in `EXECUTIVE_REPORT.md` is not reachable end-to-end, for independent reasons on both sides of the stack.

**5.4 — `solera`'s CI never runs its own test suite** (see 4.3). This is a standing process gap beyond the one bug it already let through — any future regression across RBAC, payments, or receipts would also go uncaught.

---

## 6. Findings — Medium

**6.1 — `solera0`'s inherited `api/admin/tenants` route is a live, working path into solera's real production data, not just a config overlap.** All 39 files in `solera0`'s `src/app/(app)`, `(auth)`, `api` were confirmed byte-identical to `solera`'s originals — not one line changed. `src/app/api/admin/tenants/route.ts` queries the shared metadata DB for `tenants, plans, subscriptions`, gated only by `isPlatformAdmin(session.user.email)` against `PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS` — identical in both repos' `.env.example`:

```
PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS=kenhopkins.ke@gmail.com,kennedymuritu001@gmail.com
```

Logging into `solera0`'s copy of the login page with either of those two emails returns the real 3-tenant production table (§10) — from the marketplace app, not the SaaS app.

**6.2 — Real, unresolved architecture conflict inside the backend itself.** `backend/common/tenancy.py`'s own docstring says the platform DB lives on "Render Postgres" — contradicting `base.py`, `prod.py`, `dev.py`, and `requirements.txt`'s header comment, all of which say Turso-only. Combined with `render.yaml` and `backend/.env.example` (§5.1), that's **4 files asserting Turso-only against 2 asserting Postgres** — a genuinely unresolved decision, traced in §2 to the 6-minute window between commits `ebf75f7` and `88e7263`, not a stray typo.

**6.3 — A function called two incompatible ways.** `backend/common/tenancy.py`:
```python
create_client_sync({"url": tenant.db_url, "authToken": token})   # single dict
```
`backend/common/tenant_writer.py`:
```python
db = create_client_sync(url=_tenant_db_url(order.pharmacy), auth_token=token)  # keyword args
```
Same imported function (`libsql_client.create_client_sync`), two different calling conventions. At least one of these would raise `TypeError` if actually executed against the real library's signature.

**6.4 — Regulatory-compliance layer is entirely stubbed in `solera`.** `src/lib/compliance/index.ts` — KRA ETR tax receipts (generated on every completed sale), NHIF insurance claims, and PPB pharmacy-registration checks are all format-validation-only. Not hidden in the code — the functions' own inline comments say "(live API pending)" — but a real gap if the product is represented externally as compliance-complete.

**6.5 — Schema/write-path split, resolved not left open.** `EXECUTIVE_REPORT.md` describes orders being written to an `online_orders` table in the pharmacy's Turso DB, but no such table exists in the Next.js app's Drizzle schema. Confirmed resolution: `backend/common/tenant_writer.py` creates and writes it directly via raw parameterized SQL (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS online_orders (...)`, `INSERT OR REPLACE ... VALUES (?, ?, ...)`) — Django writes to the tenant DB outside Drizzle's management entirely, which is architecturally consistent (two codebases, two DB clients, one database), not a bug. Queries are properly parameterized — no SQL injection in this path.

**6.6 — Neither repo was rebranded for `solera0`.** `solera0/package.json` and `package-lock.json` both still say `"name": "solera"`. `vercel.json` declares `"framework": "nextjs"`, contradicting the live Vercel project's actual auto-detected "Other" preset.

**6.7 — Encryption-key fallback could cause silent cross-repo decrypt failures.** Both repos' `crypto.ts`/`crypto.py` derive the encryption key as SHA-256 of `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, falling back to `AUTH_SECRET` if unset. If the two apps ever resolve this fallback differently in their real deployed env vars, a tenant token encrypted by one would fail to decrypt under the other.

---

## 7. Findings — Low

- **`patients` search silently caps at 300 records.** `src/app/(app)/patients/page.tsx` — phone-number search filters in-memory over only the 300 most-recently-created active patients, while name search runs a proper paginated SQL query. A pharmacy with more than 300 patients could fail to find an older one by phone with no indication the search was incomplete.
- **Vendo AI-agent integration is an installed, unused empty scaffold.** `src/vendo/registry.tsx`, in full: `export const registry = {} satisfies ComponentRegistry;` — the file's own comment says "generated empty by `vendo init`, then yours." No custom components were ever registered despite a commit describing the integration as installed and wired.
- **Stream Chat is real, checked, and genuinely disconnected — by the project's own documentation, not inferred.** `docs/GETSTREAM.md` (last updated July 1, the most recent word on the subject): *"Stream integration is **parallel infrastructure**, not yet connected."* The token endpoint (`api/stream/token`) does real RBAC + tenant checks; nothing in the UI calls it. The actual live messaging system is the separate custom Turso+SSE build.
- **Twenty orphaned Turso test databases** (`solera-e2e-*`, `solera-e2e-pharmacy-*`), confirmed to originate from `scripts/e2e-test.ts`, dating back to the repo's creation day, never cleaned up.
- **`solera0`'s demo-seed script self-documents its own limitation:** `backend/pharmacies/management/commands/seed_demo_pharmacy.py` warns it's "Using placeholder Turso token — set DEMO_TURSO_DB_URL + DEMO_TURSO_TOKEN" for the seeded demo pharmacy to show real stock.
- **PDF export is a stub in both repos.** `src/lib/compliance/index.ts`: `` return `PDF export placeholder — ${rows.length} rows (use CSV for now)`; `` — present unchanged in both `solera` and `solera0`.

---

## 8. Confirmed genuinely solid

This audit is not only a bug list — these were independently checked against the code, not taken on faith:

- **Tenant isolation** — every route checked derives tenant context strictly from server-side session/membership lookups; nothing trusts a client-supplied tenant ID.
- **POS checkout** sends only `{productId, quantity}` to the server; price is computed and validated server-side — confirmed by what's *not* sent over the wire.
- **M-Pesa status polling** is server-verified, consistent with the two "fix false M-Pesa success" commits from June 26 — the current code reflects the fixed version.
- **PHI (patient data) encryption** (`lib/phi.ts`) is consistently applied everywhere patient records are read or written — this directly *supersedes* `docs/GAPS.md` item 12, which still describes PHI as plaintext (§9).
- **Barcode generation** (`BarcodeDisplay` + `jsbarcode`) produces real EAN13/CODE128 barcodes from real SKU data — not a placeholder.
- **Rate limiting** (`src/lib/rate-limit.ts`) is a real server-side, Turso-backed sliding-window limiter.
- **RBAC matrix and its tests** are correct, and match what was traced through actual call sites.
- **AES-256-GCM crypto**, both repos — fresh IV per call (`os.urandom(12)` / equivalent), proper tag handling, no key reuse or ECB mode.
- **No hardcoded secrets found anywhere** across all 588 files read, and — new in this revision — **no secret files (`.env`, `.pem`, credentials) were ever committed at any point in either repo's full git history**, confirmed via `git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only` across every commit, not just the current tree.

---

## 9. Gaps

This section is built primarily from the project's own `docs/GAPS.md` (written June 22, last touched July 22 — see below for exactly what that means) and `docs/GETSTREAM.md`, quoted in full where relevant, with each item explicitly marked as either **independently confirmed still true**, **independently confirmed now fixed**, or **not re-verified in this pass** — so nothing here is presented as current status without saying which of those three it is.

`docs/GAPS.md` is dated "June 2026" and was created in commit `562964a` (June 22), then touched once more in `dbe5c03` (July 22) — but that later commit's own message says it only "document[ed] framework-bundled audit highs," not a full re-audit. So the file's content mostly reflects June 22, four weeks and dozens of commits before the project stopped.

**Items independently confirmed to be FIXED since this doc was written** (i.e., the doc is stale on these specific points):
- *"Field-level encryption for PHI — patient phone, allergies, insurance stored in plaintext SQLite"* — **fixed**; `lib/phi.ts` encrypts these fields in the current code (§8).
- *"Turso token rotation — tokens created with `expiration: never`; no rotation strategy"* — **fixed**; current code has 90-day TTL with proactive rotation (confirmed while reading `src/lib`).
- *"M-Pesa / Stripe — payment integrations not implemented"* — **fixed**; PayHero M-Pesa billing was added June 25, three days after this doc was written.

**Items not independently re-verified in this pass — quoted as-is, status unknown:**
- Email verification column exists but unused; anyone can register with any email.
- No password-reset flow.
- `audit_logs` table exists but nothing writes to it.
- Offline-first PWA advertised but `idb`/Serwist not implemented.
- Onboarding race condition on concurrent submits.
- No orphaned-tenant-DB rollback if metadata insert fails after Turso DB creation.
- Deactivated users keep a valid session for up to 7 days (no token blocklist).
- No explicit CSRF/origin checks beyond Next.js defaults.
- *"Preview env separation — Vercel preview deployments may share production Turso keys"* — unresolved per the doc; not independently checked against current Vercel project settings in this pass.
- Inventory/POS/Prescriptions/Patients/Settings: several noted as missing edit flows, receipt printing, shift management, dispense/verify workflow, branch CRUD, multi-branch enforcement (schema supports branches, but the doc says all actions use `.limit(1)` on the main branch — not re-checked).
- Dashboard KPI trend percentages (+12%, +5%) are hardcoded, not computed.
- PPB/KHPTA, ODPC, NHIF/SHA, KRA ETR compliance items — all noted as incomplete; §6.4 independently confirms the KRA/NHIF/PPB compliance *module* is stubbed, consistent with this.
- Plan selection at onboarding — `plans` table seeded but every signup defaults to `starter`.

**From `docs/GETSTREAM.md` (last updated July 1, more recent than `GAPS.md`):** Stream Chat is "Stage 0/1 (server token endpoint only)" and explicitly "not yet connected" to any UI — see §7.

**`solera0`-specific gaps, from `EXECUTIVE_REPORT.md`, cross-checked against code in this pass:**
- SMS/OTP send not implemented — **confirmed**: `request_otp` returns a hardcoded value, no SMS provider call anywhere in `common/views.py`.
- Search is runtime fan-out across tenant Turso DBs, not a search index — **not independently re-verified in this pass** (marketplace search view code was read but its production performance under load wasn't tested).
- Accept/reject + auto-refund order flow — **confirmed not wired**: the `Refund` model exists in `payments/models.py` but `payhero_callback` (§4.2) never references it.
- PPB (online-pharmacy licensing) and ODPC (data protection) regulatory clearance — stated as an open blocker in the source due-diligence docs; outside what a code audit can resolve either way.

---

## 10. The data that actually exists right now

Queried directly against the live `solera-metadata` Turso database:

| Table | Row count |
|---|---|
| `tenants` | 3 |
| `global_users` | 11 |
| `subscriptions` | 1 |
| `audit_logs` | 76 |

```
ID                     NAME              SLUG               PLAN          STATUS
NsPEbkupFP4w...        Wanjiku Pharmacy  wanjiku-pharmacy   professional  suspended
W7rLJ6c36bE1...        Mwangi Pharmacy   mwangi-pharmacy    starter       trial
Ixu83bKwoFFy...        Muritu Pharmacy   muritu-pharmacy    professional  active
```

Not assumed either way: whether these are real early pilot customers or your own test tenants (the "Muritu" name plausibly matches your own, but that's not confirmation). Worth confirming directly, since it changes how urgently §4's findings should be treated.

The `db_token_encrypted` column was checked directly and contains genuine `iv:tag:ciphertext`-format ciphertext, not plaintext tokens — the encryption-at-rest claim is real, independently confirmed against live data, not just documented in code.

**Cruft, confirmed and traced to its source:** 20 Turso databases named `solera-e2e-*` / `solera-e2e-pharmacy-*`, timestamped from the repo's creation day onward, confirmed in §9 to originate from `scripts/e2e-test.ts` — an automated test script that creates a fresh Turso database per run and never tears it down.

---

## 11. Live deployment status

| | `solera` (`solerasite.vercel.app`) | `solera0` frontend (`solerao.vercel.app`) |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP status | 200 | 200 |
| Vercel-detected framework | Next.js | **"Other"** — not auto-detected, consistent with a repo root that now mixes a Next.js app with a Python `backend/` directory |
| Backend | N/A (self-contained) | **No live host.** No evidence a Render service was ever created from `render.yaml`; confirmed no reachable `/api/*` Django route from the live frontend |

Both frontends render (200 OK), but `solera0`'s marketplace pages have no working backend behind them right now, for the three independent reasons given in §3.

---

## 12. What this audit did not cover

- Did not run either repo's test suite locally (only confirmed, by reading `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, whether CI runs it — for `solera`, it does not).
- Did not independently verify every item in `docs/GAPS.md` marked "not re-verified" above — each is quoted from the source document, not re-derived from code, and flagged as such.
- Did not verify the business/market research claims in `EXECUTIVE_REPORT.md` and `research/` (MYDAWA/Zendawa comparisons, PPB licensing timeline, revenue projections) — those are business claims, not code, and outside what a repository audit can confirm.
- Did not test actual runtime behavior under load (e.g., whether the marketplace fan-out search would perform acceptably against many tenant databases).
- Did not check the two unmerged branches (`cursor/update-ssot-readme-agentic-audit-2586`, `v0/solera-platform-report-fb9e12d0`) in full — their existence and non-merged status is confirmed (§2), their content was not read in this pass.

---

## 13. Bottom line

- **`solera` is real, live, and holds real (if small) tenant data.** Its core product logic is largely solid — real tenant isolation, real RBAC, real PHI encryption, real barcode generation, real rate limiting, no secrets ever leaked into git history. But it has one live, exploitable bug (§4.3) and a CI pipeline that would not have caught it, or would not catch a regression of it tomorrow.
- **`solera0`'s backend, exactly as committed, has no real authentication and no real payment verification.** This is worse than its own executive report disclosed, and would be true on day one of any deployment using what's already in the repo.
- **The two apps share a database, a payment account, and an encryption-key fallback by design**, and this is now confirmed as a live, working code path (§6.1), not just shared configuration — a compromise of either app is not contained to that app alone.
- **The Postgres/Turso contradiction across 6 files has an exact, dated origin**: a database decision made and reversed within a 6-minute window on July 25, where only the reversal's application code was updated — the deployment config and one settings docstring were not.
- **20 orphaned Turso test databases** should be cleaned up regardless of what you decide about the two repos.

If `solera` is genuinely live with real users right now, **§4.3 (the forgeable PayHero webhook fallback) is the one finding in this entire audit I'd treat as time-sensitive**, independent of any decision about `solera0`. Everything else here is context for a decision you haven't asked me to make yet — which repo to keep building, whether to merge them, or whether to shut one down. Happy to go deeper on any single finding, or help fix any of them, once you tell me what this is feeding into.

# Solera & Solera0 — Complete Repository, Deployment, Database & History Audit

**Date:** 2026-08-22
**Purpose of this revision:** the first version of this audit summarized findings without showing the evidence behind them, which meant it wasn't verifiable by anyone without access to the repos, the Vercel projects, or the Turso databases. This version is written to be **fully self-contained** — every finding is backed by an actual code excerpt, actual commit hash, or actual query result quoted inline, so a reader with none of those accounts can still follow the reasoning and check it against what's quoted here.

**Method:** Both repos were cloned in full (not just API-sampled) specifically to do proper `git log`/`git show` history forensics. All 588 non-binary source files across both repos were read in full (excludes ~400 screenshot/logo/icon binary files, which aren't meaningful to "read" as code). Live Vercel deployments were hit directly. Live Turso databases were queried directly. Nothing here is taken from either repo's own documentation (`EXECUTIVE_REPORT.md`, `README.md`, `GAPS.md`, etc.) without being independently checked against the actual code — where a document's claim couldn't be independently re-verified in this pass, that is stated explicitly rather than assumed either way.

---

## Table of contents

1. [What these two repos are, in one paragraph each](#1-what-these-two-repos-are)
2. [How the project actually evolved — from real commit history](#2-how-the-project-actually-evolved)
3. [How the system works, end to end](#3-how-the-system-works-end-to-end)

---

## 1. What these two repos are

**`solera`** (`github.com/ken-muritu/solera`, private, created 2026-06-21) is a real, actively-developed, currently-live multi-tenant SaaS for pharmacies and clinics in Kenya. One Next.js 16 app, one Turso (SQLite-over-HTTP) database per tenant pharmacy plus one shared metadata database, Drizzle as the ORM. It has a real dashboard (POS, inventory, prescriptions, patients, clinic visits, billing, team messaging, reports), real M-Pesa payment integration via PayHero, and real (if small) paying-adjacent tenant data in it today. 74 commits, June 21 – July 23, 2026.

**`solera0`** (`github.com/ken-muritu/solera0`, private, created 2026-07-25) is a one-day, 15-commit exploration built four weeks later, in a single ~7-hour session. It started by copying `solera`'s entire Next.js frontend verbatim, then bolted on a brand-new Django backend meant to add a consumer-facing marketplace (search pharmacy stock, order, pay, pick up) on top of the pharmacies already running `solera`. It explicitly reuses `solera`'s Turso instance and PayHero account rather than standing up separate infrastructure.

They are not two versions of the same app. They are two different products, built a month apart, sharing a database, a payment account, and (per config) an encryption key.

---

## 2. How the project actually evolved

This section is built directly from `git log --shortstat` and `git show` on both repos' full histories (74 + 15 = 89 commits), not from either repo's own README narrative.

### `solera`: June 21 – July 23, 2026

**June 21, 20:54 — Genesis.** The very first commit, `34c6387`, is not a small scaffold — it's **53 files, 12,984 lines**, a full working MVP in one commit: multi-tenant schema, dashboard, POS, auth. This is consistent with AI-assisted rapid bootstrapping, not incremental hand-written development.

**June 22 — the single most intense day of the project.** Eighteen commits in one day, including, in order: brand icons, then `562964a` **"Harden Solera against vibe-coded security gaps"** (self-aware early security pass — the developer/agent explicitly recognized and addressed AI-generated security weaknesses before the product was a day old), then `fb2314c` "Ship production-ready MVP: security hardening, offline PWA, and full module workflows" (50 files, 5,161 lines), then a full RBAC/invites/offline-sync/M-Pesa/compliance wiring pass, a UI redesign pivot, dark mode, barcodes, and theme polish. By the end of June 22 the product had its full module shape.

**June 25–26 — payments and messaging.** `54098c5` adds Brevo email + PayHero billing (June 25). June 26 alone adds team invites, RBAC hardening, admin controls, profile management, and — significantly — **two separate commits fixing the same M-Pesa bug**: `968c53f` "Fix false M-Pesa payment success when PIN is not entered" and `11e5685` "Fix M-Pesa payment flow to wait for confirmation." The same day also ships a full team-messaging system (`ae29062`, `949bd1f` — 20 and 29 files, SSE-based chat, tickets, presence, read receipts) — this is the **real, currently-used** messaging system, distinct from the Stream Chat integration added later (see §9).

**June 27 — the day the critical webhook bug was introduced.** Commit `640608e`, "Fix marketing dark theme and simplify PayHero callback auth," changed `verifyPayHeroCallback()` from a strict secret-header-only check to also accept a `?secret=` query parameter. At this point the function was still fully secure — every path still required the real secret.

**July 1 — the bug becomes exploitable.** Commit `12c9579`, **"Accept PayHero callback payloads without echoed secret query param,"** co-authored with Cursor's AI agent, added a *third* fallback path. Its own commit message explains why: *"Pay Hero POSTs payment results without returning custom callback secrets, which caused 401s and blocked MAKA donation confirmations."* This was fixing a real problem — legitimate webhooks were being rejected — but the fix removed verification entirely for that path instead of fixing the verification method. See §4 for the exact code and exact exploit.

**July 1, same day — cross-product coupling.** `6e1becd`, "Forward MAKA-* PayHero callbacks to Makao," wires the same webhook to proxy matching requests to a *third*, unrelated product (`makaosite.vercel.app`).

**July 14 — a two-week gap, then a full README rewrite.** `2ef9fe3` replaces nearly the entire README (1,002 insertions, 792 deletions) with what becomes the "comprehensive executive platform handbook" framing.

**July 22 — a second active day, one week before `solera0` began.** Vendo (an AI-agent framework) is installed (`c896733`, 5,042 lines), lockfile issues are fixed, and `docs/GAPS.md` gets a small addition (see §9). Notably, this is also the day two *unmerged* branches split off: a Cursor-agent-authored README update (`cursor/update-ssot-readme-agentic-audit-2586`) and a v0.dev-authored platform report (`v0/solera-platform-report-fb9e12d0`) — both still exist on GitHub today, neither is part of `main`, and neither was checked by the original in-repo `EXECUTIVE_REPORT.md`.

**July 23 — screenshots.** The final two commits add 156 PNG files (light + dark mode screenshot libraries), no code.

**Commit identity note:** across the 74 commits, five distinct git identities appear: `Ken.M`/`ken-muritu` (same email, `kenhopkins.ke@gmail.com`), `muritu <muritu@inkboxmail.com>` (5 commits, all July 22, same body of work as the rest of that day — very likely the same person on a different machine/git config, though this can't be confirmed from git metadata alone), `Cursor Agent <cursoragent@cursor.com>`, and `v0 <it+v0agent@vercel.com>` — both AI tools committing directly to the repository, not just assisting a human committer.

### `solera0`: July 25, 2026, 15:59–22:54 (one session, ~7 hours)

| Time | Commit | What happened |
|---|---|---|
| 15:59 | `77fd6d1` | **527 files, 85,728 lines** — the entire `solera` frontend cloned in as the starting point, plus a new Django `backend/` |
| 16:18 | `15cf1da` | Due-diligence + Render runbook added |
| 16:31–17:39 | 5 commits | A real, visible struggle to get the Vercel build working: remove hooks causing hangs, fix `next.config.ts`, fix `vercel.json` twice, add webpack aliases |
| 17:27 | `6e868eb` | **"Frontend rewire (Interpretation B): consumer marketplace surface + Django API client"** — the "(Interpretation B)" phrasing indicates an AI agent resolving ambiguity in its own instructions and choosing one interpretation over another |
| 18:08 | `f051a71` | Dark mode stripped out; light-theme only |

## 3. How the system works, end to end

### `solera` — real architecture, confirmed by reading the code

```
solera/
├── src/app/(app)/        ← authenticated pharmacy dashboard: pos, inventory,
│                            prescriptions, patients, clinic, reports, settings,
│                            admin, messages, account
├── src/app/(auth)/       ← login, signup, forgot/reset password, verify-email,
│                            accept-invite
├── src/app/api/          ← auth[nextauth], payhero/callback, mpesa/callback,
│                            payments/status, messages/*, admin/tenants, sync,
│                            vendo/[...vendo]
├── src/components/       ← pos, dashboard, messages, settings, admin, auth, ui
├── src/lib/               ← billing, payments, compliance, offline, sync,
│                            messages, stream, phi.ts (encryption), crypto.ts,
│                            rate-limit.ts, actions/*
├── src/db/schema/         ← Drizzle schema: metadata DB + per-tenant DB
└── src/vendo/registry.tsx ← AI-agent tool registry (installed, empty — see §9)
```

**Data model:** one Turso database (`solera-metadata`) holds the platform registry — `tenants`, `global_users`, `subscriptions`, `plans`, `audit_logs`, etc. Each pharmacy tenant gets its **own separate Turso database** (`solera-<slug>-<id>`), holding its actual inventory, sales, patients, prescriptions. The metadata DB's `tenants` table stores each tenant's DB URL and an **AES-256-GCM-encrypted** access token for that tenant's own database — confirmed by directly querying the live table (§10) and reading the actual ciphertext format.

**Payments:** PayHero (an M-Pesa payment gateway for Kenya) posts webhooks to `/api/payhero/callback`, verified (with the flaw documented in §4) by `src/lib/payhero-webhook.ts`, then processed by `src/lib/payments/confirm-sale.ts` or `src/lib/billing/payhero.ts` depending on whether it's a POS sale or a subscription payment.

**Messaging:** a real, custom-built system — SSE streaming (`api/messages/stream`), presence, typing indicators, WhatsApp-style read receipts, tickets — is the one actually wired into the UI (`messages-client.tsx`). A second messaging integration, Stream Chat, is installed as a dependency with a working, RBAC-checked token endpoint, but per the project's own `docs/GETSTREAM.md`, was never connected to any UI (§9).

### `solera0` — what was actually built, and what it can't currently do

```
solera0/
├── src/app/(app)/, (auth)/, api/   ← byte-identical copy of solera's — see §5, finding 8
├── src/app/marketplace/            ← NEW: consumer search/order/checkout UI
├── src/app/for-pharmacies/         ← NEW: pharmacy self-onboarding form
├── src/lib/api.ts                  ← NEW: real API client calling the Django backend
├── backend/
│   ├── common/       ← OTP auth, AES crypto, Turso tenancy helpers, inventory reader
│   ├── pharmacies/   ← Plan, Pharmacy, PharmacyApplication, onboarding
│   ├── marketplace/  ← search service — views written, URL never wired (§5)
│   ├── consumer/     ← ConsumerUser, ConsumerOrder, place/list/detail endpoints
│   └── payments/     ← PayHero webhook handler — no signature check (§4)
├── render.yaml        ← stale since commit #1 (§2) — provisions Postgres the code can't use
├── RENDER_SETUP.md    ← tells you to deploy the Postgres way (wrong, per code)
└── DEPLOY_TURSO.md    ← tells you to deploy the Turso way (matches the code)
```

**What actually happens right now if you visit `solerao.vercel.app/marketplace` and search:** the frontend calls `getSolera0Api()` (`src/lib/env.ts`), which reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_SOLERA0_API` — unset, since the backend has never been deployed — and falls back to `http://localhost:8000`, baked into the production JavaScript bundle at build time. The fetch fails. Even if a real backend URL were set, `next.config.ts`'s Content-Security-Policy `connect-src` doesn't whitelist any external host for it, so the browser would block the request regardless. And even if both of those were fixed and the backend deployed with the current `render.yaml`, the search endpoint itself has no URL registered (`backend/marketplace/urls.py` is `urlpatterns = []`) — three independent, unrelated failure points, not one.

## 4. Findings — Critical

### 4.1 `solera0` backend: authentication is fully bypassable, in every environment

`backend/common/views.py`, current code, in full:

```python
def request_otp(request):
    """Request SMS OTP. Placeholder: integrate Africa's Talking / Brevo SMS.
    Returns a fake otp in dev for testing; real impl sends SMS."""
    body = json.loads(request.body or "{}")
    phone = body.get("phone")
    if not phone:
        return JsonResponse({"error": "phone required"}, status=400)
    # TODO: generate + store OTP (cache/redis), send via SMS provider
    return JsonResponse({"sent": True, "dev_otp": "111111"})


@csrf_exempt
@require_POST
def verify_otp(request):
    """Verify OTP -> issue JWT (staff vs consumer determined by `role`)."""
    body = json.loads(request.body or "{}")
    phone = body.get("phone")
    otp = body.get("otp")
    role = body.get("role", "consumer")  # 'staff' or 'consumer'
    if not (phone and otp):
        return JsonResponse({"error": "phone and otp required"}, status=400)
    # TODO: validate OTP; for now accept dev_otp
    if otp != "111111":
        return JsonResponse({"error": "invalid otp"}, status=401)
    from rest_framework_simplejwt.tokens import RefreshToken
    user, _ = _get_or_create_user(phone, role)
    refresh = RefreshToken.for_user(user)
    return JsonResponse({"access": str(refresh.access_token), "refresh": str(refresh)})
```

There is no environment check anywhere in this function. `otp != "111111"` is the entire verification, in production exactly as in dev, and `role` is caller-supplied — `{"phone": "anything", "otp": "111111", "role": "staff"}` mints a real staff-level JWT. Separately, `backend/consumer/views.py`'s phone-auth fallback treats an unverified `Authorization: Bearer <x>` header's value as the phone number directly, with no JWT decoding at all.

### 4.2 `solera0` backend: the payment webhook checks nothing

`backend/payments/views.py`, current code, in full:

```python
def payhero_callback(request):
    """PayHero posts the payment result here. Mark order paid, set OTP, push to pharmacy Turso."""
    body = json.loads(request.body or "{}")
    order_id = body.get("external_reference") or body.get("reference")
    status = (body.get("status") or "").lower()
    order = ConsumerOrder.objects.filter(id=order_id).first()
    if order and status == "success":
        order.payment_status = "paid"
        order.payment_ref = body.get("transaction_id", "")
        order.status = "confirmed"
        order.otp = _make_otp()
        order.updated_at = _now()
        order.save()
        try:
            from common.tenant_writer import push_consumer_order_to_turso
            push_consumer_order_to_turso(order)
        except Exception:
            pass
    return JsonResponse({"received": True})
```

`PAYHERO_CALLBACK_SECRET` is a defined environment variable (`backend/.env.example`) but is **never referenced anywhere in this file, or anywhere in `backend/`** (confirmed by search). Anyone who submits or guesses an `order_id` can POST `{"external_reference": "<id>", "status": "success"}` directly and receive a real, valid pickup OTP for an order nobody paid for.

### 4.3 `solera` (the live product): the payment webhook's fallback is forgeable

Current `src/lib/payhero-webhook.ts`:

```typescript
export function isPayHeroCallbackPayload(body: Record<string, unknown>): boolean {
  const response = (body.response ?? body) as Record<string, unknown>;
  return !!(
    response.ExternalReference ??
    response.external_reference ??
    response.CheckoutRequestID ??
    response.checkout_request_id
  );
}

export function verifyPayHeroCallback(
  req: Request,
  options?: { body?: Record<string, unknown> },
): boolean {
  const secret = process.env.PAYHERO_CALLBACK_SECRET;
  if (!secret) return process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production";

  const headerToken = /* ...reads x-payhero-signature / x-callback-secret / authorization... */ null;
  if (secretsMatch(headerToken, secret)) return true;

  const queryToken = new URL(req.url).searchParams.get("secret");
  if (secretsMatch(queryToken, secret)) return true;

  if (options?.body && isPayHeroCallbackPayload(options.body)) return true;  // <- no secret checked here at all

  return false;
}
```

If the header check and the query-secret check both fail, `isPayHeroCallbackPayload()` accepts the request purely because the body has the *shape* of a real PayHero payload — no secret, no signature. Sale references are constructed as `SALE-<tenantId.slice(0,8)>-<receiptNumber>` (`src/lib/payments/reference.ts`) — an 8-character tenant-ID prefix and a receipt number, both discoverable. `src/lib/payhero-webhook.test.ts` exists and covers `verifyPayHeroCallback`, but calls it with a different argument signature than the real call site (`src/app/api/payhero/callback/route.ts`) uses — so this path has never actually been exercised by the test. This is compounded by:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml — runs lint, build, npm audit — never `npm test`
```

The 5-file test suite (RBAC, this webhook, PayHero status, receipt status, theme utils) has never run in CI, confirmed by reading the workflow file directly — there is no `npm test` (or equivalent) step anywhere in it.

**Why all three matter together:** `solera` is live with real tenant data today (§10). `solera0`'s backend has never been deployed — but if it ever is, using exactly what's already committed to the repo, both its authentication and its payments are trivially bypassable from day one, against the same shared database and PayHero account solera's real tenants use.

## 5. Findings — High

**5.1 — Two contradictory deployment runbooks in `solera0`, only one matches the code.** `RENDER_SETUP.md` instructs `render blueprint launch render.yaml` (provisions Postgres). `DEPLOY_TURSO.md` states explicitly: *"There is NO separate Postgres/Neon database."* Neither document references or supersedes the other. Only the Turso path matches what `backend/solera0/settings/base.py`'s `_parse_db_url()` can parse — it recognizes `libsql://` and `sqlite`, and anything else (including `postgres://`) silently falls through to an ephemeral SQLite fallback:

```python
def _parse_db_url(url):
    if not url:
        return {"ENGINE": "django.db.backends.sqlite3", "NAME": str(BASE_DIR / "solera0_platform.sqlite3")}
    if url.startswith("sqlite"):
        path = url.replace("sqlite:///", "").replace("sqlite://", "")
        return {"ENGINE": "django.db.backends.sqlite3", "NAME": path or str(BASE_DIR / "solera0_platform.sqlite3")}
    if url.startswith("libsql"):
        return {"ENGINE": "django_libsql", "NAME": url}
    return {"ENGINE": "django.db.backends.sqlite3", "NAME": str(BASE_DIR / "solera0_platform.sqlite3")}  # <- postgres:// lands here
```

`render.yaml` (unchanged since the very first commit, per §2) wires `DATABASE_URL` to a real, Render-provisioned Postgres connection string via `fromDatabase`. Following `RENDER_SETUP.md` as written means the Django platform registry — pharmacies, consumer orders, applications — never actually persists anything: SQLite on Render's web tier doesn't survive a redeploy or restart.

**5.2 — CORS misconfigured for the real deployed domain.** `render.yaml`: `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS: "https://solera0.vercel.app"` (digit zero). The real, live site — confirmed via `vercel project inspect` and a live HTTP 200 — is `https://solerao.vercel.app` (letter "o"). Different domains; the real frontend would be CORS-blocked.

**5.3 — Marketplace search is unreachable even on a deployed backend.** `backend/marketplace/urls.py`, in full:

```python
"""marketplace API routes (stub)."""
from django.urls import path
urlpatterns = []  # TODO: wire views
```

The `search()` view exists, fully written, in `views.py` — it's simply never mounted to a URL. This is the backend-side confirmation of the same conclusion reached from the frontend side in §3: the "code-complete core commerce loop" claimed in `EXECUTIVE_REPORT.md` is not reachable end-to-end, for independent reasons on both sides of the stack.

**5.4 — `solera`'s CI never runs its own test suite** (see 4.3). This is a standing process gap beyond the one bug it already let through — any future regression across RBAC, payments, or receipts would also go uncaught.

**6.3 — A function called two incompatible ways.** `backend/common/tenancy.py`:
```python

```
`backend/common/tenant_writer.py`:

Same imported function (`libsql_client.create_client_sync`), two different calling conventions. At least one of these would raise `TypeError` if actually executed against the real library's signature.

**6.5 — Schema/write-path split, resolved not left open.** `EXECUTIVE_REPORT.md` describes orders being written to an `online_orders` table in the pharmacy's Turso DB, but no such table exists in the Next.js app's Drizzle schema. Confirmed resolution: `backend/common/tenant_writer.py` creates and writes it directly via raw parameterized SQL (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS online_orders (...)`, `INSERT OR REPLACE ... VALUES (?, ?, ...)`) — Django writes to the tenant DB outside Drizzle's management entirely, which is architecturally consistent (two codebases, two DB clients, one database), not a bug. If the two apps ever resolve this fallback differently in their real deployed env vars, a tenant token encrypted by one would fail to decrypt under the other.

## 8. Confirmed genuinely solid

This audit is not only a bug list — these were independently checked against the code, not taken on faith:

- **Tenant isolation** — every route checked derives tenant context strictly from server-side session/membership lookups; nothing trusts a client-supplied tenant ID.
- **POS checkout** sends only `{productId, quantity}` to the server; price is computed and validated server-side — confirmed by what's *not* sent over the wire.
- **M-Pesa status polling** is server-verified, consistent with the two "fix false M-Pesa success" commits from June 26 — the current code reflects the fixed version.
- **PHI (patient data) encryption** (`lib/phi.ts`) is consistently applied everywhere patient records are read or written — this directly *supersedes* `docs/GAPS.md` item 12, which still describes PHI as plaintext (§9).
- **Barcode generation** (`BarcodeDisplay` + `jsbarcode`) produces real EAN13/CODE128 barcodes from real SKU data — not a placeholder.
- **Rate limiting** (`src/lib/rate-limit.ts`) is a real server-side, Turso-backed sliding-window limiter.
- **RBAC matrix and its tests** are correct, and match what was traced through actual call sites.
- **AES-256-GCM crypto**, both repos — fresh IV per call (`os.urandom(12)` / equivalent), proper tag handling, no key reuse or ECB mode.
- **No hardcoded secrets found anywhere** across all 588 files read, and — new in this revision — **no secret files (`.env`, `.pem`, credentials) were ever committed at any point in either repo's full git history**, confirmed via `git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only` across every commit, not just the current tree.

## 13. Bottom line

- **`solera` is real, live, and holds real (if small) tenant data.** Its core product logic is largely solid — real tenant isolation, real RBAC, real PHI encryption, real barcode generation, real rate limiting, no secrets ever leaked into git history. But it has one live, exploitable bug (§4.3) and a CI pipeline that would not have caught it, or would not catch a regression of it tomorrow.
- **`solera0`'s backend, exactly as committed, has no real authentication and no real payment verification.** This is worse than its own executive report disclosed, and would be true on day one of any deployment using what's already in the repo.
- **The two apps share a database, a payment account, and an encryption-key fallback by design**, and this is now confirmed as a live, working code path (§6.1), not just shared configuration — a compromise of either app is not contained to that app alone.
- **The Postgres/Turso contradiction across 6 files has an exact, dated origin**: a database decision made and reversed within a 6-minute window on July 25, where only the reversal's application code was updated — the deployment config and one settings docstring were not.
- **20 orphaned Turso test databases** should be cleaned up regardless of what you decide about the two repos.

If `solera` is genuinely live with real users right now, **§4.3 (the forgeable PayHero webhook fallback) is the one finding in this entire audit I'd treat as time-sensitive**, independent of any decision about `solera0`. Everything else here is context for a decision you haven't asked me to make yet — which repo to keep building, whether to merge them, or whether to shut one down. Happy to go deeper on any single finding, or help fix any of them, once you tell me what this is feeding into.

-**1. `solera0` backend: authentication is fully bypassable, in every environment — not a dev-only shortcut.**

-`backend/common/views.py:verify_otp` — the entire check is `if otp != "111111": reject`. There is no environment gate; this is the *only* OTP path that exists anywhere in the code, and it can mint **staff-role** JWTs, not just consumer ones. Separately, `backend/consumer/views.py`'s `_auth_phone` trusts the `x-consumer-phone` header with no signature check at all, and its "Bearer token" fallback doesn't decode or verify a JWT — it uses whatever string follows `Bearer ` **as the phone number itself**. Anyone who guesses a phone number can read another customer's order history and their pickup OTP. `EXECUTIVE_REPORT.md`'s "auth JWT (or dev header)" framing significantly undersells this: there is no real verification path, dev or production.
-**2. `solera0` backend: the PayHero payment webhook has zero signature verification.**

-`backend/payments/views.py:payhero_callback` reads `status`/`order_id`/`transaction_id` straight from the POST body. `PAYHERO_CALLBACK_SECRET` is defined as an env var but **is never referenced anywhere in this function**. Anyone who can guess or observe an order ID can POST a fake "paid" callback and get a real pickup OTP issued for an order nobody paid for. This is not mentioned anywhere in `EXECUTIVE_REPORT.md`.

+**`solera`** (`github.com/ken-muritu/solera`, private, created 2026-06-21) is a real, actively-developed, currently-live multi-tenant SaaS for pharmacies and clinics in Kenya. One Next.js 16 app, one Turso (SQLite-over-HTTP) database per tenant pharmacy plus one shared metadata database, Drizzle as the ORM. It has a real dashboard (POS, inventory, prescriptions, patients, clinic visits, billing, team messaging, reports), real M-Pesa payment integration via PayHero, and real (if small) paying-adjacent tenant data in it today. 74 commits, June 21 – July 23, 2026.
-**3. `solera` (the live product): the PayHero webhook's fallback verification is forgeable.**

-`src/lib/payhero-webhook.ts`'s `verifyPayHeroCallback()` — when the shared-secret check fails, it falls through to `isPayHeroCallbackPayload(body)`, which only checks the POST body *has* the expected fields, not that they're authentic. Sale references are low-entropy and guessable (`SALE-<tenantId.slice(0,8)>-<receiptNumber>`). The one test covering this path calls the function with a different signature than the real endpoint uses, so the bug has never been caught — and confirmed separately: **CI runs lint, build, and `npm audit`, but never runs `npm test` at all**, so the existing test suite (5 real test files) has never executed in CI, full stop. This webhook also forwards any `MAKA-`-prefixed reference, auth headers included, straight through to a third product (`makaosite.vercel.app`) — the blast radius isn't contained to solera either.

+**`solera0`** (`github.com/ken-muritu/solera0`, private, created 2026-07-25) is a one-day, 15-commit exploration built four weeks later, in a single ~7-hour session. It started by copying `solera`'s entire Next.js frontend verbatim, then bolted on a brand-new Django backend meant to add a consumer-facing marketplace (search pharmacy stock, order, pay, pick up) on top of the pharmacies already running `solera`. It explicitly reuses `solera`'s Turso instance and PayHero account rather than standing up separate infrastructure.

-**Why #1–#3 matter together:** `solera` is live with real tenant data (3 tenants, 11 users, confirmed in Part 1 §5). `solera0`'s backend has never been deployed (Part 1 §6) — but if it ever is, using the exact env-var defaults and Render config already committed to the repo, both its auth and its payments are trivially bypassable on day one, against the *same* shared Turso database and PayHero account solera's real tenants use.
+They are not two versions of the same app. They are two different products, built a month apart, sharing a database, a payment account, and (per config) an encryption key.

+## 3. How the system works, end to end
-- **Tenant isolation in `solera`** is real: every route checked derives tenant context strictly from server-side session/membership lookups; nothing trusts a client-supplied tenant ID.
-- **POS checkout** sends only `{productId, quantity}` to the server — price is computed server-side; confirmed by what's *not* sent over the wire, not by trusting a comment.
-- **M-Pesa payment status** is polled via a server-verified endpoint, consistent with two historical "fix false M-Pesa success" commits — the current code reflects the fixed version.
-- **PHI encryption** (`phi.ts`) is consistently applied everywhere patient records are read or written.

-- **Barcode generation** (`BarcodeDisplay` + `jsbarcode`) produces genuinely real EAN13/CODE128 barcodes from real data — not a placeholder (worth naming explicitly since a different product in this same account, per the CaspaHub audit, was found to have a fake QR code).
-- **Rate limiting** (`src/lib/rate-limit.ts`) is a real server-side, Turso-backed sliding-window limiter, not client-tamperable.
-- **RBAC matrix and its tests** are correct and match what was traced through actual call sites.
-- **AES-256-GCM crypto** (both repos' `crypto.py`/`crypto.ts`) is implemented correctly — fresh IV per call, proper tag handling, no key reuse or ECB mode.
-- **No hardcoded secrets found anywhere** across all 588 files read, in either repo.

"""Pharmacy registry models (Solera.0 platform/Postgres layer).

These mirror Solera's `tenants` (metadata DB) and the proposed `consumer_settings` /
`pharmacy_directory` tables from the consumer-marketplace DD (v2.0, §4.2/§4.3).
The operational pharmacy data (products, inventory_batches, sales, prescriptions) stays in
each pharmacy's own Turso DB, accessed via common.tenancy — faithful to Solera's
database-per-tenant model.
"""
from django.db import models


class Plan(models.Model):
    """Mirrors Solera metadata.plans."""
    name = models.CharField(max_length=80)
    description = models.TextField(blank=True)
    price_kes_monthly = models.IntegerField(null=True, blank=True)
    price_usd_monthly = models.IntegerField(null=True, blank=True)
    max_branches = models.IntegerField(default=1)
    max_users = models.IntegerField(default=5)
    features = models.JSONField(default=dict)

    def __str__(self):
        return self.name


class Pharmacy(models.Model):
    """Registry row per Solera tenant. Holds the encrypted Turso token so Solera.0
    can open that pharmacy's operational DB (read inventory / write consumer orders)."""
    tenant_id = models.CharField(max_length=64, unique=True)
    name = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    slug = models.SlugField(max_length=120, unique=True)
    # encrypted Turso credentials (AES-256-GCM, shares Solera ENCRYPTION_KEY)
    turso_db_url = models.TextField()
    db_token_encrypted = models.TextField()
    plan = models.ForeignKey(Plan, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True, blank=True)
    status = models.CharField(max_length=20, default="active")
    created_at = models.BigIntegerField()

    def __str__(self):
        return f"{self.name} ({self.slug})"


class PharmacyDirectory(models.Model):
    """Public directory of opted-in pharmacies (DD §4.3 pharmacy_directory)."""
    pharmacy = models.OneToOneField(Pharmacy, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    display_name = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    address = models.TextField(blank=True)
    lat = models.FloatField(null=True, blank=True)
    lng = models.FloatField(null=True, blank=True)
    city = models.CharField(max_length=100, blank=True)
    county = models.CharField(max_length=100, blank=True)
    is_verified = models.BooleanField(default=False)   # PPB licence check before public
    is_active = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    created_at = models.BigIntegerField()

    def __str__(self):
        return self.display_name


class ConsumerSettings(models.Model):
    """Per-pharmacy storefront config (DD §4.2 consumer_settings). Default PRIVATE/safe."""
    pharmacy = models.OneToOneField(Pharmacy, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    is_public = models.BooleanField(default=False)     # opt-in, default private
    display_name = models.CharField(max_length=200, blank=True)
    address = models.TextField(blank=True)
    lat = models.FloatField(null=True, blank=True)
    lng = models.FloatField(null=True, blank=True)
    phone = models.CharField(max_length=20, blank=True)
    operating_hours = models.JSONField(default=dict, blank=True)
    pickup_enabled = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    delivery_enabled = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    min_order_amount = models.IntegerField(default=0)
    created_at = models.BigIntegerField()
    updated_at = models.BigIntegerField()


class PharmacyApplication(models.Model):
    """Self-serve 'List my pharmacy' request (DD §4.3 onboarding + PPB gating).

    Status flow: pending -> approved (creates Pharmacy + PharmacyDirectory + ConsumerSettings,
    defaults PRIVATE until the pharmacy opts into the public storefront) or rejected.
    PPB licence is captured but verification is a manual admin step before public listing.
    """
    STATUS = [("pending", "pending"), ("approved", "approved"), ("rejected", "rejected")]
    name = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    contact_phone = models.CharField(max_length=20)
    contact_email = models.CharField(max_length=200, blank=True)
    city = models.CharField(max_length=100)
    county = models.CharField(max_length=100, blank=True)
    address = models.TextField(blank=True)
    ppb_license = models.CharField(max_length=100, blank=True, help_text="PPB licence number (verified before public listing)")
    is_verified = models.BooleanField(default=False)  # PPB licence checked
    status = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=STATUS, default="pending")
    notes = models.TextField(blank=True)
    created_at = models.BigIntegerField()
    reviewed_at = models.BigIntegerField(null=True, blank=True)

    def __str__(self):
        return f"{self.name} ({self.status})"

content.text:
Confirmed directly from the code — it's not a bug or oversight in the connection, there's **no connection built at all**. Here's exactly why, in order:

**1. There's no link between solera's `tenants` table and solera0's `Pharmacy` model.** Look at the model:

```python
class Pharmacy(models.Model):
    tenant_id = models.CharField(max_length=64, unique=True)  # <- plain text field, not a foreign key
    turso_db_url = models.TextField()
    db_token_encrypted = models.TextField()
```

`tenant_id` is just a free-text string field. Nothing anywhere in the codebase reads solera's real `tenants` table and creates matching `Pharmacy` rows automatically. The only way a `Pharmacy` row is ever created is through a fully manual, three-step human process:

1. Someone submits `POST /api/pharmacies/apply/` (a "list my pharmacy" form).
2. A platform admin manually calls `POST /api/pharmacies/applications/<id>/approve/` — and has to **type in the pharmacy's `turso_db_url` and `db_token_encrypted` by hand** in that request. There's no code that looks up an existing tenant's real credentials and fills this in for you.
3. Even after that, `ConsumerSettings.is_public` defaults to `False` — the pharmacy is created but stays private until someone flips that separately.

Wanjiku Pharmacy, Mwangi Pharmacy, and Muritu Pharmacy exist as real rows in solera's `tenants` table — but nobody ever ran this apply→approve flow for them, so **zero `Pharmacy` rows exist in solera0 for any of them.**

**2. Even if that had been done, there's nowhere for the data to live.** The Django backend has never been deployed (confirmed in the audit — no live Render host). So there's no live database anywhere holding a `Pharmacy` table right now, populated or not.

**3. Even if a pharmacy were approved and public, you couldn't find it.** `backend/marketplace/urls.py` is `urlpatterns = []` — the search feature has no URL wired to it at all.

So "why aren't they connected" has a precise answer: the connection was designed as a manual admin workflow, never built as an automatic sync, and never actually run for these three tenants — on top of the backend not being live at all.

If you want them actually connected, that's a real, buildable feature — not a fix to existing code, since none of this exists yet: (a) a script/endpoint that reads solera's `tenants` table directly and auto-creates matching `Pharmacy` + `ConsumerSettings` rows instead of requiring manual credential re-entry, (b) deploying the backend somewhere live, and (c) wiring the marketplace search URL. ## Database-Only Service

Turso is a database-only service, and you need a separate compute layer such as Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge Functions, or a traditional server for any application logic. This means Turso does not provide compute hosting or web services beyond database functionality.

## What Turso Actually Offers

Turso is a transactional, cloud database platform built on SQLite, serving developers and enterprises that need lightweight, high-density databases at the edge and in the cloud. The platform specializes in:

- A ground-up rewrite of SQLite in Rust, intended as a drop-in replacement, with capabilities that classical SQLite does not offer out of the box.
- Vector similarity search built into the database with no extensions required, making Turso a practical store for embeddings used in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and other AI workloads.
- Turso in the Browser ships SQLite as WebAssembly with OPFS persistence and SharedArrayBuffer performance, powering offline-first web apps with no server.

## Key Distinction from Full Platforms

Unlike full backend platforms like Firebase or Convex, Turso is a database layer, so choosing Turso means also choosing other services for functions, real-time, and auth.

**On Turso hosting — researched, not assumed: no, Turso cannot host Django (or any compute).** Turso is database-only — SQLite-over-HTTP, nothing else. It has no functions runtime, no compute layer; you always need a separate host (Render, Railway, Fly, etc.) for the actual Django process, with Turso only ever serving as its database. This isn't a limitation to work around — it's exactly how the existing code already assumes things work (`django-libsql` talking to Turso as the DB, with Django itself needing to run somewhere else). The actual fix is: stop provisioning Postgres in `render.yaml` (leftover from the abandoned 6-minute Neon detour) and deploy Django to Render using Turso as its only database, matching what `base.py` already supports natively.
