# Fix Solera + Solera0 bugs, and connect them

## Context

The audit (`~/Downloads/Solera & Solera0 - Repo, Deployment & Database Audit.md`) found a live, exploitable payment-webhook forgery bug in `solera` (which has real tenant data today), a fully bypassable auth system and an unverified payment webhook in `solera0`'s never-deployed backend, an architecture conflict (`render.yaml` still provisions Postgres though the code is Turso-only, traced to an abandoned decision made and reversed within 6 minutes on July 25 and never fully cleaned up), a CORS domain typo, an unwired search endpoint, and no actual connection between solera's real pharmacy tenants and solera0's marketplace directory — that connection is a fully manual admin workflow that was designed but never run for any of the 3 existing tenants.

Turso was researched directly (WebSearch, not assumed): it is database-only, no compute/hosting layer. Django still needs a real host (Render, as already scaffolded) — Turso only ever serves as its database, which `django-libsql`/`libsql_client` already support natively once `render.yaml` stops fighting that.

Decisions already confirmed with the user:
- This pass makes the code correct and deployment-ready. **No live Render deployment, no real production secrets provisioned** — that's a separate, deliberate step the user triggers later.
- `solera` fixes land as a **direct commit to `main`**, only after full local validation (install, type-check, test, build all green) — same rigor as the earlier CaspaHub cleanup, given this touches a live payment path.
- The new tenant→pharmacy sync creates rows **private by default** (`ConsumerSettings.is_public=False`) — matches the existing `approve()` flow's own default and the documented PPB-verification gate. Nothing becomes publicly searchable without an explicit follow-up action.

## Scope: what's fixed now vs. deferred

**Fixed in this pass** — every finding in the audit's Critical/High/Medium sections that is a genuine, verifiable code defect fixable through code alone, plus the tenant-sync connecting feature.

**Explicitly deferred, not attempted in this pass** — the broader feature backlog in `docs/GAPS.md` (password-reset flow, PWA offline support, NHIF/KRA/PPB compliance API integrations, real audit-log writes, multi-branch enforcement, dashboard KPI real computation, plan-selection UX, email verification enforcement). These are net-new features or third-party integrations requiring real accounts/credentials and product decisions, not bugs — bundling them into a security-fix pass risks doing all of it hastily. I'll list them back out as a clean follow-up backlog at the end of this work rather than touch them now.

---

## `solera` — fixes (commit directly to `main` after full local validation)

### 1. [Critical] PayHero webhook forgery — `src/lib/payhero-webhook.ts`
Root cause (confirmed via `git show 12c9579`): PayHero doesn't reliably echo back a secret, so `isPayHeroCallbackPayload()` was added as a fallback that accepts any correctly-shaped body with **no verification at all**.

Fix: instead of trusting the webhook body's `status` field when the secret checks fail, treat an unverified-but-shaped callback as a *trigger to independently re-check the transaction with PayHero's own authenticated status API* (using `PAYHERO_AUTH_TOKEN`, server-side only, never attacker-controlled) before marking anything paid. Solera already has this exact capability for client-side polling (`src/app/api/payments/status/route.ts`, and a `payhero-status` test file per the audit) — I'll locate and reuse that existing PayHero-status-check function rather than write a new one, wiring it into the webhook path as the source of truth when the shared-secret path can't confirm authenticity. If header/query secret verification succeeds, trust the webhook directly as today (fast path preserved); only the currently-forgeable fallback changes.

### 2. [High] CI never runs tests — `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
Add an `npm test` (or the project's actual test script name) step, so the 5 existing test files — including the payhero-webhook coverage — actually run on every push/PR, not just lint/build/audit.

### 3. [Medium] Fix the payhero-webhook test's signature mismatch
`payhero-webhook.test.ts` calls `verifyPayHeroCallback(req)` with one argument; the real call site passes `{ body }` as a second argument. Fix the test to call it the same way production does, so it actually exercises the path being fixed in #1.

### Validation before commit
`npm install && npx tsc --noEmit && npm test && npm run build` — all green, matching the CaspaHub precedent, before a single commit to `main`.

---

## `solera0` — backend fixes

### 4. [Critical] OTP auth fully bypassable — `backend/common/views.py`
Replace the hardcoded `"111111"` check with real OTP generation (random code, short expiry, stored server-side — cache or a small DB-backed model, not a bare constant) and real verification against the stored value. For actual delivery, wire Brevo SMS (`BREVO_API_KEY` is already a declared env var in `backend/.env.example`; Brevo supports SMS send via API) rather than leaving it a TODO. Keep a dev-only bypass *only* when `settings.DEBUG` is explicitly `True` — never unconditional.

Also fix `consumer/views.py`'s `_auth_phone`: stop treating an unverified `Authorization: Bearer <x>` value as a phone number directly — require and properly decode/verify a real JWT (SimpleJWT is already a dependency and already used by `verify_otp`'s issuance path).

### 5. [Critical] PayHero webhook has zero verification — `backend/payments/views.py`
Same root fix as solera's #1: use PayHero's own status-check API server-side to confirm a transaction before marking an order paid, rather than trusting the POST body. Keep both apps' webhook-verification logic consistent since they share one PayHero account.

### 6. [High] `render.yaml` still provisions Postgres; code can't use it
Rewrite `render.yaml`: remove the `databases:` block and the `DATABASE_URL: fromDatabase` wiring; set `TURSO_DATABASE_URL`/`TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN` as `sync: false` secrets instead, matching what `base.py`/`prod.py` already parse. Fix `backend/common/tenancy.py`'s docstring (currently claims "Render Postgres") to match the Turso-only reality already implemented in `base.py`/`prod.py`/`dev.py`/`requirements.txt`. Fix `backend/.env.example` to drop the contradictory `SOLERA0_DB_*`/`postgres://` example block.

Consolidate the two contradictory runbooks: `DEPLOY_TURSO.md` is already correct — keep it as the one deployment doc. Replace `RENDER_SETUP.md`'s content with a short note pointing to `DEPLOY_TURSO.md`, rather than leaving two documents that actively disagree.

### 7. [High] CORS domain typo — `render.yaml`
`CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS: "https://solera0.vercel.app"` → `"https://solerao.vercel.app"` (the real live domain, confirmed via `vercel project inspect`).

### 8. [High] Marketplace search never wired to a URL — `backend/marketplace/urls.py`
Currently `urlpatterns = []`. Add the actual route(s) for the existing, fully-written `search()` view in `views.py`.

### 9. [Medium] `create_client_sync` called two incompatible ways
`tenancy.py` calls it with a single dict; `tenant_writer.py` calls it with keyword args (`url=`, `auth_token=`) — the real `libsql_client` signature. Fix `tenancy.py` to match the correct keyword-argument form used in `tenant_writer.py`.

### Validation
`python manage.py check`, `python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` (confirms no model/migration drift introduced by any of the above), and a syntax/import pass across touched files. A real Turso connection can't be exercised without live credentials (the project's own July 25 commit message notes libsql hangs in this sandbox) — noted as a known limitation, not skipped silently.

---

## `solera0` — frontend fixes

### 10. [High] Frontend can't reach the backend even when deployed — architecture fix, not a patch
Currently: `src/lib/env.ts` falls back to `http://localhost:8000` baked into the production bundle, *and* `next.config.ts`'s CSP `connect-src` doesn't whitelist any backend origin even if the URL were set — two independent breaks.

Better fix than patching the CSP allowlist: add a `rewrites()` block in `next.config.ts` that proxies `/api/pharmacies/*`, `/api/marketplace/*`, `/api/consumer/*`, `/api/auth/*` (the real Django paths, confirmed from `src/lib/api.ts`) to the backend host via a **server-only** env var (e.g. `SOLERA0_API_URL`, not `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`). This means the browser only ever calls same-origin `/api/*` — no CORS needed, no CSP whitelist needed, and the backend URL is never exposed client-side. Update `src/lib/api.ts`/`env.ts` to call the same-origin path instead of resolving a public backend URL directly.

### 11. [Medium] Never rebranded — `package.json`, `package-lock.json`
`"name": "solera"` → `"name": "solera0"` in both.

### 12. [Medium] `vercel.json` disagrees with live deployment reality
Declares `"framework": "nextjs"` but the live Vercel project shows "Other." Will check `vercel.json`'s actual settings against the project's Root Directory/build config during implementation and correct whichever is wrong — flagging this one as verify-then-fix rather than a known-exact diff, since the live-project side of this needs checking via the Vercel MCP tools at implementation time.

---

## New feature: connect solera's tenants into solera0's Pharmacy directory

### 13. `backend/pharmacies/management/commands/sync_solera_tenants.py`
New Django management command, following the existing pattern in `seed_demo_pharmacy.py`:
- Connects to solera's real `solera-metadata` Turso DB (same `TURSO_DATABASE_URL` both apps already share) and reads the `tenants` table directly.
- For each tenant not already represented (matched by a `solera_tenant_id` field — added to the `Pharmacy` model — against solera's real tenant `id`), creates a `Pharmacy` row. The tenant's `db_url` and `db_token_encrypted` are copied **directly** from solera's `tenants` table — both apps share the same `ENCRYPTION_KEY` per the existing architecture, so the ciphertext is usable as-is without decrypt/re-encrypt.
- Creates a matching `PharmacyDirectory` row (name from the tenant; city/address left blank where solera's metadata schema doesn't carry them — not invented).
- Creates `ConsumerSettings` with `is_public=False` (per the confirmed decision).
- Idempotent — safe to re-run; skips tenants already synced.

This directly answers "why aren't the pharmacies connected": after this, running the command against real production credentials (a step the user triggers, not run automatically here) would create the missing `Pharmacy`/`ConsumerSettings` rows for Wanjiku/Mwangi/Muritu Pharmacy — still private until explicitly published, exactly matching the existing manual-approval model's own intent, just no longer requiring hand-typed credential re-entry.

### Migration
A small migration for `pharmacies` app adding `solera_tenant_id` to `Pharmacy`.

---

## Verification, end to end

- `solera`: `npm install && npx tsc --noEmit && npm test && npm run build`, all green, before the single commit to `main`.
- `solera0` backend: `python manage.py check`, `makemigrations --check --dry-run`, review the sync command's SQL/logic carefully since it can't be run against live Turso in this sandbox.
- `solera0` frontend: `npm install && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build` — confirms the `next.config.ts` rewrite doesn't break the build and no CSP regression.
- Report exactly which of the audit's Critical/High/Medium findings were fixed, which frontend/backend commits touched, and re-state the deferred `GAPS.md` backlog clearly as follow-up, not silently dropped.

## Follow-up backlog (not touched in this pass)

From `docs/GAPS.md`, explicitly carried forward, not silently dropped: email verification enforcement, password-reset flow, real audit-log writes, offline-first PWA (`idb`/Serwist), onboarding race-condition locking, orphaned-tenant-DB rollback on failed provisioning, session/token blocklist on deactivation, explicit CSRF/origin checks, Vercel preview-env Turso-key separation, inventory/POS/prescriptions/patients functional gaps (edit flows, receipt printing, shift management, dispense workflow), multi-branch enforcement, real dashboard KPI computation, plan selection at onboarding, and the PPB/ODPC/NHIF/KRA compliance integrations.

content.text:
Good question, but let me be honest about the actual scope before folding it into "as we proceed."

**Technically, yes — Django is just a framework, nothing stops it powering both.** But "both in Django" means rewriting `solera`'s entire live product — the full dashboard, POS, inventory, prescriptions, patients, clinic, billing, RBAC, and messaging system (223 source files, 74 commits of real work) — out of Next.js/TypeScript/Drizzle and into Django/DRF. That's not an addition alongside the current bug fixes; it's a from-scratch rewrite of a **live product with real tenant data**, and it's a separate, much bigger undertaking than what's in the approved plan.

What's already true, worth knowing before deciding: `solera0`'s Django backend already reads and writes `solera`'s real data directly (same Turso DB, same encryption key) — that connection exists at the data layer regardless of what framework the frontend is written in. So if the goal is "the two systems talk to each other," that's already the case and is exactly what this fix pass is repairing. If the goal is "one shared codebase/framework for both, going forward," that's a real, large, separate migration project.

"""Per-tenant Turso (libSQL) wrapper — mirrors Solera's createTenantClient/getTenantDb.

Solera is database-per-tenant: each pharmacy has its own encrypted Turso DB. Solera.0
wraps those same DBs so it can read live inventory and write consumer orders without
migrating data. The platform/registry/consumer layers live in Render Postgres (see
models in pharmacies/marketplace/consumer apps).
"""
import os
from libsql_client import create_client_sync


def get_metadata_client():
    """Solera's metadata Turso DB (tenants table, plans, etc.)."""
    return create_client_sync({
        "url": os.environ["TURSO_DATABASE_URL"],
        "authToken": os.environ.get("TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN", ""),
    })


def get_tenant_client(url: str, auth_token: str):
    """Open a connection to a specific pharmacy's Turso DB. decrypt() the token first."""
    return create_client_sync({"url": url, "authToken": auth_token})


def tenant_query(client, sql: str, params=None):
    """Execute a read against a tenant DB and return rows as dicts."""
    res = client.execute(sql, params or {})
    cols = res.columns
    return [dict(zip(cols, row)) for row in res.rows]

"""Consumer order endpoints (DD §4.2 / §8).

Place an order -> Django creates the ConsumerOrder + items, initiates M-Pesa STK via PayHero
server-side, and returns the checkout request id. The PayHero callback (payments app) marks the
order paid and generates the pickup OTP (mirrors MYDAWA's order-verification OTP).
"""
import json
import secrets
import string
import time
from django.http import JsonResponse
from django.views.decorators.csrf import csrf_exempt
from django.views.decorators.http import require_POST, require_GET
from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404

from .models import ConsumerOrder, ConsumerOrderItem, ConsumerUser

OTP_ALPHABET = string.digits


def _now():
    return int(time.time() * 1000)


def _make_otp(n=6):
    return "".join(secrets.choice(OTP_ALPHABET) for _ in range(n))


def _auth_phone(request):
    """Extract consumer phone from Bearer token (best-effort; dev fallback to header)."""
    auth = request.META.get("HTTP_AUTHORIZATION", "")
    # In dev without a real JWT, allow x-consumer-phone header for testing.
    return request.headers.get("x-consumer-phone") or auth.replace("Bearer ", "") or None


@csrf_exempt
@require_POST
def place_order(request):
    body = json.loads(request.body or "{}")
    phone = body.get("phone") or _auth_phone(request)
    pharmacy_id = body.get("pharmacy_id")
    items = body.get("items", [])
    fulfilment = body.get("fulfilment_type", "pickup")
    customer_name = body.get("customer_name", "")

    if not (phone and pharmacy_id and items):
        return JsonResponse({"error": "phone, pharmacy_id, items required"}, status=400)

    from pharmacies.models import Pharmacy
    pharmacy = get_object_or_404(Pharmacy, id=pharmacy_id)

    total = sum(int(i.get("unit_price", 0)) * int(i.get("quantity", 0)) for i in items)
    order_id = "CO-" + "".join(secrets.choice(string.ascii_uppercase + string.digits) for _ in range(10))

    consumer, _ = ConsumerUser.objects.get_or_create(phone=phone, defaults={"name": customer_name})
    order = ConsumerOrder.objects.create(
        id=order_id,
        pharmacy=pharmacy,
        consumer=consumer,
        status="pending",
        fulfilment_type=fulfilment,
        total_amount=total,
        payment_status="unpaid",
        otp="",  # set on payment
        created_at=_now(),
        updated_at=_now(),
    )
    for it in items:
        ConsumerOrderItem.objects.create(
            order=order,
            product_id=str(it.get("product_id", "")),
            product_name=it.get("product_name", ""),
            quantity=int(it.get("quantity", 1)),
            unit_price=int(it.get("unit_price", 0)),
            batch_id=it.get("batch_id", ""),
        )

    # Initiate M-Pesa STK via PayHero (payments module). Fail-soft: order still created.
    stk = None
    try:
        from payments.payhero import initiate_stk
        stk = initiate_stk(
            phone=phone,
            amount=total,
            reference=order_id,
            description=f"Solera0 order {order_id}",
        )
    except Exception as e:  # pragma: no cover - network/provider failure
        stk = {"error": str(e)}

    return JsonResponse({
        "order_id": order_id,
        "status": order.status,
        "total_amount": total,
        "payment_status": order.payment_status,
        "fulfilment_type": fulfilment,
        "stk": stk,
    }, status=201)


@require_GET
def my_orders(request):
    phone = _auth_phone(request)
    if not phone:
        return JsonResponse({"error": "phone required"}, status=400)
    qs = ConsumerOrder.objects.filter(consumer__phone=phone).order_by("-created_at")[:50]
    out = []
    for o in qs:
        out.append({
            "order_id": o.id,
            "pharmacy": o.pharmacy.display_name,
            "status": o.status,
            "fulfilment_type": o.fulfilment_type,
            "total_amount": o.total_amount,
            "payment_status": o.payment_status,
            "otp": o.otp if o.payment_status == "paid" else "",
            "created_at": o.created_at,
            "items": [{"product_name": i.product_name, "quantity": i.quantity,
                       "unit_price": i.unit_price} for i in o.items.all()],
        })
    return JsonResponse({"orders": out})


@require_GET
def order_detail(request, order_id):
    phone = _auth_phone(request)
    if not phone:
        return JsonResponse({"error": "phone required"}, status=400)
    o = get_object_or_404(ConsumerOrder, id=order_id, consumer__phone=phone)
    return JsonResponse({
        "order_id": o.id,
        "pharmacy": o.pharmacy.display_name,
        "status": o.status,
        "fulfilment_type": o.fulfilment_type,
        "total_amount": o.total_amount,
        "payment_status": o.payment_status,
        "otp": o.otp if o.payment_status == "paid" else "",
        "items": [{"product_name": i.product_name, "quantity": i.quantity,
                   "unit_price": i.unit_price} for i in o.items.all()],
    })

"""Aggregated consumer search across opted-in pharmacies (DD 7.1).

Runtime fan-out across PUBLIC pharmacies' Turso DBs. Replaced by a search-index projection
(Meilisearch/Algolia fed by StockSyncLedger) at scale. Flattens results to the exact shape
the frontend expects: {pharmacy_id, pharmacy, city, in_stock, quantity, unit_price,
product_name, batch_id}.
"""
import time
from pharmacies.models import Pharmacy, ConsumerSettings, PharmacyDirectory
from common.inventory import available_stock, pharmacy_is_stale


def search_medicine(term, city=None, otc_only=True, limit_per_pharmacy=5):
    q = Pharmacy.objects.filter(status="active")
    if city:
        q = q.filter(pharmacydirectory__city=city)
    results = []
    for ph in q:
        cs = ConsumerSettings.objects.filter(pharmacy=ph, is_public=True).first()
        if not cs:
            continue
        if pharmacy_is_stale(ph):
            # Still list the pharmacy but with no live items (freshness guard, DD 6.3).
            results.append({
                "pharmacy_id": ph.id, "pharmacy": ph.name, "city": ph.slug and "",
                "in_stock": False, "quantity": 0, "unit_price": 0,
                "product_name": "", "batch_id": "",
            })
            continue
        stock = available_stock(ph, term, otc_only=otc_only)[:limit_per_pharmacy]
        directory = PharmacyDirectory.objects.filter(pharmacy=ph).first()
        city_name = directory.city if directory else ""
        for row in stock:
            results.append({
                "pharmacy_id": ph.id,
                "pharmacy": ph.name,
                "city": city_name,
                "in_stock": int(row.get("qty", 0) or 0) > 0,
                "quantity": int(row.get("qty", 0) or 0),
                "unit_price": int(round(float(row.get("selling_price", 0) or 0))),
                "product_name": row.get("name", ""),
                "batch_id": str(row.get("id", "")),
            })
    return results

"""Short-lived, database-backed OTP codes for common.views.request_otp/verify_otp.

Deliberately DB-backed rather than Django's cache framework: this project has no
Redis/memcached configured (see requirements.txt), and gunicorn typically runs multiple
worker processes in production — an in-memory cache would silently fail to share OTPs
issued by one worker with a verification request that lands on another.
"""
from django.db import models


class OtpCode(models.Model):
    phone = models.CharField(max_length=20, db_index=True)
    code = models.CharField(max_length=10)
    role = models.CharField(max_length=20, default="consumer")
    consumed = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    expires_at = models.BigIntegerField()
    created_at = models.BigIntegerField()

    def __str__(self):
        return f"OTP for {self.phone} ({'used' if self.consumed else 'active'})"

"""Brevo transactional SMS — ports Solera's src/lib/email.ts sendSms() to Python so
Solera.0 sends real OTP codes instead of hardcoding one. Same API, same account
(BREVO_API_KEY/BREVO_SMS_SENDER are already shared with Solera per backend/.env.example).
"""
import os
import re

import requests

BREVO_SMS_API = "https://api.brevo.com/v3/transactionalSMS/sms"


def _normalize_kenyan_phone(phone: str) -> str:
    digits = re.sub(r"\D", "", phone or "")
    return re.sub(r"^0", "254", digits)


def send_sms(phone: str, message: str) -> bool:
    """Returns True only on a confirmed-sent response from Brevo. False (never raises) on
    missing config or any delivery failure — callers must treat this as best-effort."""
    api_key = os.environ.get("BREVO_API_KEY")
    sender = os.environ.get("BREVO_SMS_SENDER")
    if not api_key or not sender:
        return False
    try:
        res = requests.post(
            BREVO_SMS_API,
            headers={
                "api-key": api_key,
                "Content-Type": "application/json",
                "Accept": "application/json",
            },
            json={
                "sender": sender,
                "recipient": _normalize_kenyan_phone(phone),
                "content": message,
                "type": "transactional",
            },
            timeout=10,
        )
    except requests.RequestException:
        return False
    return res.ok

    items = body.get("items", [])
    fulfilment = body.get("fulfilment_type", "pickup")

    order_id = "CO-" + "".join(secrets.choice(string.ascii_uppercase + string.digits) for _ in range(10))

    consumer, _ = ConsumerUser.objects.get_or_create(phone=phone, defaults={"name": customer_name})
    order = ConsumerOrder.objects.create(

        payment_status="unpaid",
        otp="",  # set on payment

            order=order,
            product_id=str(it.get("product_id", "")),
            product_name=it.get("product_name", ""),
            quantity=int(it.get("quantity", 1)),
            unit_price=int(it.get("unit_price", 0)),
            batch_id=it.get("batch_id", ""),

"""Per-tenant Turso (libSQL) wrapper — mirrors Solera's createTenantClient/getTenantDb.

Solera is database-per-tenant: each pharmacy has its own encrypted Turso DB. Solera.0
wraps those same DBs so it can read live inventory and write consumer orders without
migrating data. The platform/registry/consumer layers live in Render Postgres (see
models in pharmacies/marketplace/consumer apps).
"""
import os
from libsql_client import create_client_sync


def get_metadata_client():
    """Solera's metadata Turso DB (tenants table, plans, etc.)."""
    return create_client_sync({
        "url": os.environ["TURSO_DATABASE_URL"],
        "authToken": os.environ.get("TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN", ""),
    })


def get_tenant_client(url: str, auth_token: str):
    """Open a connection to a specific pharmacy's Turso DB. decrypt() the token first."""
    return create_client_sync({"url": url, "authToken": auth_token})


def tenant_query(client, sql: str, params=None):
    """Execute a read against a tenant DB and return rows as dicts."""
    res = client.execute(sql, params or {})
    cols = res.columns
    return [dict(zip(cols, row)) for row in res.rows]

import os
from libsql_client import create_client_sync

        "authToken": os.environ.get("TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN", ""),
    })


def get_tenant_client(url: str, auth_token: str):
    """Open a connection to a specific pharmacy's Turso DB. decrypt() the token first."""
    return create_client_sync({"url": url, "authToken": auth_token})


def tenant_query(client, sql: str, params=None):
    """Execute a read against a tenant DB and return rows as dicts."""
    res = client.execute(sql, params or {})
    cols = res.columns
    return [dict(zip(cols, row)) for row in res.rows]

# Solera.0 — Render Setup

This document previously described a Postgres-based deploy path that was abandoned the
same day it was written (see `DEPLOY_TURSO.md`'s own history) but never removed, leaving
two runbooks that actively disagreed with each other and with the actual code in
`backend/solera0/settings/base.py` (which only ever supported `libsql://` and `sqlite`,
never `postgres://`).

**Use [`DEPLOY_TURSO.md`](./DEPLOY_TURSO.md) instead** — it's the one deploy path that

# Solera.0 — Render Setup (step by step, for you to run)

> The Vercel `solera.o` frontend is being deployed from the agent. The **Django backend on Render**
> is what YOU set up (the agent sandbox cannot reach render.com). This is a ~5 minute terminal session
> on your machine. Everything below is verified-ready in the repo (`render.yaml`, `Procfile`,
> `runtime.txt`, `requirements.txt`).

## Prerequisites
- Install Render CLI: `brew install render` (mac) or `npm i -g render-cli`
- `render login` (browser opens, connect your account)
- You need Solera's REAL secret values (from the original `solera` Vercel project env):
  - `TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN`, `TURSO_API_TOKEN`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY`  ← CRITICAL, must match Solera
  - PayHero: `PAYHERO_AUTH_TOKEN` (Basic <base64>), `PAYHERO_ACCOUNT_ID` (9910), `PAYHERO_CHANNEL_ID` (9360)
  - Brevo: `BREVO_API_KEY`

## Step 1 — Create the service + Postgres from render.yaml
```bash
cd solera0
render blueprint launch render.yaml
```
If `blueprint launch` isn't available, do it manually in the dashboard:
- New → Web Service → connect `ken-muritu/solera0`
- Runtime: **Python 3.11** | Build: `pip install -r requirements.txt`
- Start: `gunicorn solera0.wsgi:application --bind 0.0.0.0:$PORT`
- Add a **Postgres** database (render.yaml defines `solera0-db`); Render auto-injects `DATABASE_URL`.

## Step 2 — Set environment variables (paste REAL values)
In Render dashboard → solera0-api → Environment, add:
```
DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE = solera0.settings.prod
SECRET_KEY = <openssl rand -hex 32>
DEBUG = False
TURSO_DATABASE_URL = libsql://solera-metadata-ken-muritu.aws-eu-west-1.turso.io
TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN = <Solera's real TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN>
TURSO_API_TOKEN = <Solera's real TURSO_API_TOKEN>
TURSO_ORG = ken-muritu
ENCRYPTION_KEY = <Solera's real ENCRYPTION_KEY>   # MUST match Solera or tenant tokens won't decrypt
PAYHERO_AUTH_TOKEN = Basic <base64>
PAYHERO_ACCOUNT_ID = 9910
PAYHERO_CHANNEL_ID = 9360
PAYHERO_CALLBACK_URL = https://solera0.onrender.com/api/payments/payhero/callback
PAYHERO_CALLBACK_SECRET = <openssl rand -hex 32>
BREVO_API_KEY = <Brevo key>
BREVO_SMS_SENDER = Solera
CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS = https://solerao.vercel.app
```
`DATABASE_URL` is auto-injected by the Postgres attach (do not set manually).

## Step 3 — Run migrations (one time)
Use Render's shell, or locally with the same env:
```bash
python manage.py migrate
```

## Step 4 — Verify
```bash
curl https://solera0.onrender.com/api/health/
# -> {"status":"ok","service":"solera0","mode":"django"}
curl "https://solera0.onrender.com/api/health/research/"
# -> lists the embedded research docs
```

## Why ENCRYPTION_KEY must match Solera
Solera.0's `common/crypto.py` uses AES-256-GCM with `key = SHA256(ENCRYPTION_KEY)`. Solera stored each
pharmacy's Turso token encrypted with Solera's `ENCRYPTION_KEY`. If Solera.0 uses a different key, it
cannot decrypt those tokens → cannot open pharmacy DBs → no inventory reads, no order writes. So copy
Solera's `ENCRYPTION_KEY` exactly.

## After both are up (Interpretation A = done)
- Vercel `solerao.vercel.app` serves the Solera frontend (separate instance, same Turso org).
- Render `solera0.onrender.com` serves the Django API reading live pharmacy stock.
- Next: implement FRONTEND_REWIRING.md so consumers buy through Django (Interpretation B).

# Solera.0 Backend Deployment — Turso only (no Postgres / Neon / Fly)

Solera.0 wraps Solera's existing per-tenant Turso/libSQL databases. The platform registry
(pharmacies, consumer orders, applications) ALSO lives in a Turso "metadata" DB — the same
model as Solera. There is NO separate Postgres/Neon database and NO Fly config.

## Prereqs
- A Turso metadata DB for Solera.0. Reuse Solera's existing metadata DB, or create one:
  ```bash
  turso db create solera0-metadata --org ken-muritu
  turso db tokens create solera0-metadata --permissions read-write
  ```
- Django reads the registry from `DATABASE_URL` (a `libsql://` URL) via the `django-libsql` backend.
  No database add-on is needed on the host — Turso IS the database.

## Environment (all required on the host)
```
DATABASE_URL=libsql://solera0-metadata-ken-muritu.aws-eu-west-1.turso.io
TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN=<token for the metadata db>
DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=solera0.settings.prod
SECRET_KEY=<rand -hex 32>
DEBUG=False
ENCRYPTION_KEY=<Solera's real ENCRYPTION_KEY>   # must match or tenant tokens won't decrypt
TURSO_ORG=ken-muritu
PAYHERO_AUTH_TOKEN=<base64>
PAYHERO_ACCOUNT_ID=9910
PAYHERO_CHANNEL_ID=9360
PAYHERO_CALLBACK_URL=https://<your-backend-host>/api/payments/payhero/callback
PAYHERO_CALLBACK_SECRET=<rand -hex 32>
BREVO_API_KEY=<key>
BREVO_SMS_SENDER=Solera
CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://solerao.vercel.app
PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS=kenhopkins.ke@gmail.com
```

## Host (any $0 / cheap container host — no DB add-on needed)
The backend is plain Django + gunicorn. Because the DB is Turso (not Postgres), you do NOT need
Render's paid Postgres or Neon. Pick any host that runs a Docker/Python web service:
- **Railway** (simplest): `railway init` + set env vars above + `railway up`.
- **Fly.io**: `fly launch --no-deploy` + `fly secrets set ...` + `fly deploy` (keep fly.toml if you
  want it; it is NOT required — any host works).
- **Render free tier**: works now because there is no Postgres dependency. `render.yaml` is optional.

## After deploy
```bash
python manage.py migrate                 # creates registry tables in the Turso metadata DB
python manage.py seed_demo_pharmacy      # PUBLIC demo pharmacy so /marketplace shows stock
curl https://<host>/api/health/          # {"status":"ok",...}
```
Then in Vercel set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SOLERA0_API=<host>` and git-push the frontend.

## Pharmacy onboarding (self-serve)
- `/for-pharmacies` (frontend) -> `POST /api/pharmacies/apply` stores a PharmacyApplication.
- Admin approves via `POST /api/pharmacies/applications/<id>/approve/` with header
  `x-admin-email: kenhopkins.ke@gmail.com` + the pharmacy's Turso creds. Approval creates the
  Pharmacy row (+ directory + ConsumerSettings, defaults PRIVATE). Flip `is_public=True` to list.

## Why not Postgres/Neon?
Solera.0 is explicitly a Turso-first wrapper around Solera's tenant DBs. Adding Postgres/Neon was
a detour; the registry now lives in Turso exactly like Solera's own metadata store.

"""Pharmacy registry models (Solera.0 platform/Postgres layer).

These mirror Solera's `tenants` (metadata DB) and the proposed `consumer_settings` /
`pharmacy_directory` tables from the consumer-marketplace DD (v2.0, §4.2/§4.3).
The operational pharmacy data (products, inventory_batches, sales, prescriptions) stays in
each pharmacy's own Turso DB, accessed via common.tenancy — faithful to Solera's
database-per-tenant model.
"""
from django.db import models


class Plan(models.Model):
    """Mirrors Solera metadata.plans."""
    name = models.CharField(max_length=80)
    description = models.TextField(blank=True)
    price_kes_monthly = models.IntegerField(null=True, blank=True)
    price_usd_monthly = models.IntegerField(null=True, blank=True)
    max_branches = models.IntegerField(default=1)
    max_users = models.IntegerField(default=5)
    features = models.JSONField(default=dict)

    def __str__(self):
        return self.name


class Pharmacy(models.Model):
    """Registry row per Solera tenant. Holds the encrypted Turso token so Solera.0
    can open that pharmacy's operational DB (read inventory / write consumer orders)."""
    tenant_id = models.CharField(max_length=64, unique=True)
    name = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    slug = models.SlugField(max_length=120, unique=True)
    # encrypted Turso credentials (AES-256-GCM, shares Solera ENCRYPTION_KEY)
    turso_db_url = models.TextField()
    db_token_encrypted = models.TextField()
    plan = models.ForeignKey(Plan, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True, blank=True)
    status = models.CharField(max_length=20, default="active")
    created_at = models.BigIntegerField()

    def __str__(self):
        return f"{self.name} ({self.slug})"


class PharmacyDirectory(models.Model):
    """Public directory of opted-in pharmacies (DD §4.3 pharmacy_directory)."""
    pharmacy = models.OneToOneField(Pharmacy, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    display_name = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    address = models.TextField(blank=True)
    lat = models.FloatField(null=True, blank=True)
    lng = models.FloatField(null=True, blank=True)
    city = models.CharField(max_length=100, blank=True)
    county = models.CharField(max_length=100, blank=True)
    is_verified = models.BooleanField(default=False)   # PPB licence check before public
    is_active = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    created_at = models.BigIntegerField()

    def __str__(self):
        return self.display_name


class ConsumerSettings(models.Model):
    """Per-pharmacy storefront config (DD §4.2 consumer_settings). Default PRIVATE/safe."""
    pharmacy = models.OneToOneField(Pharmacy, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    is_public = models.BooleanField(default=False)     # opt-in, default private
    display_name = models.CharField(max_length=200, blank=True)
    address = models.TextField(blank=True)
    lat = models.FloatField(null=True, blank=True)
    lng = models.FloatField(null=True, blank=True)
    phone = models.CharField(max_length=20, blank=True)
    operating_hours = models.JSONField(default=dict, blank=True)
    pickup_enabled = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    delivery_enabled = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    min_order_amount = models.IntegerField(default=0)
    created_at = models.BigIntegerField()
    updated_at = models.BigIntegerField()


class PharmacyApplication(models.Model):
    """Self-serve 'List my pharmacy' request (DD §4.3 onboarding + PPB gating).

    Status flow: pending -> approved (creates Pharmacy + PharmacyDirectory + ConsumerSettings,
    defaults PRIVATE until the pharmacy opts into the public storefront) or rejected.
    PPB licence is captured but verification is a manual admin step before public listing.
    """
    STATUS = [("pending", "pending"), ("approved", "approved"), ("rejected", "rejected")]
    name = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    contact_phone = models.CharField(max_length=20)
    contact_email = models.CharField(max_length=200, blank=True)
    city = models.CharField(max_length=100)
    county = models.CharField(max_length=100, blank=True)
    address = models.TextField(blank=True)
    ppb_license = models.CharField(max_length=100, blank=True, help_text="PPB licence number (verified before public listing)")
    is_verified = models.BooleanField(default=False)  # PPB licence checked
    status = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=STATUS, default="pending")
    notes = models.TextField(blank=True)
    created_at = models.BigIntegerField()
    reviewed_at = models.BigIntegerField(null=True, blank=True)

    def __str__(self):
        return f"{self.name} ({self.status})"

"""Seed a demo pharmacy + make it PUBLIC so the marketplace shows live stock.

Run: python manage.py seed_demo_pharmacy
Set env to point at a REAL Solera tenant Turso DB for actual stock, otherwise it seeds a
placeholder (the pharmacy appears but reports no live stock until real Turso creds are set).

Env:
  DEMO_TURSO_DB_URL      e.g. libsql://<slug>-ken-muritu.aws-eu-west-1.turso.io
  DEMO_TURSO_TOKEN       the tenant's Turso auth token (encrypted with ENCRYPTION_KEY)
  DEMO_PHARMACY_NAME     default "Solera Demo Pharmacy"
  DEMO_CITY              default "Nairobi"
"""
import os
import time
from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand
from django.conf import settings
from common.crypto import encrypt
from pharmacies.models import Pharmacy, PharmacyDirectory, ConsumerSettings, Plan


class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = "Seed a demo pharmacy and mark it public for the marketplace."

    def handle(self, *args, **opts):
        name = os.environ.get("DEMO_PHARMACY_NAME", "Solera Demo Pharmacy")
        city = os.environ.get("DEMO_CITY", "Nairobi")
        county = os.environ.get("DEMO_COUNTY", "Nairobi")
        turso_db_url = os.environ.get("DEMO_TURSO_DB_URL", "libsql://solera-demo-ken-muritu.aws-eu-west-1.turso.io")
        raw_token = os.environ.get("DEMO_TURSO_TOKEN", "REPLACE_WITH_REAL_TOKEN")
        token_enc = encrypt(raw_token)

        plan, _ = Plan.objects.get_or_create(name="Starter", defaults={"price_kes_monthly": 0})
        slug = name.lower().replace(" ", "-").replace("'", "")[:120]

        ph, created = Pharmacy.objects.update_or_create(
            slug=slug,
            defaults={
                "tenant_id": f"demo-{slug}",
                "name": name,
                "turso_db_url": turso_db_url,
                "db_token_encrypted": token_enc,
                "plan": plan,
                "status": "active",
                "created_at": int(time.time() * 1000),
            },
        )
        PharmacyDirectory.objects.update_or_create(
            pharmacy=ph,
            defaults={"display_name": name, "city": city, "county": county,
                      "is_verified": True, "is_active": True,
                      "created_at": int(time.time() * 1000)},
        )
        ConsumerSettings.objects.update_or_create(
            pharmacy=ph,
            defaults={"is_public": True, "display_name": name, "city": city,
                      "phone": "+254700000000", "created_at": int(time.time() * 1000),
                      "updated_at": int(time.time() * 1000)},
        )
        self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS(
            f"Demo pharmacy '{name}' {'created' if created else 'updated'} and PUBLIC."
        ))
        if raw_token == "REPLACE_WITH_REAL_TOKEN":
            self.stdout.write(self.style.WARNING(
                "Using placeholder Turso token — set DEMO_TURSO_DB_URL + DEMO_TURSO_TOKEN "
                "to a real Solera tenant DB for live stock."
            ))

"""Connect Solera's real tenants into Solera.0's Pharmacy directory.

Answers the standing gap: Solera's tenants table and Solera.0's Pharmacy model have no
automatic link — the only wiring that existed before this command was the fully manual
apply()/approve() admin flow (pharmacies/views.py), which requires hand-typing a tenant's
Turso credentials into an API call. Nobody had run that flow for any of Solera's existing
tenants, so none of them showed up here.

This command reads Solera's tenants table directly (same TURSO_DATABASE_URL both apps
already share) and creates the matching Pharmacy/PharmacyDirectory/ConsumerSettings rows,
copying db_url and db_token_encrypted AS-IS — both apps share the same ENCRYPTION_KEY, so
the ciphertext is valid without decrypt/re-encrypt.

Every synced pharmacy is created PRIVATE (ConsumerSettings.is_public=False), matching the
existing approve() flow's own default and the documented PPB-verification gate. Nothing
becomes publicly searchable by running this command — that's a deliberate, separate,
per-pharmacy action.

Idempotent: matches on Pharmacy.tenant_id (Solera's real tenant id), safe to re-run as new
tenants sign up on Solera.

Run: python manage.py sync_solera_tenants
"""
import time

from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand

from common.tenancy import get_metadata_client, tenant_query
from pharmacies.models import Pharmacy, PharmacyDirectory, ConsumerSettings


class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = "Create Pharmacy/ConsumerSettings rows for every existing Solera tenant (private by default)."

    def handle(self, *args, **opts):
        client = get_metadata_client()
        try:
            rows = tenant_query(
                client,
                "SELECT id, name, slug, db_url, db_token_encrypted, status, created_at FROM tenants",
            )
        finally:
            close = getattr(client, "close", None)
            if callable(close):
                close()

        created_count = 0
        skipped_count = 0
        now = int(time.time() * 1000)

        for row in rows:
            tenant_id = row["id"]
            existing = Pharmacy.objects.filter(tenant_id=tenant_id).first()
            if existing:
                skipped_count += 1
                self.stdout.write(f"skip (already synced): {row['name']} ({tenant_id})")
                continue

            # Plan intentionally left unset: Solera's plan_id is a foreign key into its own
            # plans table, whose contents this command doesn't assume or invent a mapping
            # for. Set Pharmacy.plan by hand afterward if you want it reflected here.
            pharmacy = Pharmacy.objects.create(
                tenant_id=tenant_id,
                name=row["name"],
                slug=row["slug"],
                turso_db_url=row["db_url"],
                db_token_encrypted=row["db_token_encrypted"],
                status=row.get("status") or "active",
                created_at=row.get("created_at") or now,
            )
            PharmacyDirectory.objects.create(
                pharmacy=pharmacy,
                display_name=row["name"],
                # Solera's tenants table doesn't carry city/address — left blank rather
                # than guessed; fill in via the Django admin once known.
                is_verified=False,
                is_active=True,
                created_at=now,
            )
            ConsumerSettings.objects.create(
                pharmacy=pharmacy,
                is_public=False,
                display_name=row["name"],
                created_at=now,
                updated_at=now,
            )
            created_count += 1
            self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS(f"synced (private): {row['name']} ({tenant_id})"))

        self.stdout.write(
            self.style.SUCCESS(f"Done. {created_count} synced, {skipped_count} already present.")
        )
        if created_count:
            self.stdout.write(
                "All newly-synced pharmacies are PRIVATE. Flip ConsumerSettings.is_public=True "
                "per pharmacy (Django admin, or an approve-style endpoint) when ready to publish."
            )

# Solera.0 Backend Deployment — Turso only (no Postgres / Neon / Fly)

Solera.0 wraps Solera's existing per-tenant Turso/libSQL databases. The platform registry
(pharmacies, consumer orders, applications) ALSO lives in a Turso "metadata" DB — the same
model as Solera. There is NO separate Postgres/Neon database and NO Fly config.

## Prereqs
- A Turso metadata DB for Solera.0. Reuse Solera's existing metadata DB, or create one:
  ```bash
  turso db create solera0-metadata --org ken-muritu
  turso db tokens create solera0-metadata --permissions read-write
  ```
- Django reads the registry from `DATABASE_URL` (a `libsql://` URL) via the `django-libsql` backend.
  No database add-on is needed on the host — Turso IS the database.

## Environment (all required on the host)
```
DATABASE_URL=libsql://solera0-metadata-ken-muritu.aws-eu-west-1.turso.io
TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN=<token for the metadata db>
DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=solera0.settings.prod
SECRET_KEY=<rand -hex 32>
DEBUG=False
ENCRYPTION_KEY=<Solera's real ENCRYPTION_KEY>   # must match or tenant tokens won't decrypt
TURSO_ORG=ken-muritu
PAYHERO_AUTH_TOKEN=<base64>
PAYHERO_ACCOUNT_ID=9910
PAYHERO_CHANNEL_ID=9360
PAYHERO_CALLBACK_URL=https://<your-backend-host>/api/payments/payhero/callback
PAYHERO_CALLBACK_SECRET=<rand -hex 32>
BREVO_API_KEY=<key>
BREVO_SMS_SENDER=Solera
CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://solerao.vercel.app
PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS=kenhopkins.ke@gmail.com
```

## Host (any $0 / cheap container host — no DB add-on needed)
The backend is plain Django + gunicorn. Because the DB is Turso (not Postgres), you do NOT need
Render's paid Postgres or Neon. Pick any host that runs a Docker/Python web service:
- **Railway** (simplest): `railway init` + set env vars above + `railway up`.
- **Fly.io**: `fly launch --no-deploy` + `fly secrets set ...` + `fly deploy` (keep fly.toml if you
  want it; it is NOT required — any host works).
- **Render free tier**: works now because there is no Postgres dependency. `render.yaml` is optional.

## After deploy
```bash
python manage.py migrate                 # creates registry tables in the Turso metadata DB
python manage.py seed_demo_pharmacy      # PUBLIC demo pharmacy so /marketplace shows stock
curl https://<host>/api/health/          # {"status":"ok",...}
```
Then in Vercel set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SOLERA0_API=<host>` and git-push the frontend.

## Pharmacy onboarding (self-serve)
- `/for-pharmacies` (frontend) -> `POST /api/pharmacies/apply` stores a PharmacyApplication.
- Admin approves via `POST /api/pharmacies/applications/<id>/approve/` with header
  `x-admin-email: kenhopkins.ke@gmail.com` + the pharmacy's Turso creds. Approval creates the
  Pharmacy row (+ directory + ConsumerSettings, defaults PRIVATE). Flip `is_public=True` to list.

## Why not Postgres/Neon?
Solera.0 is explicitly a Turso-first wrapper around Solera's tenant DBs. Adding Postgres/Neon was
a detour; the registry now lives in Turso exactly like Solera's own metadata store.

cd /home/pop-os/Downloads/.fix-tmp/solera
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix: close PayHero webhook forgery gap; run tests in CI

verifyPayHeroCallback's shape-only fallback (added in 12c9579, to work around
PayHero not reliably echoing back a shared secret) accepted any correctly-shaped
POST body with zero verification — a forged webhook with a guessable reference
(SALE-<tenantId8>-<receiptNumber>) could mark a sale or subscription paid without
payment.

Fix: the fallback no longer trusts the body's claimed outcome. It now
independently reconciles the reference against PayHero's own authenticated
status API (getTransactionStatus, already used for client-side payment
polling) before anything is marked paid. The fast, fully-trusted path (real
secret match) is unchanged.

verifyPayHeroCallback now returns "verified" | "unverified_shape" | "rejected"
instead of a boolean, so call sites can no longer conflate "looks right" with
"is authentic."

Also: CI ran lint/build/audit but never `npm test`, so the one existing test
covering this function had never actually run — it called
verifyPayHeroCallback(req) with a different signature than the real call site
uses, so it never exercised the vulnerable path either. Fixed the test's
signature and added coverage that specifically asserts a shaped-but-unsigned
body returns "unverified_shape", not "verified". Added `npm test` to CI.

Unrelated, needed for local `npm run build` to complete on this machine:
approved install scripts for esbuild/sharp/unrs-resolver via `npm
install-scripts approve` (package.json's new `allowScripts` block) — these
packages' native-binary postinstall steps were previously silently skipped by
npm's own script-allowlisting, which would affect any fresh `npm ci` in CI
too, not just this change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01CnExWcAK4d4P1a7aFRmTmd
EOF
)"

**`solera` (live product) — done and pushed.** Commit `a2f8bb7..3cd4e37` on `main`. The critical PayHero webhook forgery bug is fixed — unverified callbacks now get independently reconciled against PayHero's real API instead of being trusted. One small piece still pending: the CI workflow addition (`npm test` step) is written locally but can't push — GitHub blocks workflow-file changes without a `workflow`-scoped token, and the current `gh` auth only has `repo`/`gist`/`read:org`. # Fix Solera + Solera0 bugs, and connect them

## Context

The audit (`~/Downloads/Solera & Solera0 - Repo, Deployment & Database Audit.md`) found a live, exploitable payment-webhook forgery bug in `solera` (which has real tenant data today), a fully bypassable auth system and an unverified payment webhook in `solera0`'s never-deployed backend, an architecture conflict (`render.yaml` still provisions Postgres though the code is Turso-only, traced to an abandoned decision made and reversed within 6 minutes on July 25 and never fully cleaned up), a CORS domain typo, an unwired search endpoint, and no actual connection between solera's real pharmacy tenants and solera0's marketplace directory — that connection is a fully manual admin workflow that was designed but never run for any of the 3 existing tenants.

Turso was researched directly (WebSearch, not assumed): it is database-only, no compute/hosting layer. Django still needs a real host (Render, as already scaffolded) — Turso only ever serves as its database, which `django-libsql`/`libsql_client` already support natively once `render.yaml` stops fighting that.

Decisions already confirmed with the user:
- This pass makes the code correct and deployment-ready. **No live Render deployment, no real production secrets provisioned** — that's a separate, deliberate step the user triggers later.
- `solera` fixes land as a **direct commit to `main`**, only after full local validation (install, type-check, test, build all green) — same rigor as the earlier CaspaHub cleanup, given this touches a live payment path.
- The new tenant→pharmacy sync creates rows **private by default** (`ConsumerSettings.is_public=False`) — matches the existing `approve()` flow's own default and the documented PPB-verification gate. Nothing becomes publicly searchable without an explicit follow-up action.

## Scope: what's fixed now vs. deferred

**Fixed in this pass** — every finding in the audit's Critical/High/Medium sections that is a genuine, verifiable code defect fixable through code alone, plus the tenant-sync connecting feature.

**Explicitly deferred, not attempted in this pass** — the broader feature backlog in `docs/GAPS.md` (password-reset flow, PWA offline support, NHIF/KRA/PPB compliance API integrations, real audit-log writes, multi-branch enforcement, dashboard KPI real computation, plan-selection UX, email verification enforcement). These are net-new features or third-party integrations requiring real accounts/credentials and product decisions, not bugs — bundling them into a security-fix pass risks doing all of it hastily. I'll list them back out as a clean follow-up backlog at the end of this work rather than touch them now.

---

## `solera` — fixes (commit directly to `main` after full local validation)

### 1. [Critical] PayHero webhook forgery — `src/lib/payhero-webhook.ts`
Root cause (confirmed via `git show 12c9579`): PayHero doesn't reliably echo back a secret, so `isPayHeroCallbackPayload()` was added as a fallback that accepts any correctly-shaped body with **no verification at all**.

Fix: instead of trusting the webhook body's `status` field when the secret checks fail, treat an unverified-but-shaped callback as a *trigger to independently re-check the transaction with PayHero's own authenticated status API* (using `PAYHERO_AUTH_TOKEN`, server-side only, never attacker-controlled) before marking anything paid. Solera already has this exact capability for client-side polling (`src/app/api/payments/status/route.ts`, and a `payhero-status` test file per the audit) — I'll locate and reuse that existing PayHero-status-check function rather than write a new one, wiring it into the webhook path as the source of truth when the shared-secret path can't confirm authenticity. If header/query secret verification succeeds, trust the webhook directly as today (fast path preserved); only the currently-forgeable fallback changes.

### 2. [High] CI never runs tests — `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
Add an `npm test` (or the project's actual test script name) step, so the 5 existing test files — including the payhero-webhook coverage — actually run on every push/PR, not just lint/build/audit.

### 3. [Medium] Fix the payhero-webhook test's signature mismatch
`payhero-webhook.test.ts` calls `verifyPayHeroCallback(req)` with one argument; the real call site passes `{ body }` as a second argument. Fix the test to call it the same way production does, so it actually exercises the path being fixed in #1.

### Validation before commit
`npm install && npx tsc --noEmit && npm test && npm run build` — all green, matching the CaspaHub precedent, before a single commit to `main`.

---

## `solera0` — backend fixes

### 4. [Critical] OTP auth fully bypassable — `backend/common/views.py`
Replace the hardcoded `"111111"` check with real OTP generation (random code, short expiry, stored server-side — cache or a small DB-backed model, not a bare constant) and real verification against the stored value. For actual delivery, wire Brevo SMS (`BREVO_API_KEY` is already a declared env var in `backend/.env.example`; Brevo supports SMS send via API) rather than leaving it a TODO. Keep a dev-only bypass *only* when `settings.DEBUG` is explicitly `True` — never unconditional.

Also fix `consumer/views.py`'s `_auth_phone`: stop treating an unverified `Authorization: Bearer <x>` value as a phone number directly — require and properly decode/verify a real JWT (SimpleJWT is already a dependency and already used by `verify_otp`'s issuance path).

### 5. [Critical] PayHero webhook has zero verification — `backend/payments/views.py`
Same root fix as solera's #1: use PayHero's own status-check API server-side to confirm a transaction before marking an order paid, rather than trusting the POST body. Keep both apps' webhook-verification logic consistent since they share one PayHero account.

### 6. [High] `render.yaml` still provisions Postgres; code can't use it
Rewrite `render.yaml`: remove the `databases:` block and the `DATABASE_URL: fromDatabase` wiring; set `TURSO_DATABASE_URL`/`TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN` as `sync: false` secrets instead, matching what `base.py`/`prod.py` already parse. Fix `backend/common/tenancy.py`'s docstring (currently claims "Render Postgres") to match the Turso-only reality already implemented in `base.py`/`prod.py`/`dev.py`/`requirements.txt`. Fix `backend/.env.example` to drop the contradictory `SOLERA0_DB_*`/`postgres://` example block.

Consolidate the two contradictory runbooks: `DEPLOY_TURSO.md` is already correct — keep it as the one deployment doc. Replace `RENDER_SETUP.md`'s content with a short note pointing to `DEPLOY_TURSO.md`, rather than leaving two documents that actively disagree.

### 7. [High] CORS domain typo — `render.yaml`
`CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS: "https://solera0.vercel.app"` → `"https://solerao.vercel.app"` (the real live domain, confirmed via `vercel project inspect`).

### 8. [High] Marketplace search never wired to a URL — `backend/marketplace/urls.py`
Currently `urlpatterns = []`. Add the actual route(s) for the existing, fully-written `search()` view in `views.py`.

### 9. [Medium] `create_client_sync` called two incompatible ways
`tenancy.py` calls it with a single dict; `tenant_writer.py` calls it with keyword args (`url=`, `auth_token=`) — the real `libsql_client` signature. Fix `tenancy.py` to match the correct keyword-argument form used in `tenant_writer.py`.

### Validation
`python manage.py check`, `python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` (confirms no model/migration drift introduced by any of the above), and a syntax/import pass across touched files. A real Turso connection can't be exercised without live credentials (the project's own July 25 commit message notes libsql hangs in this sandbox) — noted as a known limitation, not skipped silently.

---

## `solera0` — frontend fixes

### 10. [High] Frontend can't reach the backend even when deployed — architecture fix, not a patch
Currently: `src/lib/env.ts` falls back to `http://localhost:8000` baked into the production bundle, *and* `next.config.ts`'s CSP `connect-src` doesn't whitelist any backend origin even if the URL were set — two independent breaks.

Better fix than patching the CSP allowlist: add a `rewrites()` block in `next.config.ts` that proxies `/api/pharmacies/*`, `/api/marketplace/*`, `/api/consumer/*`, `/api/auth/*` (the real Django paths, confirmed from `src/lib/api.ts`) to the backend host via a **server-only** env var (e.g. `SOLERA0_API_URL`, not `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`). This means the browser only ever calls same-origin `/api/*` — no CORS needed, no CSP whitelist needed, and the backend URL is never exposed client-side. Update `src/lib/api.ts`/`env.ts` to call the same-origin path instead of resolving a public backend URL directly.

### 11. [Medium] Never rebranded — `package.json`, `package-lock.json`
`"name": "solera"` → `"name": "solera0"` in both.

### 12. [Medium] `vercel.json` disagrees with live deployment reality
Declares `"framework": "nextjs"` but the live Vercel project shows "Other." Will check `vercel.json`'s actual settings against the project's Root Directory/build config during implementation and correct whichever is wrong — flagging this one as verify-then-fix rather than a known-exact diff, since the live-project side of this needs checking via the Vercel MCP tools at implementation time.

---

## New feature: connect solera's tenants into solera0's Pharmacy directory

### 13. `backend/pharmacies/management/commands/sync_solera_tenants.py`
New Django management command, following the existing pattern in `seed_demo_pharmacy.py`:
- Connects to solera's real `solera-metadata` Turso DB (same `TURSO_DATABASE_URL` both apps already share) and reads the `tenants` table directly.
- For each tenant not already represented (matched by a `solera_tenant_id` field — added to the `Pharmacy` model — against solera's real tenant `id`), creates a `Pharmacy` row. The tenant's `db_url` and `db_token_encrypted` are copied **directly** from solera's `tenants` table — both apps share the same `ENCRYPTION_KEY` per the existing architecture, so the ciphertext is usable as-is without decrypt/re-encrypt.
- Creates a matching `PharmacyDirectory` row (name from the tenant; city/address left blank where solera's metadata schema doesn't carry them — not invented).
- Creates `ConsumerSettings` with `is_public=False` (per the confirmed decision).
- Idempotent — safe to re-run; skips tenants already synced.

This directly answers "why aren't the pharmacies connected": after this, running the command against real production credentials (a step the user triggers, not run automatically here) would create the missing `Pharmacy`/`ConsumerSettings` rows for Wanjiku/Mwangi/Muritu Pharmacy — still private until explicitly published, exactly matching the existing manual-approval model's own intent, just no longer requiring hand-typed credential re-entry.

### Migration
A small migration for `pharmacies` app adding `solera_tenant_id` to `Pharmacy`.

---

## Verification, end to end

- `solera`: `npm install && npx tsc --noEmit && npm test && npm run build`, all green, before the single commit to `main`.
- `solera0` backend: `python manage.py check`, `makemigrations --check --dry-run`, review the sync command's SQL/logic carefully since it can't be run against live Turso in this sandbox.
- `solera0` frontend: `npm install && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build` — confirms the `next.config.ts` rewrite doesn't break the build and no CSP regression.
- Report exactly which of the audit's Critical/High/Medium findings were fixed, which frontend/backend commits touched, and re-state the deferred `GAPS.md` backlog clearly as follow-up, not silently dropped.

## Follow-up backlog (not touched in this pass)

From `docs/GAPS.md`, explicitly carried forward, not silently dropped: email verification enforcement, password-reset flow, real audit-log writes, offline-first PWA (`idb`/Serwist), onboarding race-condition locking, orphaned-tenant-DB rollback on failed provisioning, session/token blocklist on deactivation, explicit CSRF/origin checks, Vercel preview-env Turso-key separation, inventory/POS/prescriptions/patients functional gaps (edit flows, receipt printing, shift management, dispense workflow), multi-branch enforcement, real dashboard KPI computation, plan selection at onboarding, and the PPB/ODPC/NHIF/KRA compliance integrations.

- Use `get_project_url` and `get_publishable_api_key` when helping users configure client-side integrations

- Rely on the MCP tools directly for all Supabase interactions
- Use `apply_migration` carefully, as changes go directly to the remote project

content.content:
"""Connect Solera's real tenants into Solera.0's Pharmacy directory.

Answers the standing gap: Solera's tenants table and Solera.0's Pharmacy model have no
automatic link — the only wiring that existed before this command was the fully manual
apply()/approve() admin flow (pharmacies/views.py), which requires hand-typing a tenant's
Turso credentials into an API call. Nobody had run that flow for any of Solera's existing
tenants, so none of them showed up here.

This command reads Solera's tenants table directly (same TURSO_DATABASE_URL both apps
already share) and creates the matching Pharmacy/PharmacyDirectory/ConsumerSettings rows,
copying db_url and db_token_encrypted AS-IS — both apps share the same ENCRYPTION_KEY, so
the ciphertext is valid without decrypt/re-encrypt.

Every synced pharmacy is created PRIVATE (ConsumerSettings.is_public=False), matching the
existing approve() flow's own default and the documented PPB-verification gate. Nothing
becomes publicly searchable by running this command — that's a deliberate, separate,
per-pharmacy action.

Idempotent: matches on Pharmacy.tenant_id (Solera's real tenant id), safe to re-run as new
tenants sign up on Solera.

Run: python manage.py sync_solera_tenants
"""
import time

from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand

from common.tenancy import get_metadata_client, tenant_query
from pharmacies.models import Pharmacy, PharmacyDirectory, ConsumerSettings


class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = "Create Pharmacy/ConsumerSettings rows for every existing Solera tenant (private by default)."

    def handle(self, *args, **opts):
        client = get_metadata_client()
        try:
            rows = tenant_query(
                client,
                "SELECT id, name, slug, db_url, db_token_encrypted, status, created_at FROM tenants",
            )
        finally:
            close = getattr(client, "close", None)
            if callable(close):
                close()

        created_count = 0
        skipped_count = 0
        now = int(time.time() * 1000)

        for row in rows:
            tenant_id = row["id"]
            existing = Pharmacy.objects.filter(tenant_id=tenant_id).first()
            if existing:
                skipped_count += 1
                self.stdout.write(f"skip (already synced): {row['name']} ({tenant_id})")
                continue

            # Plan intentionally left unset: Solera's plan_id is a foreign key into its own

"""Connect Solera's real tenants into Solera.0's Pharmacy directory.

Answers the standing gap: Solera's tenants table and Solera.0's Pharmacy model have no
automatic link — the only wiring that existed before this command was the fully manual
apply()/approve() admin flow (pharmacies/views.py), which requires hand-typing a tenant's
Turso credentials into an API call. Nobody had run that flow for any of Solera's existing
tenants, so none of them showed up here.

This command reads Solera's tenants table directly (same TURSO_DATABASE_URL both apps
already share) and creates the matching Pharmacy/PharmacyDirectory/ConsumerSettings rows,
copying db_url and db_token_encrypted AS-IS — both apps share the same ENCRYPTION_KEY, so
the ciphertext is valid without decrypt/re-encrypt.

Every synced pharmacy is created PRIVATE (ConsumerSettings.is_public=False), matching the
existing approve() flow's own default and the documented PPB-verification gate. Nothing
becomes publicly searchable by running this command — that's a deliberate, separate,
per-pharmacy action.

Idempotent: matches on Pharmacy.tenant_id (Solera's real tenant id), safe to re-run as new
tenants sign up on Solera.

Run: python manage.py sync_solera_tenants
"""
import time

from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand

from common.tenancy import get_metadata_client, tenant_query
from pharmacies.models import Pharmacy, PharmacyDirectory, ConsumerSettings


class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = "Create Pharmacy/ConsumerSettings rows for every existing Solera tenant (private by default)."

    def handle(self, *args, **opts):
        client = get_metadata_client()
        try:
            rows = tenant_query(
                client,
                "SELECT id, name, slug, db_url, db_token_encrypted, status, created_at FROM tenants",
            )
        finally:
            close = getattr(client, "close", None)
            if callable(close):
                close()

        created_count = 0
        skipped_count = 0
        now = int(time.time() * 1000)

        for row in rows:
            tenant_id = row["id"]
            existing = Pharmacy.objects.filter(tenant_id=tenant_id).first()
            if existing:
                skipped_count += 1
                self.stdout.write(f"skip (already synced): {row['name']} ({tenant_id})")
                continue

            # Plan intentionally left unset: Solera's plan_id is a foreign key into its own
            # plans table, whose contents this command doesn't assume or invent a mapping
            # for. Set Pharmacy.plan by hand afterward if you want it reflected here.
            pharmacy = Pharmacy.objects.create(
                tenant_id=tenant_id,
                name=row["name"],
                slug=row["slug"],
                turso_db_url=row["db_url"],
                db_token_encrypted=row["db_token_encrypted"],
                status=row.get("status") or "active",
                created_at=row.get("created_at") or now,
            )
            PharmacyDirectory.objects.create(
                pharmacy=pharmacy,

                # Solera's tenants table doesn't carry city/address — left blank rather
                # than guessed; fill in via the Django admin once known.
                is_verified=False,
                is_active=True,
                created_at=now,
            )
            ConsumerSettings.objects.create(
                pharmacy=pharmacy,
                is_public=False,
                display_name=row["name"],
                created_at=now,
                updated_at=now,
            )
            created_count += 1
            self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS(f"synced (private): {row['name']} ({tenant_id})"))

        self.stdout.write(
            self.style.SUCCESS(f"Done. {created_count} synced, {skipped_count} already present.")
        )

30	  webpack: (config) => {
31	    config.resolve.alias = {
32	      ...config.resolve.alias,

35	    return config;

42	  // SOLERA0_API_URL — a server-only env var, never exposed to the browser. This means:
43	  //  - the browser only ever calls same-origin /api/*, so no CORS setup is needed on
44	  //    Django and the CSP connect-src above never needs to list an external backend host
45	  //  - the backend's real URL is never present in client-side JS at all
46	  // NOTE: deliberately does NOT touch /api/auth/* — that path is already owned by the
47	  // inherited NextAuth catch-all route (src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts), which

1	# Solera & Solera0 — Complete Repository, Deployment, Database & History Audit
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-08-22
4	**Purpose of this revision:** the first version of this audit summarized findings without showing the evidence behind them, which meant it wasn't verifiable by anyone without access to the repos, the Vercel projects, or the Turso databases. This version is written to be **fully self-contained** — every finding is backed by an actual code excerpt, actual commit hash, or actual query result quoted inline, so a reader with none of those accounts can still follow the reasoning and check it against what's quoted here.
5	
6	**Method:** Both repos were cloned in full (not just API-sampled) specifically to do proper `git log`/`git show` history forensics. All 588 non-binary source files across both repos were read in full (excludes ~400 screenshot/logo/icon binary files, which aren't meaningful to "read" as code). Live Vercel deployments were hit directly. Live Turso databases were queried directly. Nothing here is taken from either repo's own documentation (`EXECUTIVE_REPORT.md`, `README.md`, `GAPS.md`, etc.) without being independently checked against the actual code — where a document's claim couldn't be independently re-verified in this pass, that is stated explicitly rather than assumed either way.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## Table of contents
11	
12	1. [What these two repos are, in one paragraph each](#1-what-these-two-repos-are)
13	2. [How the project actually evolved — from real commit history](#2-how-the-project-actually-evolved)
14	3. [How the system works, end to end](#3-how-the-system-works-end-to-end)
15	4. [Findings — Critical](#4-findings--critical)
16	5. [Findings — High](#5-findings--high)
17	6. [Findings — Medium](#6-findings--medium)
18	7. [Findings — Low](#7-findings--low)
19	8. [Confirmed genuinely solid](#8-confirmed-genuinely-solid)
20	9. [Gaps — what's documented as missing, and what that status actually is today](#9-gaps)
21	10. [The data that actually exists right now](#10-the-data-that-actually-exists-right-now)
22	11. [Live deployment status](#11-live-deployment-status)
23	12. [What this audit did not cover](#12-what-this-audit-did-not-cover)
24	13. [Bottom line](#13-bottom-line)
25	
26	---
27	
28	## 1. What these two repos are
29	
30	**`solera`** (`github.com/ken-muritu/solera`, private, created 2026-06-21) is a real, actively-developed, currently-live multi-tenant SaaS for pharmacies and clinics in Kenya. One Next.js 16 app, one Turso (SQLite-over-HTTP) database per tenant pharmacy plus one shared metadata database, Drizzle as the ORM. It has a real dashboard (POS, inventory, prescriptions, patients, clinic visits, billing, team messaging, reports), real M-Pesa payment integration via PayHero, and real (if small) paying-adjacent tenant data in it today. 74 commits, June 21 – July 23, 2026.
31	
32	**`solera0`** (`github.com/ken-muritu/solera0`, private, created 2026-07-25) is a one-day, 15-commit exploration built four weeks later, in a single ~7-hour session. It started by copying `solera`'s entire Next.js frontend verbatim, then bolted on a brand-new Django backend meant to add a consumer-facing marketplace (search pharmacy stock, order, pay, pick up) on top of the pharmacies already running `solera`. It explicitly reuses `solera`'s Turso instance and PayHero account rather than standing up separate infrastructure.
33	
34	They are not two versions of the same app. They are two different products, built a month apart, sharing a database, a payment account, and (per config) an encryption key.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## 2. How the project actually evolved
39	
40	This section is built directly from `git log --shortstat` and `git show` on both repos' full histories (74 + 15 = 89 commits), not from either repo's own README narrative.
41

84	### `solera` — real architecture, confirmed by reading the code
85	
86	```
87	solera/
88	├── src/app/(app)/        ← authenticated pharmacy dashboard: pos, inventory,
89	│                            prescriptions, patients, clinic, reports, settings,
90	│                            admin, messages, account
91	├── src/app/(auth)/       ← login, signup, forgot/reset password, verify-email,
92	│                            accept-invite
93	├── src/app/api/          ← auth[nextauth], payhero/callback, mpesa/callback,
94	│                            payments/status, messages/*, admin/tenants, sync,
95	│                            vendo/[...vendo]
96	├── src/components/       ← pos, dashboard, messages, settings, admin, auth, ui
97	├── src/lib/               ← billing, payments, compliance, offline, sync,
98	│                            messages, stream, phi.ts (encryption), crypto.ts,
99	│                            rate-limit.ts, actions/*
100	├── src/db/schema/         ← Drizzle schema: metadata DB + per-tenant DB
101	└── src/vendo/registry.tsx ← AI-agent tool registry (installed, empty — see §9)
102	```
103	
104	**Data model:** one Turso database (`solera-metadata`) holds the platform registry — `tenants`, `global_users`, `subscriptions`, `plans`, `audit_logs`, etc. Each pharmacy tenant gets its **own separate Turso database** (`solera-<slug>-<id>`), holding its actual inventory, sales, patients, prescriptions. The metadata DB's `tenants` table stores each tenant's DB URL and an **AES-256-GCM-encrypted** access token for that tenant's own database — confirmed by directly querying the live table (§10) and reading the actual ciphertext format.
105	
106	**Payments:** PayHero (an M-Pesa payment gateway for Kenya) posts webhooks to `/api/payhero/callback`, verified (with the flaw documented in §4) by `src/lib/payhero-webhook.ts`, then processed by `src/lib/payments/confirm-sale.ts` or `src/lib/billing/payhero.ts` depending on whether it's a POS sale or a subscription payment.
107	
108	**Messaging:** a real, custom-built system — SSE streaming (`api/messages/stream`), presence, typing indicators, WhatsApp-style read receipts, tickets — is the one actually wired into the UI (`messages-client.tsx`). A second messaging integration, Stream Chat, is installed as a dependency with a working, RBAC-checked token endpoint, but per the project's own `docs/GETSTREAM.md`, was never connected to any UI (§9).

200	### 4.3 `solera` (the live product): the payment webhook's fallback is forgeable
201	
202	Current `src/lib/payhero-webhook.ts`:
203	
204	```typescript
205	export function isPayHeroCallbackPayload(body: Record<string, unknown>): boolean {
206	  const response = (body.response ?? body) as Record<string, unknown>;
207	  return !!(
208	    response.ExternalReference ??
209	    response.external_reference ??
210	    response.CheckoutRequestID ??
211	    response.checkout_request_id
212	  );
213	}
214	
215	export function verifyPayHeroCallback(
216	  req: Request,
217	  options?: { body?: Record<string, unknown> },
218	): boolean {
219	  const secret = process.env.PAYHERO_CALLBACK_SECRET;
220	  if (!secret) return process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production";
221	
222	  const headerToken = /* ...reads x-payhero-signature / x-callback-secret / authorization... */ null;
223	  if (secretsMatch(headerToken, secret)) return true;
224	
225	  const queryToken = new URL(req.url).searchParams.get("secret");
226	  if (secretsMatch(queryToken, secret)) return true;
227	
228	  if (options?.body && isPayHeroCallbackPayload(options.body)) return true;  // <- no secret checked here at all
229	
230	  return false;
231	}
232	```
233	
234	If the header check and the query-secret check both fail, `isPayHeroCallbackPayload()` accepts the request purely because the body has the *shape* of a real PayHero payload — no secret, no signature. Sale references are constructed as `SALE-<tenantId.slice(0,8)>-<receiptNumber>` (`src/lib/payments/reference.ts`) — an 8-character tenant-ID prefix and a receipt number, both discoverable. `src/lib/payhero-webhook.test.ts` exists and covers `verifyPayHeroCallback`, but calls it with a different argument signature than the real call site (`src/app/api/payhero/callback/route.ts`) uses — so this path has never actually been exercised by the test. This is compounded by:

236	```yaml

238	```
239	
240	The 5-file test suite (RBAC, this webhook, PayHero status, receipt status, theme utils) has never run in CI, confirmed by reading the workflow file directly — there is no `npm test` (or equivalent) step anywhere in it.

249	
250	```python
251	def _parse_db_url(url):
252	    if not url:
253	        return {"ENGINE": "django.db.backends.sqlite3", "NAME": str(BASE_DIR / "solera0_platform.sqlite3")}
254	    if url.startswith("sqlite"):
255	        path = url.replace("sqlite:///", "").replace("sqlite://", "")
256	        return {"ENGINE": "django.db.backends.sqlite3", "NAME": path or str(BASE_DIR / "solera0_platform.sqlite3")}
257	    if url.startswith("libsql"):
258	        return {"ENGINE": "django_libsql", "NAME": url}
259	    return {"ENGINE": "django.db.backends.sqlite3", "NAME": str(BASE_DIR / "solera0_platform.sqlite3")}  # <- postgres:// lands here
