Use Claude Code with OpenRouter

Claude Code with OpenRouter is only guaranteed to work with the Anthropic first-party provider. For maximum compatibility, we recommend setting Anthropic 1P as top priority provider when using Claude Code.
​
Why Use OpenRouter with Claude Code?
OpenRouter adds a reliability and management layer between Claude Code and Anthropic’s API, giving you and your organization several key benefits.
​
Provider Failover for High Availability
Anthropic’s API occasionally experiences outages or rate limiting. When you route Claude Code through OpenRouter, your requests automatically fail over between multiple Anthropic providers. If one provider is unavailable or rate-limited, OpenRouter seamlessly routes to another, keeping your coding sessions uninterrupted.
​
Organizational Budget Controls
For teams and organizations, OpenRouter provides centralized budget management. You can set spending limits, allocate credits across team members, and prevent unexpected cost overruns. This is especially valuable when multiple developers are using Claude Code across your organization.
​
Usage Visibility and Analytics
OpenRouter gives you complete visibility into how Claude Code is being used across your team. Track usage patterns, monitor costs in real-time, and understand which projects or team members are consuming the most resources. All of this data is available in your OpenRouter Activity Dashboard.
​
Quick Start
This guide will get you running Claude Code powered by OpenRouter in just a few minutes.
​
Step 1: Install Claude Code
Native Install (Recommended)
npm
macOS, Linux, WSL:
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
Windows PowerShell:
irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex
​
Step 2: Connect Claude to OpenRouter
Instead of logging in with Anthropic directly, connect Claude Code to OpenRouter. This requires setting a few environment variables.
Requirements:
Use the full OpenRouter API URL, including the scheme: https://openrouter.ai/api
Provide your OpenRouter API key as ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
Important: Explicitly blank out ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to prevent conflicts
Why ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN: OpenRouter is an LLM gateway that authenticates requests with a bearer token, and Claude Code sends ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN as Authorization: Bearer <token> — the credential variable Anthropic documents for bearer-authenticated gateways. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is instead sent as x-api-key, is treated as a direct-Anthropic credential, and prompts you once in interactive mode to approve it over a saved login. Setting it to an empty string keeps Claude Code from falling back to authenticating against Anthropic directly.
Shell Profile
Project Settings File
Add these environment variables to your shell profile:
# Open your shell profile in nano
nano ~/.zshrc  # or ~/.bashrc for Bash users

# Add these lines to the file:
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="<your-openrouter-api-key>"
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://openrouter.ai/api"
export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="$OPENROUTER_API_KEY"
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="" # Important: Must be explicitly empty
export CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1 # Optional: enables the gateway model picker
Then reload your shell so the new values are live — otherwise you will keep testing the old environment and conclude the configuration does not work:
source ~/.zshrc  # or ~/.bashrc, or open a new terminal
Persistence: We recommend adding these lines to your shell profile (~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, or ~/.config/fish/config.fish).
Ordering matters: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="$OPENROUTER_API_KEY" is expanded when the profile is sourced. If OPENROUTER_API_KEY is defined later in the file, in a different file, or injected by a secrets manager after your profile runs, the auth token expands to an empty string and every request fails with an auth error. Ensure the key is defined before it is consumed by ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, or put it in a file that loads earlier (e.g. ~/.zshenv for zsh).
Secret hygiene: This puts a plaintext API key in your shell profile — a file that is easy to accidentally commit to a dotfiles repo or paste into a gist. Consider loading the key from your OS keychain instead, e.g. on macOS: export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="$(security find-generic-password -s openrouter -w)". If a key does leak, revoke and rotate it at openrouter.ai/settings/keys.
Variable Location: Do not put these in a project-level .env file. The native Claude Code installer does not read standard .env files.
​
Step 3: Clear any cached Anthropic login
If you were previously logged in to Claude Code with an Anthropic account, you must run /logout once to remove the cached session. Claude Code warns about auth conflicts when both a cached login and a gateway credential are present, and the conflict can cause unexpected behaviour on startup — typically surfacing as confusing model-not-found errors (e.g. for openrouter/auto, openrouter/pareto-code, or any other OpenRouter-only model).
> /logout
Then quit and re-launch claude so it picks up the new environment variables.
If you have never logged in to Claude Code with Anthropic, you can skip this step.
Where the cached login lives: On macOS the cached session is stored in the Keychain as a generic password named Claude Code-credentials (native installs do not write ~/.claude/.credentials.json). If you are debugging a stubborn auth conflict, you can confirm a stale session exists with:
security find-generic-password -s "Claude Code-credentials"
If it prints an entry after /logout, delete it with security delete-generic-password -s "Claude Code-credentials" and relaunch claude.
​
Step 4: Start your session
Navigate to your project directory and start Claude Code:
cd /path/to/your/project
claude
You are now connected! Any prompt you send will be routed through OpenRouter.
​
Step 5: Verify
You can confirm your connection by running the /status command inside Claude Code.
> /status
Auth token: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
Anthropic base URL: https://openrouter.ai/api
If the Auth token line names ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, or a Login method line names a Claude account instead, the environment did not reach the session — reload your shell and relaunch claude.
You can also check the OpenRouter Activity Dashboard to see your requests appearing in real-time.
​
How It Works
OpenRouter exposes an input that is compatible with the Anthropic Messages API.
Direct Connection: When you set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to https://openrouter.ai/api, Claude Code speaks its native protocol directly to OpenRouter. No local proxy server is required.
Anthropic Skin: OpenRouter’s “Anthropic Skin” behaves exactly like the Anthropic API. It handles model mapping and passes through advanced features like “Thinking” blocks and native tool use.
Billing: You are billed using your OpenRouter credits. Usage (including reasoning tokens) appears in your OpenRouter dashboard.
​
Configuring Models
Claude Code uses several environment variables to determine which models to use for different tasks. You can override these to route each role through a specific model:
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL="~anthropic/claude-fable-latest"
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL="~anthropic/claude-opus-latest"
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL="~anthropic/claude-sonnet-latest"
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL="~anthropic/claude-haiku-latest"
export CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL="~anthropic/claude-opus-latest"
Variable    Description
ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL    The model used for Fable-class tasks (the most demanding reasoning and long-horizon work)
ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL    The model used for Opus-class tasks (e.g. complex reasoning)
ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL    The model used for Sonnet-class tasks (e.g. general coding)
ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL    The model used for Haiku-class tasks (e.g. quick completions)
CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL    The model used for sub-agent tasks spawned by Claude Code
Claude Code 2.1.x added Fable as a fourth model class. When Claude Code points at OpenRouter, Fable is not offered in /model by default — setting ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL is the only way to make it selectable.
After setting the overrides, open /model inside Claude Code to confirm every model class you expect is listed, and check the model column in your Activity Dashboard to confirm requests route to the models you configured.
Add these to the same shell profile or project settings file where you set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN.
Claude Code is optimized for Anthropic models and may not work correctly with other providers.
​
Gateway model picker
Gateway model discovery is opt-in. Set CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1 to show the model picker. The picker shows a curated set of the highest-ranked models, not the full OpenRouter catalog. Some picker entries route to non-Anthropic providers and may be subject to the compatibility limitations noted above. Pinning a model with one of the settings above selects it directly and bypasses the picker. Claude Code stores the discovered list locally and refreshes it during startup, so restart Claude Code after enabling discovery or when you want it to fetch the list again.
​
Fast Mode
Anthropic’s fast mode provides up to 2.5x faster output at premium pricing. Fast mode is only available on Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Opus 4.8, and Claude Opus 5 — no other Anthropic models support it.
For each supported Opus version, there are three ways to request fast mode on OpenRouter:
Send speed: "fast" with anthropic/claude-opus-5, anthropic/claude-opus-4.8, anthropic/claude-opus-4.7, or anthropic/claude-opus-4.6 — OpenRouter reroutes the request to the matching *-fast model (for example, anthropic/claude-opus-5 → anthropic/claude-opus-5-fast).
Call the *-fast model directly — anthropic/claude-opus-5-fast, anthropic/claude-opus-4.8-fast, anthropic/claude-opus-4.7-fast, or anthropic/claude-opus-4.6-fast.
Send service_tier: "fast" or service_tier: "priority" — fully interchangeable with speed: "fast" on all APIs (see Fast mode). All three spellings also request the priority service tier (including its provider sorting and pricing) where available.
All options route through the Anthropic first-party provider, and the required beta header is injected automatically.
​
Using /fast in Claude Code
Claude Code has a built-in /fast command that toggles fast mode. When enabled, Claude Code sends speed: "fast" in its requests alongside the configured Opus model. OpenRouter fully supports this parameter — you just need to set the following environment variable:
export CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_FAST_MODE_ORG_CHECK=1
Requires Claude Code v2.1.96 or newer.
Claude Code only attaches speed: "fast" when the resolved model ID matches a supported Opus version (e.g. anthropic/claude-opus-5). With ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL set to the ~anthropic/claude-opus-latest alias — including the example in Configuring Models above — /fast reports “Fast mode ON” but requests are sent without the speed parameter: standard speed, standard pricing. To actually use fast mode, pin the variable to a specific Opus ID such as anthropic/claude-opus-5.
​
Pricing
Fast mode is priced at a premium over the underlying Claude Opus model’s standard token rates. See Anthropic’s fast mode pricing for current rates. When fast mode is active, the response’s usage object includes "speed": "fast" to confirm the request was processed at the higher speed tier.
If speed: "fast" is sent for a model that does not support fast mode, it still requests the priority service tier where a provider offers one (at priority pricing); otherwise the request proceeds at standard speed with standard pricing. Claude Fable has no fast tier — toggling /fast while on a Fable model does not speed Fable up. Instead, Claude Code switches your session to your configured Opus model, so subsequent requests run (and bill) on Opus rather than Fable.
​
Routing behavior
Fast mode is only served by the Anthropic first-party provider, since other providers (e.g. Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex) do not support it.
​
Agent SDK
The Anthropic Agent SDK lets you build AI agents programmatically using Python or TypeScript. Since the Agent SDK uses Claude Code as its runtime, you can connect it to OpenRouter using the same environment variables described above.
For complete setup instructions and code examples, see our Anthropic Agent SDK integration guide.
​
GitHub Action
You can use OpenRouter with the official Claude Code GitHub Action.To adapt the example workflow for OpenRouter, make two changes to the action step:
Pass your OpenRouter API key via anthropic_api_key (store it as a GitHub secret named OPENROUTER_API_KEY)
Set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to https://openrouter.ai/api and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN to the same secret in the step’s env block
- name: Run Claude Code
  uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
  with:
    anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
  env:
    ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: https://openrouter.ai/api
    ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
The action requires the anthropic_api_key input before it will launch Claude Code and does not read ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN itself, so the input satisfies that launch check while the environment variable is what puts the key in the Authorization header. Unlike the local setup, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not empty here — the action populates it from the input — which is fine because the run is non-interactive and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL still routes every request to OpenRouter.
​
Cost Tracking Statusline
You can add a custom statusline to Claude Code that tracks your OpenRouter API costs in real-time. The statusline displays the provider, model, cumulative cost, and cache discounts for your session.

Download the statusline scripts from the openrouter-examples repository, make them executable, and add the following to your ~/.claude/settings.json:
{
  "statusLine": {
    "type": "command",
    "command": "/path/to/statusline.sh"
  }
}
The script reads ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, falling back to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, so it picks up the OpenRouter key you set in the setup above.
A few practical notes:
Prerequisites: statusline.sh is a thin wrapper that runs npx tsx statusline.ts, so it requires Node.js and network access on first render (npx downloads tsx on first use, which can make the first refresh slow). Download both files and keep them in the same directory.
Only one statusline: settings.json supports a single statusLine entry. If you already use another statusline (e.g. ccusage or a tool-provided one), adding this one replaces it — they cannot be combined without writing a wrapper script that merges their output.
API usage: Each refresh makes one request to the generation endpoint per new generation in the session. Long sessions catch up incrementally; costs shown are cumulative for the current session.
State files: Per-session state accumulates at /tmp/claude-openrouter-cost-<session-id>.json. These are small and cleared on OS reboot on most systems, but you can delete them at any time.
​
Troubleshooting
Model-not-found errors for OpenRouter models (e.g. openrouter/auto, openrouter/pareto-code): Usually caused by a credential conflict that surfaces as auth-conflict warnings on startup. There are two distinct scenarios. (1) If you have a cached Anthropic OAuth login from before switching to OpenRouter, run /logout inside Claude Code, then quit and re-launch claude to clear the cached session. (2) If your shell profile still has a real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set (e.g. an old Anthropic console key), /logout will not help — it only clears the cached OAuth session, not shell environment variables. Instead, ensure ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="" is set in your shell profile per Step 2, then reload your shell. Verify with /status that the auth token is ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and the base URL is https://openrouter.ai/api.
Auth Errors: Ensure your OpenRouter key is in ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and that ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is an empty string (""). If ANTHROPIC_API_KEY holds a real Anthropic key, Claude Code sends it as x-api-key and may authenticate against Anthropic instead. Reload your shell after editing your profile, and if you still see auth errors, run /logout (see above).
Context Length Errors: If you hit context limits, consider breaking your task into smaller chunks or starting a new session.
Privacy: OpenRouter does not log your source code prompts unless you explicitly opt-in to prompt logging in your account settings. See our Privacy Policy for details.

**Bottom line: it works.** With the corrected setup, `stealth/ox-alpha` replied for real through Claude Code's own protocol:

```
claude -p "reply with just the word OK, then name yourself" --model stealth/ox-alpha
→ OK — I'm ox-alpha, developed by an undisclosed organization.
```

(The Hermes background test failed separately — "empty content after retries" — unrelated, don't need to chase that if this path works.)

**What was actually wrong before**, confirmed by the docs you pasted:
1. Base URL must be `https://openrouter.ai/api` — **no `/v1`**. We had `/v1` appended, which is wrong for Claude Code specifically (their SDK/curl examples use `/v1`, but the Claude-Code integration uses the bare `/api` "Anthropic Skin" endpoint).
2. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` must be explicitly set to `""`. Your machine has a real, cached Anthropic Pro OAuth login — Claude Code prefers that over the gateway token whenever both are present, which is exactly why it kept saying "model not found": it wasn't even talking to OpenRouter, it was going straight to Anthropic and Anthropic obviously doesn't know a model called `stealth/ox-alpha`.

**To set this up permanently on your machine**, add to `~/.bashrc`:

```bash
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="sk-or-v1-..."
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://openrouter.ai/api"
export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="$OPENROUTER_API_KEY"
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=""
export CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1
```

Then `source ~/.bashrc` (or open a new terminal), run `/logout` inside any running `claude` session to drop the cached OAuth, relaunch `claude`, and verify with `/status` — it should show `Auth token: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` and `Anthropic base URL: https://openrouter.ai/api`.

**Important trade-off, since you want this as your daily driver:** this is systemwide — as long as those env vars are exported, *every* `claude` session in that shell (this local project work included) routes through OpenRouter/ox-alpha instead of real Anthropic, using your OpenRouter credits/free-tier instead of your Pro subscription. If you want both available, I'd suggest **not** putting this in `~/.bashrc` — instead wrap it in a shell function/alias (e.g. `claude-or`) so plain `claude` still uses your Pro login by default, and you opt into ox-alpha deliberately. Want me to set that up instead of the always-on version?

content.content:
1	# Emotional Intelligence
2	## A Teaching Series by Pastor Charles Muchemi
3	### Royal Priesthood Embassy · Sunday Services
4	**A Three-Part Series**
5	
6	---
7	
8	> *"He who is slow to anger is better than the mighty, and he who rules his spirit than he who takes a city."*
9	> — Proverbs 16:32 (NKJV)
10	
11	> *"If someone says, 'I love God,' and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who does not love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen?"*
12	> — 1 John 4:20 (NKJV)
13	
14	---
15	
16	## A Note Before We Begin
17	
18	Today I have an interesting subject that we shall be covering, and I guarantee you I am not going to finish this today — I am just going to start. So you must be very careful, because we will be studying the topic: emotional intelligence.
19	
20	There's a time in the recent past when I promised to do this, and I just realized this particular week that it is time for us to explore and understand what exactly it means to be emotionally intelligent — because it is very easy for you to be intelligent spiritually, yet you are not intelligent emotionally.
21	
22	When I was posting about this meeting, I wrote something I heard from my father, the Lord. One time he was teaching, and he said that people who are emotionally intelligent end up ruling over people who have a strong IQ and a weak emotional quotient. And I can guarantee you, over time I have verified that statement. I have confirmed that it is true. There is still something that will put a sharp, intelligent person at a disadvantage if they do not master it — and that thing is emotional intelligence.
23	
24	---
25	
26	# PART 1: Believer or Christian? Why Character Reveals the Master You Serve
27	
28	### First Sunday
29	
30	## Called to Represent, Not Just to Believe
31	
32	Just to lay a good foundation for where we are going with this topic — I want you to look at your life and begin to identify the things that can make people scared away from desiring your God. I know I am talking to believers. Most of you love God. But check the things in your life that may make your friends, your family, not desire your God. Because I guarantee you, most people out there have not actually had an encounter with God — but they have had an encounter with *you*. And the question is: what resulted from the encounter they had with you?
33	
34	That is exactly what God did not create us for. Because God intended that when men meet us, they meet God. That is why God does not desire that we do anything to Him that we do not do to man — that we claim to love Him yet do not love man.
35	
36	The Bible says in the book of Acts that the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch. So the question is: who were they before that, yet they had already believed in Jesus Christ?
37	
38	> *"And when he had found him, he brought him to Antioch. And it came to pass that for a whole year they assembled with the church and taught a great many people. And the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch."*
39	> — Acts 11:26 (NKJV)
40	
41	Notice — they assembled with the church, they taught a great many people, for a whole year, and *then* the disciples were first called Christians. It means these people were in the church, but they were not yet Christians. Yet they were believers. There is a difference between being a believer and being a Christian. They are not one and the same thing.
42	
43	So what is this being Christian? It is simply acting like Christ. The word "Christian" there defines a disciple, not merely a believer — because it is discipleship that made people eventually call them Christians. It is good that you have believed in Jesus Christ. It is good that you have eternal life, and we can guarantee you as a believer that you have a ticket to heaven. But while you live here on earth, will people look at you and desire your God? Will people look at you and know that Christ is your master?
44	
45	## Love Is the Proof
46	
47	I've quoted a bit of some verses already — 1 John chapter 4 and verse 20. If someone says "I love God" and hates his brother, he is a liar. There's a challenge being thrown at us here: if you want to claim that you love God, if you want us to verify that you love God, we do not believe by listening to what you say — we believe by looking into your life and finding that you love the people around you.
48	
49	> *"Therefore if you bring your gift to the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift."*
50	> — Matthew 5:23–24 (NKJV)
51	
52	God is not rejecting the fact that you have visited the altar. He is not rejecting that you have made your way there. He actually tells you to leave the gift, because He is expecting you to come back to the altar. But you being at the altar while your brother has something against you is not commendable. It is not acceptable to God.
53	
54	> *"Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal."*
55	> — 1 Corinthians 13:1 (NKJV)
56	
57	You will be at the altar, and according to you, you are saying, "Thank you, Lord, I thank you for your love toward me, I thank you because you are a good God, I thank you because when I pray, you hear me." According to you, that is what you are doing. But on the other end of heaven, what they are hearing is noise. Can you imagine a God who has the ability to hear the prayers of every person on earth — how many billions of people, how many prayers reaching Him in one minute — and He is able to hear all of them? But He separates a kind of prayer, and He says, "All I hear is noise." And that is a prayer coming from a person who does not have love.
58	
59	## The Character You Cannot Hide
60	
61	There are things in our lives that do not portray the character of Christ. I like the story about Peter. Peter promises Jesus he is not going to deny Him. Jesus tells him that before the rooster crows, he will deny Him three times.
62	
63	> *"Assuredly, I say to you that this night, before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times." Peter said to Him, "Even if I have to die with You, I will not deny You!" And so said all the disciples.*
64	> — Matthew 26:34–35 (NKJV)
65	
66	But it so happens that Peter actually denied Him. And in the process of denying Jesus, people were saying, "We saw you with him," and Peter said, "I do not even know him" — but something was selling him off. It was clear, from the way he was behaving, the way he was speaking, that he had been with Jesus.
67	
68	> *Then having arrested Him, they led Him and brought Him into the high priest's house. But Peter followed at a distance. Now when they had kindled a fire in the midst of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter sat among them. # Emotional Intelligence
## A Teaching Series by Pastor Charles Muchemi
### Royal Priesthood Embassy · Sunday Services
**A Three-Part Series**

---

> *"He who is slow to anger is better than the mighty, and he who rules his spirit than he who takes a city."*
> — Proverbs 16:32 (NKJV)

> *"If someone says, 'I love God,' and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who does not love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen?"*
> — 1 John 4:20 (NKJV)

---

## A Note Before We Begin

Today I have an interesting subject that we shall be covering, and I guarantee you I am not going to finish this today — I am just going to start. So you must be very careful, because we will be studying the topic: emotional intelligence.

There's a time in the recent past when I promised to do this, and I just realized this particular week that it is time for us to explore and understand what exactly it means to be emotionally intelligent — because it is very easy for you to be intelligent spiritually, yet you are not intelligent emotionally.

When I was posting about this meeting, I wrote something I heard from my father, the Lord. One time he was teaching, and he said that people who are emotionally intelligent end up ruling over people who have a strong IQ and a weak emotional quotient. And I can guarantee you, over time I have verified that statement. I have confirmed that it is true. There is still something that will put a sharp, intelligent person at a disadvantage if they do not master it — and that thing is emotional intelligence.

---

# PART 1: Believer or Christian? Why Character Reveals the Master You Serve

### First Sunday

## Called to Represent, Not Just to Believe

Just to lay a good foundation for where we are going with this topic — I want you to look at your life and begin to identify the things that can make people scared away from desiring your God. I know I am talking to believers. Most of you love God. But check the things in your life that may make your friends, your family, not desire your God. Because I guarantee you, most people out there have not actually had an encounter with God — but they have had an encounter with *you*. And the question is: what resulted from the encounter they had with you?

That is exactly what God did not create us for. Because God intended that when men meet us, they meet God. That is why God does not desire that we do anything to Him that we do not do to man — that we claim to love Him yet do not love man.

The Bible says in the book of Acts that the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch. So the question is: who were they before that, yet they had already believed in Jesus Christ?

> *"And when he had found him, he brought him to Antioch. And it came to pass that for a whole year they assembled with the church and taught a great many people. And the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch."*
> — Acts 11:26 (NKJV)

Notice — they assembled with the church, they taught a great many people, for a whole year, and *then* the disciples were first called Christians. It means these people were in the church, but they were not yet Christians. Yet they were believers. There is a difference between being a believer and being a Christian. They are not one and the same thing.

So what is this being Christian? It is simply acting like Christ. The word "Christian" there defines a disciple, not merely a believer — because it is discipleship that made people eventually call them Christians. It is good that you have believed in Jesus Christ. It is good that you have eternal life, and we can guarantee you as a believer that you have a ticket to heaven. But while you live here on earth, will people look at you and desire your God? Will people look at you and know that Christ is your master?

## Love Is the Proof

I've quoted a bit of some verses already — 1 John chapter 4 and verse 20. If someone says "I love God" and hates his brother, he is a liar. There's a challenge being thrown at us here: if you want to claim that you love God, if you want us to verify that you love God, we do not believe by listening to what you say — we believe by looking into your life and finding that you love the people around you.

> *"Therefore if you bring your gift to the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift."*
> — Matthew 5:23–24 (NKJV)

God is not rejecting the fact that you have visited the altar. He is not rejecting that you have made your way there. He actually tells you to leave the gift, because He is expecting you to come back to the altar. But you being at the altar while your brother has something against you is not commendable. It is not acceptable to God.

> *"Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal."*
> — 1 Corinthians 13:1 (NKJV)

You will be at the altar, and according to you, you are saying, "Thank you, Lord, I thank you for your love toward me, I thank you because you are a good God, I thank you because when I pray, you hear me." According to you, that is what you are doing. But on the other end of heaven, what they are hearing is noise. Can you imagine a God who has the ability to hear the prayers of every person on earth — how many billions of people, how many prayers reaching Him in one minute — and He is able to hear all of them? But He separates a kind of prayer, and He says, "All I hear is noise." And that is a prayer coming from a person who does not have love.

## The Character You Cannot Hide

There are things in our lives that do not portray the character of Christ. I like the story about Peter. Peter promises Jesus he is not going to deny Him. Jesus tells him that before the rooster crows, he will deny Him three times.

> *"Assuredly, I say to you that this night, before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times." Peter said to Him, "Even if I have to die with You, I will not deny You!" And so said all the disciples.*
> — Matthew 26:34–35 (NKJV)

But it so happens that Peter actually denied Him. And in the process of denying Jesus, people were saying, "We saw you with him," and Peter said, "I do not even know him" — but something was selling him off. It was clear, from the way he was behaving, the way he was speaking, that he had been with Jesus.

> *Then having arrested Him, they led Him and brought Him into the high priest's house. But Peter followed at a distance. Now when they had kindled a fire in the midst of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter sat among them. And a certain servant girl, seeing him as he sat by the fire, looked intently at him and said, "This man was also with Him." But he denied Him, saying, "Woman, I do not know Him." And after a little while another saw him and said, "You also are of them." But Peter said, "Man, I am not!" Then after about an hour had passed, another confidently affirmed, saying, "Surely this fellow also was with Him, for he is a Galilean." But Peter said, "Man, I do not know what you are saying!" Immediately, while he was still speaking, the rooster crowed.*
> — Luke 22:54–60 (NKJV)

He's trying to deny Jesus Christ, but who he is testifies of the very person he is denying. This is a blessing I want us all to receive — that when people look at us, they don't need us to even open our mouths to testify. Sometimes when they just look at you, they can see Jesus.

There is a day I was somewhere around Safari Park, just standing there, and a Buddhist guy found me and asked, "Pastor, are you going...?" I wondered — why are you calling me Pastor? I don't look like one, not even the way I'm dressed. And this wasn't the first time. I remember walking with Pastor Ryan, and someone who didn't know either of us — we weren't dressed in coats or suits — still called us pastors. I asked Pastor Ryan, "Is this man aware you are a pastor?" He told me, "No." I left testifying, and I told him: this means that if today we were the modern-day Peter, we would also be caught. We try to sit among them, and we'd be caught.

## Believers Who Do Not Look Like Christians

But now, it is also very possible for you to be a believer, going to heaven, speaking in tongues of every kind — and yet when someone looks at you, they cannot really call you a Christian. Trust me — I know people who are born again and they beat their wives. I know people who are born again and they gossip. You find, for example, two people having a very nice friendship; you enroll yourself into their friendship, and the minute you become a third friend, they are no longer friends, because instead of bringing peace, you were like a sword.

I'm not teaching this to say that I am the best. We are also looking to be perfected by God. But it's my responsibility to bring this to you: amongst ourselves, sometimes I just thought something, or I just did something, and I ask myself — did I really do that as a Christian? Could someone check what I thought, check what I did, and still call me a man of God?

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Transcribe every audio/video file in a folder via the Modulate STT batch API.

Usage: transcribe.py <src_dir> [name_filter]

Reads the API key from ~/.config/modulate/api_key (create it with `chmod 600`
BEFORE running this — never hardcode the key in this script or commit it
anywhere). Writes "<name>.txt" into a Transcripts/ subfolder of src_dir.

Idempotent: skips any file that already has a non-empty .txt transcript, so
it's safe to re-run on a folder that new source files keep landing in over
time — only the new ones get transcribed.
"""
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import requests

# Modulate STT — multilingual batch model, synchronous, .mp3/.mp4/.wav/etc,
# 100MB file limit. See https://docs.modulate.ai/get-started/stt for the full
# reference (other endpoints: english-only "vfast" variant, streaming/WebSocket).
API_URL = "https://platform.modulate.ai/api/velma-2-stt-batch"
KEY_FILE = Path.home() / ".config/modulate/api_key"

AUDIO_EXTS = (
    ".mp3", ".mp4", ".wav", ".m4a", ".aac", ".flac",
    ".ogg", ".opus", ".webm", ".aiff", ".mov",
)


def get_api_key() -> str:
    if not KEY_FILE.exists():
        sys.exit(
            f"API key not found at {KEY_FILE}\n"
            f"Create it first: umask 077 && printf '<your key>' > {KEY_FILE} && chmod 600 {KEY_FILE}"
        )
    return KEY_FILE.read_text().strip()


def transcribe(path: Path, api_key: str) -> str:
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        resp = requests.post(
            API_URL,
            headers={"X-API-Key": api_key},
            data={"speaker_diarization": "true"},
            files={"upload_file": (path.name, f, "application/octet-stream")},
            timeout=600,
        )
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json().get("text", "")


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        sys.exit("usage: transcribe.py <src_dir> [name_filter]")
    src_dir = Path(sys.argv[1]).expanduser()
    only = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None
    out_dir = src_dir / "Transcripts"
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    api_key = get_api_key()
    files = sorted(p for p in src_dir.iterdir() if p.suffix.lower() in AUDIO_EXTS)
    if only:
        files = [f for f in files if only in f.name]
    if not files:
        print("No matching audio files found.")
        return

    for path in files:
        out_path = out_dir / (path.stem + ".txt")
        if out_path.exists() and out_path.stat().st_size > 0:
            print(f"skip (already done): {path.name}")
            continue
        print(f"transcribing: {path.name} ({path.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f}MB) ...", flush=True)
        try:
            text = transcribe(path, api_key)
        except requests.HTTPError as e:
            body = e.response.text[:300] if e.response is not None else ""
            print(f"  FAILED: {e} — {body}")
            continue
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  FAILED: {e!r}")
            continue
        out_path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"  saved: {out_path.name} ({len(text)} chars)")
        time.sleep(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Life Is Happening For You

## A Teaching by Ken Muritu

### ByPass Cell Church — a breakout session of Royal Priesthood (RP)

---

> *"Sow for yourselves righteousness; Reap in mercy; Break up your fallow ground, For it is time to seek the Lord, Till He comes and rains righteousness on you."*
> — Hosea 10:12 (NKJV)

> *"For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities nor powers, nor things present nor things to come, nor height nor depth, nor any other created thing, shall be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord."*
> — Romans 8:38-39 (NKJV)

---

## A Note Before We Begin

I want to be honest with you about where this teaching starts, because it's been a minute since I've shared the word in a setup like this — a cell, not a platform.

It's been a minute, like it's been long, before I share the word with such a setup. I normally speak, and in the speaking maybe I might throw some verses, and you get to the effect of the verses. But really, to stand — I remember the last time Benson told me, "Ken, you will be ministering to the cell." I remember when Benson was starting to lead us in prayer, and I saw the way he opened with the verses. He started with Isaiah 45:19 — *"I have not spoken in secret, in a dark place of the earth."* I thought, this is a man of God. And today the Spirit is really ministering to us.

I've been reminded of high school, when I was the follow-up coordinator — the class rep, sort of — for my class. I used to love that space. For some reason I don't know why, it used to grip me — you get to hear the word of God, and you get to see the hearts of the people who are listening to you. They are expectant. They are waiting for that time. Living with them, you know most of them are people of vurugu, people of fighting — you talk to them and to others, but when that time comes, you see a girl sitting there listening, and you can see the word you're sharing is doing something on their hearts.

So I've been reminded of that. And that's the heart I'm bringing into this room tonight.

---

# PART ONE: Life Is Happening For You, Not To You

## The Fallow Ground

Yesterday we were having a session with our father, and he told us to read the book of Romans. I was reading through Romans chapter 8, and I could see the love of God — the intention of God to man, the intention of God to His sons.

There is this thing I'm trying to structure in my thoughts, because so many things are coming to my head. But there comes a time — maybe because of where I've been brought up, maybe because of the systems we've gone through, maybe academics, maybe even the patterns — where we get to a place where we're not doubting the love of God, but at the same time we're not believing it completely.

You have faith, you're a believer, you come to church, you join watches, you join fasting. You give — you give with your time, you even give with money. You're doing the things that, if we're looking at it, you're supposed to be receiving for. But then you wonder why, at certain times, when you really want something to work, it's not working out.

**There comes a time when the systems of the earth, the systems of men, the patterns of our lives, contribute to the way we approach God — the way we believe in Him.** And sometimes you'll even question: "Is God really working? Does God really love me?" You're trying to look at a certain situation, a certain circumstance, and you cannot see God in it. You're trying to piece it together, and it's not making sense at all.

# God Gives Kingdom
## A Teaching by Pastor Charles Muchemi
### Royal Priesthood Embassy · Sunday-Eve Service — Kasarani Cell Church

---

> *"He who did not spare His own Son, but delivered Him up for us all, how shall He not with Him also freely give us all things?"*
> — Romans 8:32 (NKJV)

> *"Do not fear, little flock, for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom."*
> — Luke 12:32 (NKJV)

---

## A Note Before We Begin

We began a very important topic on how to receive from God, and our emphasis last time was: God is a giver. In my heart, one of the things God really communicated with a lot of weight is what we read in Psalm 100 — that we are the sheep of His pasture. We did not make ourselves. He made us. We are His responsibility.

We moved on to see how men, by the help of God, were able to walk in the promises of God — Sarah, for example. And all of that we saw, it is not according to man's effort. It was according to the grace of God. If you have to work for everything, if you have to work for anything, that means you have a slave mentality — you must not try to work for every result, everything that you are asking God to do in your life.

Tonight I want to continue with that, because if I'm talking about God gives kingdom, I cannot talk kingdom without talking righteousness. Most people do not know that righteousness is not about morals. It is about kingdom. It's about kingdom living.

---

# What Kind of Prayer Are You Praying?

## The Question From John Chapter Two

Before we get there, I want to ask you a question — so as we read this, expect a question after it. I want to see whether your mentality is that God gives, and whether your understanding of that will shape your mindset a certain way. Because there are certain expectations that are built in your heart, and that is how you posture yourself when God comes into your life.

> *"On the third day there was a wedding in Cana of Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there. Now both Jesus and His disciples were invited to the wedding. And when they ran out of wine, the mother of Jesus said to Him, 'They have no wine.' Jesus said to her, 'Woman, what does your concern have to do with Me? My hour has not yet come.' His mother said to the servants, 'Whatever He says to you, do it.' Now there were set there six waterpots of stone, according to the manner of purification of the Jews, containing twenty or thirty gallons apiece. Jesus said to them, 'Fill the waterpots with water.' And they filled them up to the brim. And He said to them, 'Draw some out now, and take it to the master of the feast.' And they took it. When the master of the feast had tasted the water that was made wine, and did not know where it came from (but the servants who had drawn the water knew), the master of the feast called the bridegroom. And he said to him, 'Every man at the beginning sets out the good wine, and when the guests have well drunk, then the inferior. You have kept the good wine until now!'"*
> — John 2:1–10 (NKJV)

If you were to pray, to make any prayer from that passage — verse one to verse ten — who would you be?

Think about it: someone just received a miracle. It's a shame for the wine — or the cake, whatever it is for you — not to be enough at your own wedding. But even if it was not yet His time, when Jesus stepped in, there was something the mother of Jesus knew about Him. Even when Jesus said it was not yet His time, she did not listen — she continued to tell them, "Whatever He tells you, do it." And the giving of God was evident.

## Every Prayer Point Given Was a Receiving Prayer

When I asked the room for prayer points from that passage, this is what came back:

- *"God helps me to obey, because it is after obedience that the miracle happens."*
- *"The grace to do exactly what Jesus tells me to do."*
- *"My ears to be open — that I may hear the instructions that will lead me to actually have what I want in my hands."*
- *"God to help me see where my provision is, because He has already done it."*
- *"God to give me an ear to hear and wisdom to obey the instruction."*
- *"God to make me a vessel for His miracles."*
- *"Grace to continually live in thankfulness."*
- *"My eyes to be open to identify the giving of God — that when I see something that is not available, I can identify that it is available with God."*
- *"Go and use what is already in my hands. Fill the waterpot with water."*
- *"Grace to finish — it's not just enough to begin, but to complete."*

All of those prayer points are nice, and none of them are wrong. But I noticed something: most of you concentrated so much on the side of the one receiving the miracle. Not many of you went to the other side — the side of the one who is actually performing the miracle. You are a miracle worker.

I remember one time I taught you that when you are reading the Bible and you see Jesus healing people, you are not the person receiving the healing — you are the person giving the healing. Do you remember? Because this is the mentality.

---

# You Are Not the Creation Waiting — You Are the Son Revealing

## "I Said, You Are Gods"

Psalm 82 says something with weight:

> *"I said, 'You are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High.'"*
> — Psalm 82:6 (NKJV)

If you are a child of the Most High, you are expected to be doing what your Father does. This is what Jesus showed us in the book of John — He said, "I do what I see My Father do." Jesus did not have the Bible. You have the Bible. What Jesus used to do is have fellowship with the Father, and what He saw the Father do is what He came and replicated.

> *"The heaven, even the heavens, are the LORD's; but the earth He has given to the children of men."*
> — Psalm 115:16 (NKJV)

Now see this — Jesus says:

> *"Then Jesus answered and said to them, 'Most assuredly, I say to you, the Son can do nothing of Himself, but what He sees the Father do; for whatever He does, the Son also does in like manner.'"*
> — John 5:19 (NKJV)

Before someone argues that there is a difference between God and us — that God is Father and we are only sons — here Jesus is telling us something different: the Son does also in like manner. You do exactly what your Father does.

## Son of Man, Son of God

There's a reason you're called children of men. Do you know the difference between the Son of God and the Son of Man? Jesus called Himself both — in fact Jesus called Himself Son of Man; it is people who called Him Son of God. The reason He called Himself Son of Man is because He came as man's representative. No man had the capacity to save mankind, yet it had to be one of them, because it was one of them — through one man — that sin entered the world. The wages of sin is death; there is a price, a cost to sin, and it had to be paid by one of them.

So Jesus was sent as man's representative. That's why He was born in the form of man, and that's why He called Himself Son of Man. And one of the reasons He was able to represent man — to be Son of Man — is because He was Son of God.

> *"For He made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us, that we might become the righteousness of God in Him."*
> — 2 Corinthians 5:21 (NKJV)

He didn't have any sin. So for you as well — when the Bible says you are a son of God, that you the children of men have been given the earth, then you also are called gods. Now do you see the connection? Now you begin to understand why Jesus would come and say, "I do what I see My Father do."

## The Creation Is Waiting — For Your Manifestation, Not God's

When you are reading the Bible, you will always find two parties in play: you'll find God, and you'll find creation — and God is always doing something for the creation. Most times we position ourselves as part of the creation, receiving what God is doing for the creation. And we forget:

> *"For the earnest expectation of the creation eagerly waits for the revealing of the sons of God."*
> — Romans 8:19 (NKJV)

Who are the sons of God? We are the sons of God. So there is no way we can be the sons of God and at the same time be the creation that is eagerly waiting. You are not seated somewhere because of a situation, waiting for someone to come and change it. You are very much aware: I am the one sent to change the situation. The reason I am in this situation is not so that I suffer from it — it's so that I can change it.

This is why you will stay with your friends and they will be complaining about the economy, and you won't join them in complaining — because you know you are the one who is supposed to fix it. Because they are the creation, and the creation is waiting for my manifestation, because I am a son of God. I want you to change your mindset completely.

---

# From Receiving to Giving

## "What I See My Father Do, I Do in Like Manner"

Going back to John chapter 2 — your first response to that passage was to first see what God was giving. So immediately your first prayer point began preparing you to receive. But if God gives, and John 5 says "what I see My Father do, I do in like manner" — then if God gives, what do you do? You give.

Last time when I was teaching you about how to receive, we said: God is a giver, so how do you receive? By giving. That's the point I'm trying to drive you to. Now someone is already offended, thinking I'm talking about giving money — that's another slave mindset. It will even have nothing to do with money — it may, if God tells you to — but it's not even about God giving to you. It's about you impacting people. That's the giving I'm talking about.

That the creation eagerly awaits my manifestation — so how I receive is by posturing myself as one who wants to respond to the need of the creation. That's the giving.

## Destiny Helper, Not Destiny-Helped

In the same passage — why is it that the mother of Jesus told the servants specifically, "Whatever He tells you, do it"? When she spotted the shame that was upon these people because the wedding had run out of wine, she identified someone who could become the solution to that shame.

When people take that passage and pray for "destiny helpers," they're praying that Jesus becomes a destiny helper *to them* — someone who carries their shame away. But why would you not take the same passage and pray, "God, make me a destiny helper to those who are in shame"?

When you are selfish, you always receive, receive, receive. But if you made that one prayer — "God, make me a destiny helper" — and God begins to open your eyes, you will not even move to the next prayer point in your usual list. When you tell God you want to become a destiny helper, you immediately begin to find images coming to your mind, and you won't even know how long you've been praying. You'll have an endless list of the people you want to impact.

## The Boldness of a Son, Not the Timidity of a Beggar

Are you aware that the inner man — the real you — knows who you really are? When you are begging for rent, you are timid. When you are declaring the works you are going to do, you are bold — because the real you is now awake, becoming alive in God. Have you ever seen a slave come in and demand something? A slave kneels and begs, "I am kindly asking." They can do anything, because they are begging.

If you don't adopt this mentality, you will not be bold enough to do the things of God. Anytime you feel inferiority setting in while you pray, that prayer is not the prayer you should be praying. The reason you tell God to open your eyes is not so that you see where your money is — it's so that you can see where you will spend your money. That's why, after all these years of praying "open my eyes," you have never seen anything. The problem has always been the mindset you carry.

I am not looking to receive what I see my Father doing. Show me in Scripture any place someone was watching God do something, and God was the inferior one asking for it. Never happens. God is always repairing the broken ruins. God is always raising the dead. If that is what you saw your Father do, why are you looking to do something different?

You don't see with your eyes — you see with your mind. That's why you've always told God "open my eyes" while your mindset says "I want to receive money, I want to receive a car." That's why you never see.

> *"…the eyes of your understanding being enlightened; that you may know what is the hope of His calling, what are the riches of the glory of His inheritance in the saints, and what is the exceeding greatness of His power toward us who believe, according to the working of His mighty power which He worked in Christ when He raised Him from the dead and seated Him at His right hand in the heavenly places…"*
> — Ephesians 1:18–20 (NKJV)

What is the hope of *His* calling — God's calling. What are the riches of *His* inheritance — you are calling, you are inheriting; it is not you who is being called upon. These are the things you are supposed to be seeing. Your eyes are not supposed to be open to see anything else that is not God — because when you see it in God, you see it in you.

---

# God Gives Kingdom

This is why some people stay long in prayer and you don't — it's because of what you do in prayer. Prayer is all about beholding Him, beholding the beauty, beholding the glory. You cannot finish seeing the things God wants to manifest on this earth.

In John chapter 2, the major prayer you should make is that you see what Jesus did and desire to be Jesus. Whatever you have been expecting Jesus to give you — the reason you don't have it is because you are seeing yourself as the one in need, not as the one who carries it. Whatever you see yourself as, that's what you become. You always see yourself as the one who is in need of a miracle — that is why you are always in need of one. The day you see yourself as a miracle worker, you cannot work out a miracle you don't have. If I'm bringing a miracle into your life, where did I get it? Not having money physically does not stop me from praying that prayer, because the minute I make that prayer, it moves money to come — so that I can fulfill what I have prayed.

Now that's when you'll understand why God gives you Kingdom. This year you must understand Kingdom. Do you remember I told you I had names I wanted to give this year — one of them fruitfulness, and another, our year of the new order? You cannot go through this year without understanding the kingdom. This is what will liberate you. The minute you understand the kingdom, it delivers you out of very many prayer problems.

> *"Do not fear, little flock, for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom."*
> — Luke 12:32 (NKJV)

It is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom. So what He gives is Kingdom. When He tells you that you're going to receive Kingdom from the Father, the first thing He tells you is: do not fear. When you know it pleases God to give you the kingdom — will you fear that He might not? No. It pleases Him to give. And if you're not fearing, what do you have? Faith.

---

## Closing Prayer

*Father Lord, we thank You for Your goodness over our lives. Thank You for allowing us to see that You have called us as solutions to the creation. Thank You for allowing us to see that we are not beggars in this world. We are not slaves to the world. We are the liberators, the kingdom ambassadors on earth. We are the light that shines in darkness. We are the glory, the honor that eliminates shame in the face of the Father. Lord, I ask You — position us to seek Him. Let our mindsets change from this day, that even our prayers shall reflect who we are. Our talk shall reflect who we are. Our behavior, our desires, our language — everything about us shall reflect who we are, in Jesus' name. Amen.*

# God Gives Kingdom
## A Teaching by Pastor Charles Muchemi
### Royal Priesthood Embassy · Sunday-Eve Service — Kasarani Cell Church

---

> *"He who did not spare His own Son, but delivered Him up for us all, how shall He not with Him also freely give us all things?"*
> — Romans 8:32 (NKJV)

> *"Do not fear, little flock, for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom."*
> — Luke 12:32 (NKJV)

---

## A Note Before We Begin

We began a very important topic on how to receive from God, and our emphasis last time was: God is a giver. In my heart, one of the things God really communicated with a lot of weight is what we read in Psalm 100 — that we are the sheep of His pasture. We did not make ourselves. He made us. We are His responsibility.

We moved on to see how men, by the help of God, were able to walk in the promises of God — Sarah, for example. And all of that we saw, it is not according to man's effort. It was according to the grace of God. If you have to work for everything, if you have to work for anything, that means you have a slave mentality — you must not try to work for every result, everything that you are asking God to do in your life.

Tonight I want to continue with that, because if I'm talking about God gives kingdom, I cannot talk kingdom without talking righteousness. Most people do not know that righteousness is not about morals. It is about kingdom. It's about kingdom living.

---

# What Kind of Prayer Are You Praying?

## The Question From John Chapter Two

Before we get there, I want to ask you a question — so as we read this, expect a question after it. I want to see whether your mentality is that God gives, and whether your understanding of that will shape your mindset a certain way. Because there are certain expectations that are built in your heart, and that is how you posture yourself when God comes into your life.

> *"On the third day there was a wedding in Cana of Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there. Now both Jesus and His disciples were invited to the wedding. And when they ran out of wine, the mother of Jesus said to Him, 'They have no wine.' Jesus said to her, 'Woman, what does your concern have to do with Me? My hour has not yet come.' His mother said to the servants, 'Whatever He says to you, do it.' Now there were set there six waterpots of stone, according to the manner of purification of the Jews, containing twenty or thirty gallons apiece. Jesus said to them, 'Fill the waterpots with water.' And they filled them up to the brim. And He said to them, 'Draw some out now, and take it to the master of the feast.' And they took it. When the master of the feast had tasted the water that was made wine, and did not know where it came from (but the servants who had drawn the water knew), the master of the feast called the bridegroom. And he said to him, 'Every man at the beginning sets out the good wine, and when the guests have well drunk, then the inferior. You have kept the good wine until now!'"*
> — John 2:1–10 (NKJV)

If you were to pray, to make any prayer from that passage — verse one to verse ten — who would you be?

Think about it: someone just received a miracle. It's a shame for the wine — or the cake, whatever it is for you — not to be enough at your own wedding. But even if it was not yet His time, when Jesus stepped in, there was something the mother of Jesus knew about Him. Even when Jesus said it was not yet His time, she did not listen — she continued to tell them, "Whatever He tells you, do it." And the giving of God was evident.

## Every Prayer Point Given Was a Receiving Prayer

When I asked the room for prayer points from that passage, this is what came back:

- *"God helps me to obey, because it is after obedience that the miracle happens."*
- *"The grace to do exactly what Jesus tells me to do."*
- *"My ears to be open — that I may hear the instructions that will lead me to actually have what I want in my hands."*
- *"God to help me see where my provision is, because He has already done it."*
- *"God to give me an ear to hear and wisdom to obey the instruction."*
- *"God to make me a vessel for His miracles."*
- *"Grace to continually live in thankfulness."*
- *"My eyes to be open to identify the giving of God — that when I see something that is not available, I can identify that it is available with God."*
- *"Go and use what is already in my hands. Fill the waterpot with water."*
- *"Grace to finish — it's not just enough to begin, but to complete."*

All of those prayer points are nice, and none of them are wrong. But I noticed something: most of you concentrated so much on the side of the one receiving the miracle. Not many of you went to the other side — the side of the one who is actually performing the miracle. You are a miracle worker.

I remember one time I taught you that when you are reading the Bible and you see Jesus healing people, you are not the person receiving the healing — you are the person giving the healing. Do you remember? Because this is the mentality.

---

# You Are Not the Creation Waiting — You Are the Son Revealing

## "I Said, You Are Gods"

Psalm 82 says something with weight:

> *"I said, 'You are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High.'"*
> — Psalm 82:6 (NKJV)

If you are a child of the Most High, you are expected to be doing what your Father does. This is what Jesus showed us in the book of John — He said, "I do what I see My Father do." Jesus did not have the Bible. You have the Bible. What Jesus used to do is have fellowship with the Father, and what He saw the Father do is what He came and replicated.

> *"The heaven, even the heavens, are the LORD's; but the earth He has given to the children of men."*
> — Psalm 115:16 (NKJV)

Now see this — Jesus says:

> *"Then Jesus answered and said to them, 'Most assuredly, I say to you, the Son can do nothing of Himself, but what He sees the Father do; for whatever He does, the Son also does in like manner.'"*
> — John 5:19 (NKJV)

Before someone argues that there is a difference between God and us — that God is Father and we are only sons — here Jesus is telling us something different: the Son does also in like manner. You do exactly what your Father does.

## Son of Man, Son of God

There's a reason you're called children of men. Do you know the difference between the Son of God and the Son of Man? Jesus called Himself both — in fact Jesus called Himself Son of Man; it is people who called Him Son of God. The reason He called Himself Son of Man is because He came as man's representative. No man had the capacity to save mankind, yet it had to be one of them, because it was one of them — through one man — that sin entered the world. The wages of sin is death; there is a price, a cost to sin, and it had to be paid by one of them.

So Jesus was sent as man's representative. That's why He was born in the form of man, and that's why He called Himself Son of Man. And one of the reasons He was able to represent man — to be Son of Man — is because He was Son of God.

> *"For He made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us, that we might become the righteousness of God in Him."*
> — 2 Corinthians 5:21 (NKJV)

He didn't have any sin. So for you as well — when the Bible says you are a son of God, that you the children of men have been given the earth, then you also are called gods. Now do you see the connection? Now you begin to understand why Jesus would come and say, "I do what I see My Father do."

## The Creation Is Waiting — For Your Manifestation, Not God's

When you are reading the Bible, you will always find two parties in play: you'll find God, and you'll find creation — and God is always doing something for the creation. Most times we position ourselves as part of the creation, receiving what God is doing for the creation. And we forget:

> *"For the earnest expectation of the creation eagerly waits for the revealing of the sons of God."*
> — Romans 8:19 (NKJV)

Who are the sons of God? We are the sons of God. So there is no way we can be the sons of God and at the same time be the creation that is eagerly waiting. You are not seated somewhere because of a situation, waiting for someone to come and change it. You are very much aware: I am the one sent to change the situation. The reason I am in this situation is not so that I suffer from it — it's so that I can change it.

This is why you will stay with your friends and they will be complaining about the economy, and you won't join them in complaining — because you know you are the one who is supposed to fix it. Because they are the creation, and the creation is waiting for my manifestation, because I am a son of God. I want you to change your mindset completely.

---

# From Receiving to Giving

## "What I See My Father Do, I Do in Like Manner"

Going back to John chapter 2 — your first response to that passage was to first see what God was giving. So immediately your first prayer point began preparing you to receive. But if God gives, and John 5 says "what I see My Father do, I do in like manner" — then if God gives, what do you do? You give.

Last time when I was teaching you about how to receive, we said: God is a giver, so how do you receive? By giving. That's the point I'm trying to drive you to. Now someone is already offended, thinking I'm talking about giving money — that's another slave mindset. It will even have nothing to do with money — it may, if God tells you to — but it's not even about God giving to you. It's about you impacting people. That's the giving I'm talking about.

That the creation eagerly awaits my manifestation — so how I receive is by posturing myself as one who wants to respond to the need of the creation. That's the giving.

## Destiny Helper, Not Destiny-Helped

In the same passage — why is it that the mother of Jesus told the servants specifically, "Whatever He tells you, do it"? When she spotted the shame that was upon these people because the wedding had run out of wine, she identified someone who could become the solution to that shame.

When people take that passage and pray for "destiny helpers," they're praying that Jesus becomes a destiny helper *to them* — someone who carries their shame away. But why would you not take the same passage and pray, "God, make me a destiny helper to those who are in shame"?

When you are selfish, you always receive, receive, receive. But if you made that one prayer — "God, make me a destiny helper" — and God begins to open your eyes, you will not even move to the next prayer point in your usual list. When you tell God you want to become a destiny helper, you immediately begin to find images coming to your mind, and you won't even know how long you've been praying. You'll have an endless list of the people you want to impact.

## The Boldness of a Son, Not the Timidity of a Beggar

Are you aware that the inner man — the real you — knows who you really are? When you are begging for rent, you are timid. When you are declaring the works you are going to do, you are bold — because the real you is now awake, becoming alive in God. Have you ever seen a slave come in and demand something? A slave kneels and begs, "I am kindly asking." They can do anything, because they are begging.

If you don't adopt this mentality, you will not be bold enough to do the things of God. Anytime you feel inferiority setting in while you pray, that prayer is not the prayer you should be praying. The reason you tell God to open your eyes is not so that you see where your money is — it's so that you can see where you will spend your money. That's why, after all these years of praying "open my eyes," you have never seen anything. The problem has always been the mindset you carry.

I am not looking to receive what I see my Father doing. Show me in Scripture any place someone was watching God do something, and God was the inferior one asking for it. Never happens. God is always repairing the broken ruins. God is always raising the dead. If that is what you saw your Father do, why are you looking to do something different?

You don't see with your eyes — you see with your mind. That's why you've always told God "open my eyes" while your mindset says "I want to receive money, I want to receive a car." That's why you never see.

> *"…the eyes of your understanding being enlightened; that you may know what is the hope of His calling, what are the riches of the glory of His inheritance in the saints, and what is the exceeding greatness of His power toward us who believe, according to the working of His mighty power which He worked in Christ when He raised Him from the dead and seated Him at His right hand in the heavenly places…"*
> — Ephesians 1:18–20 (NKJV)

What is the hope of *His* calling — God's calling. What are the riches of *His* inheritance — you are calling, you are inheriting; it is not you who is being called upon. These are the things you are supposed to be seeing. Your eyes are not supposed to be open to see anything else that is not God — because when you see it in God, you see it in you.

---

# God Gives Kingdom

This is why some people stay long in prayer and you don't — it's because of what you do in prayer. Prayer is all about beholding Him, beholding the beauty, beholding the glory. You cannot finish seeing the things God wants to manifest on this earth.

In John chapter 2, the major prayer you should make is that you see what Jesus did and desire to be Jesus. Whatever you have been expecting Jesus to give you — the reason you don't have it is because you are seeing yourself as the one in need, not as the one who carries it. Whatever you see yourself as, that's what you become. You always see yourself as the one who is in need of a miracle — that is why you are always in need of one. The day you see yourself as a miracle worker, you cannot work out a miracle you don't have. If I'm bringing a miracle into your life, where did I get it? Not having money physically does not stop me from praying that prayer, because the minute I make that prayer, it moves money to come — so that I can fulfill what I have prayed.

Now that's when you'll understand why God gives you Kingdom. This year you must understand Kingdom. Do you remember I told you I had names I wanted to give this year — one of them fruitfulness, and another, our year of the new order? You cannot go through this year without understanding the kingdom. This is what will liberate you. The minute you understand the kingdom, it delivers you out of very many prayer problems.

> *"Do not fear, little flock, for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom."*
> — Luke 12:32 (NKJV)

It is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom. So what He gives is Kingdom. When He tells you that you're going to receive Kingdom from the Father, the first thing He tells you is: do not fear. When you know it pleases God to give you the kingdom — will you fear that He might not? No. It pleases Him to give. And if you're not fearing, what do you have? Faith.

---

## Closing Prayer

*Father Lord, we thank You for Your goodness over our lives. Thank You for allowing us to see that You have called us as solutions to the creation. Thank You for allowing us to see that we are not beggars in this world. We are not slaves to the world. We are the liberators, the kingdom ambassadors on earth. We are the light that shines in darkness. We are the glory, the honor that eliminates shame in the face of the Father. Lord, I ask You — position us to seek Him. Let our mindsets change from this day, that even our prayers shall reflect who we are. Our talk shall reflect who we are. Our behavior, our desires, our language — everything about us shall reflect who we are, in Jesus' name. Amen.*

## Before the Teaching: Cell Life, Prophecy, and a Send-Off

The level of manifestation of the Holy Spirit is increasing in people's lives. While praying for this meeting, God gave two words for this cell group.

The first: *"Then he named the child Ichabod, saying, 'The glory has departed from Israel!' because the ark of God had been captured, and because of her father-in-law and her husband."* — 1 Samuel 4:21 (NKJV). If you are a member of Kasarani's group, your name shall never be Ichabod. The glory will never depart from your life — that is for you to decide, but when God has said it, there is a grace to ensure this does not happen. When people come here, they shall experience the glory of the Lord — in their family, in their finances. This also puts you in a tricky place, because it means you cannot do anything without God: when the ark was captured, it means wherever the presence of God lives, He captures it. So in anything you do — business, anything — the presence of God must be there.

The second: *"Peter was therefore kept in prison, but constant prayer was offered to God for him by the church."* — Acts 12:5 (NKJV). Each cell group represents something in the ministry, and the grace that has been supplied for this cell group is prayer. No matter what — the story is not over, because there is a *but*. But prayer. It doesn't matter the economy, doesn't matter the state of your family — but prayer. A praying generation will come from this place.

### A Send-Off for Anita

Before getting into the word — Anita is flying to the UK next week for her master's, for a good stretch of time.

*"Father, I pray for Anita in the mighty name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth. We thank God for the doors that have opened for you. I declare that this going is blessed, and that the land in the UK shall receive you. You will not suffer rejection from that land."*

There's a scripture for this — Zechariah 1:17: *"...again proclaim, saying, 'Thus says the LORD of hosts: "My cities shall again spread out through prosperity..."'"* (NKJV). This door that has opened for you — one thing that comes with it is prosperity, but it is for the spread of the cities of God.

*"I declare that prosperity, when people mention prosperity, they shall see you. When someone is having an idea of what it means to prosper in their career, in everything about their life, they shall see you. Be at the top, even in that country."*

And Acts 28:10 — Paul on the island of Malta: *"They also honored us in many ways; and when we departed, they provided such things as were necessary."* (NKJV) — or, as the Message version puts it, *"We spent a wonderful three months on Malta. They treated us royally. Took care of all our needs and outfitted us for the rest of the journey."* So they shall treat you royally. Whatever you need for your stay in that place, the land of UK and its people shall provide it for you. I remove all problems with the authorities, all health problems, in the mighty name of Jesus. I declare smooth traveling — your plane shall go and land safely.

A team was organized from the cell to escort her to the airport, and the room recalled praying together on the field at school in years past — a place of prayer that, walking past it even now, is still remembered.

---

We began a very important topic on how to receive from God,

# Package-manager download caches are pure re-dow
# preemptively: an unconditional every-5-min purge means every install
# re-fetches everything (slower, more bandwidth,
# partial downloads themselves). Evict them only when usage is within
# EVICT_MARGIN_PCT of the threshold — i.e. when t
# needed soon — and never while a package manager is mid-install, since
# purging its cache under it risks corrupting an
EVICT_MARGIN_PCT=10

pkg_manager_busy() {
  local p
  for p in npm pnpm yarn pip pip3 uv cargo go; do
    pgrep -x "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
  done
  return 1
}

step_gated() {
  local desc="$1"; shift
  if pkg_manager_busy; then
    log "skip: $desc (package manager running)"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ "$(usage_pct)" -lt $(( THRESHOLD - EVICT_MARGIN_PCT )) ]; then
    log "skip: $desc (usage below ${THRESHOLD}-${e)"
    return 0
  fi
  step "$desc" "$@"
}

- `guarded-install` — pre-flight wrapper (`guarded-install --need-mb N <cmd>`) that refuses big installs (pip/torch, npm) if disk headroom doesn't fit, runs a cleanup pass before/after. Targets the session's actual historical failure mode (overlay filling mid-extract).
- `disk-cleanup.sh` upgrades: package-manager caches (npm/pip/yarn/go/cargo/uv/electron) now gated — only evicted within 10% of the disk threshold, and skipped while a package manager process is running (was: unconditional every-5-min purge, causing re-download churn and install-corruption risk). Added a predictive early `/tmp` sweep before the full emergency path, plus a per-run offender tally compacted into a once-per-boot "top eaters" notification (`disk-cleanup.sh --digest` to view anytime).

**Why:** [[reference-skiiforge]] is the durable-outputs repo for this ephemeral live-boot machine ([[user-environment]]); this hardening skill is what survives a reboot/session-crash and gets reinstalled via `install.sh`. The work was done in a *separate* Claude Code session running on OpenRouter's `stealth/ox-alpha` model (not Sonnet 5, not this session) — the user pasted a transcript of that session here "for context, just keep it." Verified real via `gh api` against the live repo before saving this (commit exists, all 3 new bin/ files present) — not taken on the transcript's word alone.

**How to apply:** Future live-session hardening requests in this repo should build on these 8 guards, not rebuild them. If asked to check "are the guards running," `guards-doctor.sh` already answers that. If troubleshooting a `disk-cleanup.sh` change, note the gating/tally logic added here before assuming the old unconditional-purge behavior still applies. Also flagged in that ox-alpha session: Modulate and OpenRouter API keys are sitting in plaintext across this machine's Claude session transcript logs — low risk since the box is ephemeral, but worth revoking those keys once actual testing is done, consistent with what was already told to the user in this session.
